fields.name: authentication
fields.description: Authentication attributes.

fields.name: allow-flood-traffic
fields.description:
Enable transmission of flood traffic (broadcast, multicast and
unknown unicast) out authentication enabled interfaces with no
authenticated client.

fields.name: auth-mode
fields.description:
The mode determining how each client on the interface can gain access
to the network.

fields.name: bpdu-auth
fields.description: BPDUs that can trigger authentication.

fields.name: cdp
fields.description: Enable CDP packets to trigger authentication.

fields.name: lldp
fields.description: Enable LLDP packets to trigger authentication.

fields.name: mac-type
fields.description:
MAC address to use when authentication is triggered by an
LLDP frame. This is applicable only when LLDP packets are
allowed to trigger authentication.

fields.name: bpdu-bypass
fields.description:
BPDUs to be serviced by the device before authentication is
successful on the interface.

fields.name: cdp
fields.description:
Enable CDP packets to be serviced by the device before
authentication is successful on the interface.

fields.name: lldp
fields.description:
Enable LLDP packets to be serviced by the device before
authentication is successful on the interface.

fields.name: bpdu-proxy-logoff
fields.description:
Proxy logoff the client based on the interface status in BPDU packets.
Device will clear authentication session of the client if it receives
an interface down status in the BPDU packet.
When not configured, no action is taken.

fields.name: cdp
fields.description: Enable CDP based proxy-logoff.

fields.name: client-limit
fields.description: Maximum number of clients that can be authenticated on the interface.

fields.name: device-profile-secure
fields.description: Enable device-profile with security.

fields.name: auth-precedence
fields.description:
Precedence order for port-access authentication. Auth-precedence must
contain either 0 or 2 elements. If empty, the default precedence
order of dot1x followed by mac-auth will be used.

fields.name: auth-priority
fields.description:
Priority order for port-access authentication. Auth-priority must
contain either 0 or 2 elements. If not set, priority will follow
the 'auth-precedence' order.

fields.name: client-auto-logoff-enable
fields.description:
The list of reasons when a client can be automatically logged off by
the device.

fields.name: client-move
fields.description: The client move configuration.

fields.name: cloud-auth
fields.description: Enable cloud authentication.

fields.name: concurrent-onboarding
fields.description:
Enable authentication methods to start concurrently for faster
onboarding. If not set, clients are onboarded based on the order
specified by 'onboarding-precedence'.

fields.name: controlled-direction
fields.description:
Configure how traffic is controlled on non-authenticated ports: in both directions (ingress and egress) or ingress only.
Default is BOTH.

fields.name: dot1xauth-server-group
fields.description: 802.1X authentication server group.

fields.name: macauth-server-group
fields.description: MAC authentication server group

fields.name: mda-data-clients-limit
fields.description:
Maximum number of 'data' clients that can be authenticated on the
interface when multi-domain is enabled. If the number of 'data' clients
on the interface exceeds this client limit, it will be considered as a
violation and the configured threshold-violation action is taken.

fields.name: onboarding-precedence
fields.description:
Precedence order when onboarding a client. Onboarding-precedence must
contain either 0 or 2 elements. If empty, the default precedence order
of AAA followed by device-profile will be used.

fields.name: auth-role
fields.description:
The role to be applied for clients that have been authenticated
but not received any specific role or attribute from the authentication
server.
When not set, no role is applied for clients that successfully
authenticated without a role assigned from the RADIUS server.

fields.name: auto-vlan-enable
fields.description:
Enable automatic creation of a VLAN for authenticated clients if the
VLAN is not already available on the device.

fields.name: cached-critical-role-enable
fields.description:
Enables caching authenticated clients and their associated
role information on the interface. Clients are assigned to their
previously authenticated role.

fields.name: critical-auth-role
fields.description:
The role to be applied for clients, that failed authentication
due to unreachable authentication servers.
When not set, no role is applied for clients that could not
complete authentication due to RADIUS server being unreachable.

fields.name: critical-data-vlan
fields.description: Configure critical-auth VLAN as data VLAN.

fields.name: critical-voice-role
fields.description:
The role to be applied to 'voice' client that have failed
re-authentication due to servers being unreachable.
When not set, no role will be applied for voice clients when they
fail re-authentication due to server being unreachable.

fields.name: critical-voice-vlan
fields.description: Configure critical-auth VLAN as voice VLAN.

fields.name: default-vlan-type
fields.description: Type of default vlan.

fields.name: fallback-role
fields.description:
The role that will be applied to clients that have not been
assigned a role via any of the onboarding methods.
When not set, no role is applied for the client.

fields.name: open-data-vlan
fields.description: Configure open-auth VLAN as data VLAN.

fields.name: open-voice-vlan
fields.description: Configure open-auth VLAN as voice VLAN.

fields.name: pre-auth-role
fields.description:
The role to be applied for clients that are yet to be authenticated.
When not set, no role is applied for clients while the
authentication is in progress for the client.

fields.name: radius-override-enable
fields.description:
Enable RADIUS override support. When enabled, RADIUS attributes
received from the server will override corresponding attributes
configured in the role assigned to the client.

fields.name: reject-role
fields.description:
The role to be applied for clients that failed authentication.
When not set, for AOS-CX devices, no role is applied for clients that fail authentication.
A default denyall role is applied on AOS-S devices.

fields.name: ubt-fallback-role
fields.description:
For any client,for which the corresponding UBT zone reachability
is failed, ubt-fallback role is applied. The client on ubt-fallback
role is automatically reverted to the previous role whenever UBT zone
status is back to reachable state.

fields.name: security-violation
fields.description: Security violation configuration.

fields.name: action
fields.description:
Action to take on a security violation (notify or shutdown).
This is only supported on physical ports.

fields.name: recovery-timer
fields.description:
Time in seconds after which the interface is re-enabled if it was
shutdown in response to a violation event.
This is only applicable if shutdown recovery is enabled.

fields.name: shutdown-recovery-enable
fields.description:
Enable auto-recovery of the interface. This is only applicable when
the violation action is set to shutdown.
The interface is re-enabled after the recovery timer has expired.

fields.name: security-violation.action

fields.name: security-violation.shutdown-recovery-enable
fields.description: Enable auto-recovery of the interface. This is only applicable when the violation action is set to shutdown. The interface is re-enabled after the recovery timer has expired.

fields.name: auth-role
fields.description:
The role to be applied for clients that have been authenticated
but not received any specific role or attribute from the authentication
server.
When not set, no role is applied for clients that successfully
authenticated without a role assigned from the RADIUS server.

fields.name: auto-vlan-enable
fields.description:
Enable automatic creation of a VLAN for authenticated clients if the
VLAN is not already available on the device.

fields.name: cached-critical-role-enable
fields.description:
Enables caching authenticated clients and their associated
role information on the interface. Clients are assigned to their
previously authenticated role.

fields.name: critical-auth-role
fields.description:
The role to be applied for clients, that failed authentication
due to unreachable authentication servers.
When not set, no role is applied for clients that could not
complete authentication due to RADIUS server being unreachable.

fields.name: critical-data-vlan
fields.description: Configure critical-auth VLAN as data VLAN.

fields.name: critical-voice-role
fields.description:
The role to be applied to 'voice' client that have failed
re-authentication due to servers being unreachable.
When not set, no role will be applied for voice clients when they
fail re-authentication due to server being unreachable.

fields.name: critical-voice-vlan
fields.description: Configure critical-auth VLAN as voice VLAN.

fields.name: default-vlan-type
fields.description: Type of default vlan.

fields.name: fallback-role
fields.description:
The role that will be applied to clients that have not been
assigned a role via any of the onboarding methods.
When not set, no role is applied for the client.

fields.name: open-data-vlan
fields.description: Configure open-auth VLAN as data VLAN.

fields.name: open-voice-vlan
fields.description: Configure open-auth VLAN as voice VLAN.

fields.name: pre-auth-role
fields.description:
The role to be applied for clients that are yet to be authenticated.
When not set, no role is applied for clients while the
authentication is in progress for the client.

fields.name: radius-override-enable
fields.description:
Enable RADIUS override support. When enabled, RADIUS attributes
received from the server will override corresponding attributes
configured in the role assigned to the client.

fields.name: reject-role
fields.description:
The role to be applied for clients that failed authentication.
When not set, for AOS-CX devices, no role is applied for clients that fail authentication.
A default denyall role is applied on AOS-S devices.

fields.name: ubt-fallback-role
fields.description:
For any client,for which the corresponding UBT zone reachability
is failed, ubt-fallback role is applied. The client on ubt-fallback
role is automatically reverted to the previous role whenever UBT zone
status is back to reachable state.

the violation action is set to shutdown.

fields.name: called-station-id
fields.description: Configure this parameter to be sent with the RADIUS attribute Called Station ID for authentication and accounting requests. For AP, this API is applicable for WLAN profile and AP port profile. For GW, this API is applicable for the authentication server profile. This feature is applicable for AP and GW.

fields.name: include-ssid
fields.description: Include SSID in called-station-id attribute.

fields.name: include-ssid-delimiter
fields.description: The delimiter between mac address and SSID. For example, the delimiter is dash. The called-station-id like aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff-wlanssid.

fields.name: mac-address-delimiter
fields.description: By default, called-station-id is AP MAC Address string and no delimiter, when configure mac-address-delimiter, AP MAC Address will be added delimiter in authentication packet.

fields.name: type
fields.description:
Configure the called-station-id types.
For AP, The type includes AP group, AP MAC address, AP name, AP IP or user vlan. The default value is AP MAC address.

fields.name: upper-case
fields.description: By default, called-station-id is AP MAC Address string, when enabled upper-case, AP MAC Address will be changed to upper case in authentication packet.

fields.name: called-station-id.include-ssid
fields.description: Include SSID in called-station-id attribute.

fields.name: called-station-id.include-ssid-delimiter
fields.description: The delimiter between mac address and SSID. For example, the delimiter is dash. The called-station-id like aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff-wlanssid.

fields.name: called-station-id.mac-address-delimiter
fields.description: By default, called-station-id is AP MAC Address string and no delimiter, when configure mac-address-delimiter, AP MAC Address will be added delimiter in authentication packet.

fields.name: called-station-id.type
fields.description: Configure the called-station-id types. For AP, The type includes AP group, AP MAC address, AP name, AP IP or user vlan. The default value is AP MAC address.

fields.name: called-station-id.upper-case
fields.description: By default, called-station-id is AP MAC Address string, when enabled upper-case, AP MAC Address will be changed to upper case in authentication packet.

fields.name: acct-port
fields.description: Port number for accounting requests. This field can be configured only when type is RADIUS with radius-server-mode configured as AUTH_ONLY or AUTH_AND_COA.

fields.name: admin-dn
fields.description: DN for the admin user who has read or search privileges across all of the entries in the LDAP database (the user does not need write privileges but should be able to search the database and read attributes of other users in the database). This field can be configured only when type is LDAP.

fields.name: admin-dn-alias
fields.description: Alias for Admin DN.

fields.name: admin-password
fields.description: Password for the admin user. this field can be configured only when type is LDAP.

fields.name: admin-password-alias
fields.description: Alias for Admin password.

fields.name: allow-cleartext
fields.description: Allow unencrypted communication with LDAP server. this field can be configured only when type is LDAP.

fields.name: auth-modifier
fields.description: Attributes modifier for authentication-request. this field can be configured only when type is RADIUS with radius-server-mode configured as AUTH_ONLY or AUTH_AND_COA.

fields.name: auth-port
fields.description: Port number for authentication requests.For CX, default auth-port for RADIUS Servers is 1812 and TACACS Servers is 49. For CX and PVOS, this parameter cannot be modified.

fields.name: auth-server-address
fields.description: IP address or FQDN of the Auth server. For CX and PVOS, auth-server-address is a mandatory parameter and can not be modified.

fields.name: auth-throttle
fields.description: AP measures request-response times for each packet exchange. As the time taken approaches the timeout, AP throttles new transactions.

fields.name: authentication-type
fields.description: Specifies authentication protocol which is used for communication with Auth servers. If not specified, the global timeout value will be picked. This field can be configured only when type is TACACS OR RADIUS with radius-server-mode configured as AUTH_ONLY or AUTH_AND_COA.

fields.name: base-dn
fields.description: DN name of the node which contains the entire user database to use. this field can be configured only when type is LDAP.

fields.name: base-dn-alias
fields.description: Alias for Base DN.

fields.name: chase-referrals
fields.description: LDAP Chase Referrals. this field can be configured only when type is LDAP.

fields.name: clearpass
fields.description: Host RADIUS server on ClearPass.

fields.name: cppm-password-config
fields.description: Auth server Clearpass password configuration used for authentication. This field can be configured only when type is RADIUS with radius-server-mode configured as AUTH_ONLY or AUTH_AND_COA.

fields.name: ciphertext-value
fields.description:
Ciphertext password of the ClearPass server to authenticate. This field can be configured only when password-type is CIPHER_TEXT.
For CX, supported length is 1-64.

fields.name: password-type

fields.name: preferred-conn-type
fields.description: Preferred Connection Type. this field can be configured only when type is LDAP.

fields.name: radius-server-mode
fields.description: Specifies the mode in which the RADIUS server is used. - AUTH_ONLY: Server is used only for authentication. - COA_ONLY: Server is used only for Change of Authorization (CoA). - AUTH_AND_COA: Server is used for both authentication and CoA.

fields.name: radius-server-mode-alias
fields.description: Alias for Radius server mode.

fields.name: radsec-client-cert
fields.description: RADIUS Security Client Certificate Name. This field can be configured only when type is RADIUS with radius-server-mode configured as AUTH_ONLY or AUTH_AND_COA

fields.name: radsec-est-cert-profile
fields.description: RADIUS Security Server Certificate Name. This field can be configured only when type is RADIUS with radius-server-mode configured as AUTH_ONLY or AUTH_AND_COA.

fields.name: radsec-keepalive
fields.description: If there is no radius activity for more than 15 minutes, with status-server keepalive, CPPM doesn't terminate connection every 15 minutes, with tcp-keepalive , CPPM terminates the RADSEC connection after 15 minutes

fields.name: radsec-port
fields.description: Designates a RadSec port for RADIUS data transport This field can be configured only when type is RADIUS with radius-server-mode configured as AUTH_ONLY or AUTH_AND_COA and enable-radsec is set to true. For CX and PVOS, this parameter cannot be modified.

fields.name: radsec-trusted-cacert-name
fields.description: RADIUS Security Trusted CA Cert Name. This field can be configured only when type is RADIUS with radius-server-mode configured as AUTH_ONLY or AUTH_AND_COA

fields.name: radsec-trusted-servercert-name
fields.description: RADIUS Security Server Certificate Name. This field can be configured only when type is RADIUS with radius-server-mode configured as AUTH_ONLY or AUTH_AND_COA.

fields.name: replay-protection
fields.description: Replay protection for DAC(Dynamic Authorization Client) requests this field can be configured only when type is RADIUS and radius-server-mode is equal to COA_ONLY or AUTH_AND_COA.

fields.name: rfc5176-enforcement-mode
fields.description: Enforcement mode of RFC5176.

fields.name: rfc5997
fields.description: When enabled, this parameter allows the Instant AP to send a status-server request to determine the actual status of the authentication or accounting server. This proves useful when there is a authentication or request time rfc5997—RFC5997 support enabled for both authentication and accounting on the authentication server. auth-only—RFC5997 support enabled for authentication only. acct-only—RFC5997 support enabled for accounting only no rfc5997—Disables RFC5997 support for the authentication server.

fields.description: Source VLAN Interface to use in messages to the Auth server This field can be configured only when type is TACACS or RADIUS with radius-server-mode configured as AUTH_ONLY or AUTH_AND_COA.

fields.name: tcp-port
fields.description: Port number used by the server. This field can be configured only when type is TACACS

fields.name: timeout
fields.description: Maximum time, in seconds, that the manager device(AP, GW and SW_CX) waits before timing out the request and resending it. For CX, range is 1-60. If not specified, the global timeout value will be picked. For AP, the default value of RADIUS and LDAP is 5, TACACS is 20. This field can be configured only when type is TACACS, LDAP, or RADIUS with radius-server-mode configured as AUTH_ONLY or AUTH_AND_COA

fields.description: TLS Initial connection timeout (timeout for TLS handshake). For CX, if not specified, the global TLS Initial connection timeout value will be picked. fields.name: tracking-method

fields.name: tracking-mode
fields.description: Tracking mode of the server. Default value of tracking-mode is any. This field can be configured only when type is RADIUS with radius-server-mode configured as AUTH_ONLY or AUTH_AND_COA

fields.name: type
fields.description: Auth Server Type. AP support server types are RADIUS, LDAP, TACACS and XMLAPI. CX supports server types RADIUS and TACACS. PVOS supports RADIUS and TACACS. Type is a mandatory parameter for CX and PVOS and can not be modified. GW supports RADIUS, TACACS, WINDOWS and LDAP

fields.name: use-ip-for-calling-station-id

fields.name: use-md5

fields.name: vrf

fields.description: This option is used to set the Channel field in the Beacon Report Request frame. fields.description: Enable Last Beacon Request Indication sub-element in Beacon Report Request.

fields.description: Measurement Duration field in the Beacon Report Request frame. The Measurement Duration is set to the duration of the requested measurement. It is expressed in units of TUs.

fields.description: Measurement Mode for Beacon Reports. The mode should be one of active-all-ch|active-ch-rpt|beacon-table|passive. Default: beacon-table

fields.name: name
fields.description: Beacon report request profile name

fields.name: random-interval
fields.description: Randomization Interval field in the Beacon Report Request frame. The Randomization Interval is used to specify the desired maximum random delay in the measurement start time. It is expressed in units of TUs (Time Units). A Randomization Interval of 0 in a measurement request indicates that no random delay is to be used.

fields.name: reg-class
fields.description: Regulatory Class for Beacon Report Request. Value: auto, 1, 12, 81, 115, or 131. Default auto to use value based on country code

fields.name: report-detail
fields.description: Value for the Detail field in the Reporting Detail sub-element present in the Beacon Report Request frame.

fields.name: request-info
fields.description: Contents of the Request Information IE that could be present in the Beacon Report Request frame. The Request Information IE is present for all Measurement Modes except the Beacon Table mode. It consists of a list of Element IDs that should be included by the client in the response frame. Any valid element ID in the x/y/z format. For example, 0/21/22.

fields.name: prohibit-arp-spoofing
fields.description: Detects and prohibits arp spoofing. When this option is enabled, possible arp spoofing attacks are logged and an SNMP trap is sent.

fields.name: prohibit-ip-spoof-all
fields.description: Detects ARP spoofing, when an intruder sends ARP using the IP and MAC addresses of a known user. When this option is enabled, additional check for the user route cache entry is performed. If the route cache entry is not found or if found, but the route cache entry MAC does not match with the sender MAC in ARP frame, then, the frame is marked as spoof. The IP spoofing attacks are logged and an SNMP trap is sent. If the Prohibit IP Spoofing option is enabled, the controller denies all the traffic from the client using an IP address that is used by another client that has an entry in the user table. This option does not allow multiple MAC addresses to use the same IP address.

fields.description: List of attack-rate protocol, rate and action configurations. Sets rates which, if exceeded, can indicate a denial of service attack.

fields.name: protocol
fields.description: Protocol to monitor for Denial of Service attacks.

fields.name: rate
fields.description: Number of requests per 30 seconds. Valid range 1-16384

fields.name: ipv6.drop-ip-fragments
fields.description: When enabled, all IP fragments are dropped. You should not enable this option unless instructed to do so by an Aruba representative

fields.name: ipv6.enable-per-packet-logging
fields.description: Enables logging of every packet if logging is enabled for the corresponding session rule. Normally, one event is logged per session. If you enable this option, each packet in the session is logged. You should not enable this option unless instructed to do so by an Aruba representative, as doing so may create unnecessary overhead on the managed device.

fields.name: ipv6.enable-stateful-icmp
fields.description: Enables stateful ICMP processing. This parameter create sessions for ICMP errors and denies unidirectional replies. Disabled by default.

fields.name: ipv6.enforce-tcp-handshake
fields.description: Prevents data from passing between two clients until the three-way TCP handshake has been performed. This option should be disabled when you have mobile clients on the network as enabling this option will cause mobility to fail. You can enable this option if there are no mobile clients on the network.

fields.name: ipv6.enforce-tcp-sequence
fields.description: Enforces the TCP sequence numbers for all packets. Disabled by default

fields.name: ipv6.ext-hdr-parse-len
fields.description: Set the threshold value beyond which the IPv6 header will not be parsed and the packet will be dropped. Default value 100. Range 100-300

fields.name: ipv6.prohibit-ip-spoofing
fields.description: Detects IP spoofing (where an intruder sends messages using the IP address of a trusted client). When this option is enabled, source and destination IP and MAC addresses are checked; possible IP spoofing attacks are logged and an SNMP trap is sent. Enabled in IPv4, disabled in IPv6.

fields.name: ipv6.prohibit-rst-replay
fields.description: Closes a TCP connection in both directions if a TCP RST is received from either direction. You should not enable this option unless instructed to do so by a customer support representative

fields.name: ipv6.session-idle-timeout
fields.description: Time, in seconds, that a non-TCP session can be idle before it is removed from the session table. You should not modify this option unless instructed to do so by an Aruba representative. Default value is 16. Valid range 16-300

fields.name: ipv6.tcp-session-idle-timeout
fields.description: Time, in seconds, that a TCP session can be idle before it is removed from the session table. You should not modify this option unless instructed to do so by an Aruba representative. Default value is 16. Valid range 300-43200

aruba_central_config_create_net_group.summary: Create a network group profile with unique name

fields.name: description
fields.description: A user-defined text description for this network group profile, used for administrative identification.

fields.name: exclude
fields.description: Name of another netdestination profile whose entries should be excluded (subtracted) from this network group. When specified, destinations matching the excluded profile are removed from the effective match set of this group.

fields.name: invert
fields.description: When set to true, inverts the match logic of this network group. Traffic matching any destination NOT in this group will match the ACL rule referencing this alias. Default is false (normal match behavior).

fields.name: items
fields.description: Ordered list of network destination entries within this network group profile. Each entry defines a specific network destination (host, FQDN, range, network, VLAN, port, or interface) identified by a positional index.

fields.name: address
fields.description:
A single host IP address (IPv4 or IPv6) for this
network destination entry. Applicable when type is HOST.

fields.name: address-range
fields.description:
A contiguous IP address range defined by exactly two
elements: the start address and the end address.
Applicable when type is ADDRESS_RANGE.

fields.name: default-host
fields.description: Default host entry.

fields.name: fqdn
fields.description: A Fully Qualified Domain Name (FQDN) applicable when type is FQDN.

fields.name: index
fields.description:
Positional index of this entry within the network group.
Entries are evaluated in index order. Valid range is
1 to 1000.

fields.name: network-vlan
fields.description:
The VLAN ID used for network-level VLAN-based destination
matching. Specifies a network VLAN identifier (1-4094).
Applicable when type is VLAN.

fields.name: null-interface
fields.description: Null interface destination.

fields.name: ports
fields.description:
Operator and port values. If operator == COMPARISON_RANGE then minimum and maximum values are valid,
otherwise only the minimum value is valid.

fields.name: prefix
fields.description:
A network subnet specified as an IP prefix (address and
prefix length). Applicable when
type is NETWORK.

fields.name: tunnel-name
fields.description: Tunnel interface name.

fields.name: type
fields.description:
Configures the type of this network destination entry.
This determines which sibling leaves are applicable
and must be populated: HOST requires 'address', FQDN
requires 'fqdn', ADDRESS_RANGE requires 'address-range',
NETWORK requires 'prefix', VLAN requires 'vlan' or
'network-vlan', PORT requires the 'ports' container,
and INTERFACE requires 'null-interface' or 'tunnel-name'.

fields.name: vlan
fields.description:
The VLAN ID for a host-level VLAN override entry.
Used to match traffic based on the host's VLAN
assignment (1-4094). Applicable when type is VLAN.

fields.name: vlan-offset
fields.description:
An offset value within the VLAN subnet, used to identify
a specific host address within the VLAN. Valid range is
1 to 254. Applicable when type is VLAN.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Configures the unique name for this network group (netdestination) profile. This leaf is mandatory and serves as the key for the net-group list. The name is used to reference this group as a source or destination alias in session ACLs and firewall policies. Must be between 1 and 63 characters.

fields.name: netdestination-type
fields.description: The IP address family type for this netdestination profile. Indicates whether entries are IPv4-only or IPv6-only.

fields.name: preemptive-failover
fields.description: Enable/Disable preemptive failover.

fields.name: backup-controller-ip
fields.description:
UBT zone's secondary controller's ip address.
Each zone within a profile must have a unique backup-controller ip.
This ip must also be distinct from primary-controller ip within
the same zone and primary-controller ip of other zones

fields.name: enable
fields.description: Enables/Disables UBT functionality for this zone.

fields.name: maintenance-period
fields.description:
The user-based tunnel maintenance period is in the range of
1 to 720 hours. The default value of 0 can be used to
disable the maintenance window. If maintenance period is configured
then authenticated clients will be retained in current role in the
event of controller unreachability. Client traffic will be dropped
in switch ingress port. Once controller is reachable, client
traffic flow will be resumed. If controller is not reachable even
after configured maintenance period, clients will be
deauthenticated.

fields.name: papi-security-key
fields.description:
Shared security key that will be used to encrypt UBT PAPI messages
exchanged between this switch and the controller cluster corresponding
to this zone. When not set, shared security key is not used for
encrypting papi messages.

fields.name: primary-controller-ip
fields.description:
UBT zone's primary controller's ip address.
Each zone within a profile must have a unique primary-controller ip.
This ip must also be distinct from backup-controller ip within
the same zone and backup-controller ip of other zones

fields.name: router
fields.description: BGP Router instance. Each BGP profile supports only ONE router instance (single Autonomous System). Each instance contains complete BGP configuration including neighbor/peer relationships (internal iBGP and external eBGP), routing policies, keepalive/hold timers, address family configurations (IPv4, IPv6, VPNv4), graceful restart, route reflection, and best path selection

fields.description: EVPN global configuration block containing MAC mobility settings, ARP/ND proxy options, route targets for VLANs and VLAN-aware bundles, and bridging mode policies

fields.name: mac-mobility-threshold
fields.description:
The number of MAC mobility events that are detected for a
given MAC address within the detection-window before it is identified
as a duplicate MAC address. Once the detection threshold is reached,
updates for the MAC address are suppressed.

fields.name: mac-mobility-window
fields.description:
The time interval used in detecting a duplicate MAC address.
The value can be from 1 through 1000 seconds.

fields.name: arp-suppression
fields.description:
Enable (TRUE) or disable (FALSE) ARP suppression. If true
the  Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) queries for an
IP address that is not on that network are suppressed.
Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) suppression is a
technique used to reduce the amount of ARP broadcast
flooding within individual VXLAN segments, that is between
VMs connected to the same logical switch.

fields.name: arp-suppression-extended
fields.description:
Enable (TRUE) or disable (FALSE) ARP suppression. If true
the  Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) queries for an
IP address that is not on that network are suppressed.
Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) suppression is a
technique used to reduce the amount of ARP broadcast
flooding within individual VXLAN segments, that is between
VMs connected to the same logical switch. This configuration
is mutually exclusive with arp-suppression.
Basically arp-suppression-extended provides
complete functionality of arp-suppression on L2-only
VLANs as well as on Active Gateway SVIs.

fields.name: nd-suppression
fields.description:
Enable (TRUE) or disable (FALSE) Neighbor Discovery suppression.
If true the NDP queries for an IP address that is not on that
network are suppressed. NDP suppression is a
technique used to reduce the amount of NDP Packets
flooding within individual VXLAN segments, that is between
VMs connected to the same logical switch.

fields.name: nd-suppression-extended
fields.description:
Enable (TRUE) or disable (FALSE) Neighbor Discovery suppression.
If true the NDP queries for an IP address that is not on that
network are suppressed. NDP suppression is a
technique used to reduce the amount of NDP Packets
flooding within individual VXLAN segments, that is between
VMs connected to the same logical switch. This configuration
is mutually exclusive with nd-suppression.
Basically nd-suppression-extended provides
complete functionality of nd-suppression on L2-only
VLANs as well as on Active Gateway SVIs.

fields.description: EVPN global configuration block containing MAC mobility settings, ARP/ND proxy options, route targets for VLANs and VLAN-aware bundles, and bridging mode policies

fields.name: mac-mobility-threshold
fields.description:
The number of MAC mobility events that are detected for a
given MAC address within the detection-window before it is identified
as a duplicate MAC address. Once the detection threshold is reached,
updates for the MAC address are suppressed.

fields.name: mac-mobility-window
fields.description:
The time interval used in detecting a duplicate MAC address.
The value can be from 1 through 1000 seconds.

fields.name: arp-suppression
fields.description:
Enable (TRUE) or disable (FALSE) ARP suppression. If true
the  Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) queries for an
IP address that is not on that network are suppressed.
Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) suppression is a
technique used to reduce the amount of ARP broadcast
flooding within individual VXLAN segments, that is between
VMs connected to the same logical switch.

fields.name: arp-suppression-extended
fields.description:
Enable (TRUE) or disable (FALSE) ARP suppression. If true
the  Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) queries for an
IP address that is not on that network are suppressed.
Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) suppression is a
technique used to reduce the amount of ARP broadcast
flooding within individual VXLAN segments, that is between
VMs connected to the same logical switch. This configuration
is mutually exclusive with arp-suppression.
Basically arp-suppression-extended provides
complete functionality of arp-suppression on L2-only
VLANs as well as on Active Gateway SVIs.

fields.name: nd-suppression
fields.description:
Enable (TRUE) or disable (FALSE) Neighbor Discovery suppression.
If true the NDP queries for an IP address that is not on that
network are suppressed. NDP suppression is a
technique used to reduce the amount of NDP Packets
flooding within individual VXLAN segments, that is between
VMs connected to the same logical switch.

fields.name: nd-suppression-extended
fields.description:
Enable (TRUE) or disable (FALSE) Neighbor Discovery suppression.
If true the NDP queries for an IP address that is not on that
network are suppressed. NDP suppression is a
technique used to reduce the amount of NDP Packets
flooding within individual VXLAN segments, that is between
VMs connected to the same logical switch. This configuration
is mutually exclusive with nd-suppression.
Basically nd-suppression-extended provides
complete functionality of nd-suppression on L2-only
VLANs as well as on Active Gateway SVIs.

fields.name: redistribute-local-mac

fields.name: redistribute-local-svi

local IP address and MAC address of the SVI interfaces corresponding
to EVPN enabled VLANs.

fields.name: detection-protection
fields.description: Intrusion Detection/Pretection System offers a wide selection of intrusion detection and protection features to protect the network against wireless threats. The following policies can be configured: 1. Infrastructure Detection Policies — Specifies the policy for detecting wireless attacks    on access points. 2. Client Detection Policies — Specifies the policy for detecting wireless attacks on clients. 3. Infrastructure Protection Policies — Specifies the policy for protecting access points    from wireless attacks. 4. Client Protection Policies — Specifies the policy for protecting clients from wireless attacks. 5. Containment Methods— Prevents unauthorized stations from connecting to network.

fields.name: ghosttunnel-client
fields.description:
Ghost tunnel attack is a backdoor transmission method that can be used in an isolated
environment. A ghost tunnel attack uses 802.11 probe request packets or beacon packets
to communicate with the host without establishing a Wi-Fi connection.

For the client-side ghost tunnel attack, the AP monitors the abnormal probe request
packets in the wireless environment. When a client is heard by the AP, it looks for
abnormal probe request packets from the client. The system reports a ghost tunnel detection
event with the client's MAC address when the alert criteria is met. If only abnormal probe
request packets are monitored and there is no matching client, then the reported event does
not contain the client's MAC address.

fields.name: attack-interval
fields.description: Time interval at which the packet count is checked for client side ghost tunnel attacks.

fields.name: attack-threshold
fields.description:
Number of abnormal probe request packets required to flag a ghost tunnel attack.
When the number of probe request packets that match the ghost tunnel attack exceed the threshold
within the defined attack interval, the event is flagged as a ghost tunnel attack.

fields.name: quiet-time
fields.description:
Time to wait before resuming ghost tunnel attack detection after an attack
is detected. This avoids flooding of event logs.

fields.name: ghosttunnel-server
fields.description:
Ghost tunnel attack is a backdoor transmission method that can be used in an isolated
environment. A ghost tunnel attack uses 802.11 probe request packets or beacon packets
to communicate with the host without establishing a Wi-Fi connection.

The server side of ghost tunnel uses beacon packets to send commands to the client and
the client sends probe-request automatically in response to the server's request, thereby
infecting the system. The server-side ghost tunnel attack detection system relies on
identifying abnormal beacon packets and flagging the attacking server.

fields.name: attack-interval
fields.description: Time interval at which the packet count is checked for ghost tunnel attacks from servers.

fields.name: attack-threshold
fields.description:
Number of abnormal beacon packets required to flag a ghost tunnel attack.
When the number of beacon packets that match the ghost tunnel attack rule exceed the threshold
within the defined attack interval, the event is flagged as a ghost tunnel attack.

fields.name: quiet-time
fields.description:
Time to wait before resuming ghost tunnel attack detection after an attack is detected.
This avoids flooding of event logs.

fields.name: ghosttunnel-client
fields.description:
Ghost tunnel attack is a backdoor transmission method that can be used in an isolated
environment. A ghost tunnel attack uses 802.11 probe request packets or beacon packets
to communicate with the host without establishing a Wi-Fi connection.

For the client-side ghost tunnel attack, the AP monitors the abnormal probe request
packets in the wireless environment. When a client is heard by the AP, it looks for
abnormal probe request packets from the client. The system reports a ghost tunnel detection
event with the client's MAC address when the alert criteria is met. If only abnormal probe
request packets are monitored and there is no matching client, then the reported event does
not contain the client's MAC address.

fields.name: attack-interval
fields.description: Time interval at which the packet count is checked for client side ghost tunnel attacks.

fields.name: attack-threshold
fields.description:
Number of abnormal probe request packets required to flag a ghost tunnel attack.
When the number of probe request packets that match the ghost tunnel attack exceed the threshold
within the defined attack interval, the event is flagged as a ghost tunnel attack.

fields.name: quiet-time
fields.description:
Time to wait before resuming ghost tunnel attack detection after an attack
is detected. This avoids flooding of event logs.

fields.name: ghosttunnel-server
fields.description:
Ghost tunnel attack is a backdoor transmission method that can be used in an isolated
environment. A ghost tunnel attack uses 802.11 probe request packets or beacon packets
to communicate with the host without establishing a Wi-Fi connection.

The server side of ghost tunnel uses beacon packets to send commands to the client and
the client sends probe-request automatically in response to the server's request, thereby
infecting the system. The server-side ghost tunnel attack detection system relies on
identifying abnormal beacon packets and flagging the attacking server.

Configure external antenna connectors for an AP.
If your AP has external antenna connectors, you need to configure the transmit power of the system.
The configuration must ensure that the system's EIRP is in compliance with the limit specified

You can also measure or calculate additional attenuation between the device and antenna before configuring the antenna gain.

fields.description: Control AP to enable/disable SAM (Smart Antenna Module) feature. This feature is enabled by default. This requires reboot AP when switch enable/disable SAM. For SAM it provides the below main feature: Auto RF cable loss detection, especially for the RF cables that installed between AP RPSMA(N) and N-type connector for outdoor APs, We allowed customers to equip different types or lengths RF cables for different user scenarios, and Aruba AP equipment installers can leverage this feature, (no need to do the RF cables cable lose value by themselves, then provide one static cable lose value and the antenna gain value to provision AP, this is a fairly crude measurement process).

fields.description: The list of profiles in which AP configure its 2.4GHz/5GHz/Secondary 5GHz/6GHz radio settings. Each radio profile includes:  Extremely High Throughput (EHT) related settings,  Adaptive Radio Management (ARM) related settings,  Very High Throughput (VHT) related settings (5GHz only),  High Efficiency (HE) related settings (6GHz only),  radio enable/disable, radio mode, dot11h, etc.

fields.description: Enable the SSID to broadcast the AP Name information in the beacons frames

fields.name: afc-mode
fields.description:
Automated Frequency Coordination (AFC) is a service that enables the 6G radio of
Stand-Power (SP) or outdoor APs within US. With AFC function, APs can work in Low
Power Indoor (LPI) mode or Stand Power (SP) when Downloadable Regulatory Table (DRT)
incudes both LPI and SP channels.

fields.name: arm-control
fields.description:
Adaptive Radio Management (ARM) settings can be configured separately for 2.4GHz/5GHz/6GHz.
This enables you to maximize the efficiency of the network in dense RF environments.
This includes configuring channels, max/min bandwidth, max/min power etc.

fields.name: arm-wids-override
fields.description:
By default, WIDS protection is on dynamic mode. If an AP is heavily loaded with client
traffic and the CPU utilization exceeds the threshold limit, the WIDS processing is suspended.
This causes more CPU cycles to handle the client traffic. When the CPU utilization is within
the threshold limit, the WIDS processing is resumed. When disable-arm-wids-functions is on,
the AP will stop process frames for WIDS purposes regardless of whether the
AP is heavily loaded or not. The WIDS functionality will not take effect.
When disable-arm-wids-functions is off, the AP will always process frames for WIDS
purposes even when it is heavily loaded with client traffic. The WIDS functionality will always take effect.

fields.name: background-spectrum-monitoring
fields.description:
Allow the AP in access mode to continue with normal access service
to clients, while performing additional function of monitoring RF interference (from both neighboring
APs and non Wi-Fi sources such as, microwaves and cordless phones) on the channel they are currently serving clients.

fields.name: cell-size-reduction
fields.description:
The cell size reduction feature allows you to manage dense deployments and to increase overall system performance and capacity by shrinking an AP's receive coverage area,
thereby minimizing co-channel interference and optimizing channel reuse. This value should only be changed if the network is experiencing performance issues.
The sensitivity range values can be configured from 0 to 55.
The default 0 reduction allows the radio to retain its current default Rx sensitivity value.
If you configure this feature to use a non-default value, you must also reduce the radio's transmission (Tx) power to match its new received (Rx) sensitivity level.

fields.name: channel-switch-announcement-count

fields.name: csd-override

fields.name: frame-bursting-mode
fields.description:
In some dense deployments, it is possible for APs to hear other APs on the same channel.
This creates co-channel interference where the traffic of an active client could affect the air traffic of neighboring APs within the same channel.
Aruba allows users to control frame bursting behavior of the AP, irrespective of whether there are one or more active clients associated to it.

dynamic — Frame bursting will be enabled only when one active client is connected to the AP,
 and frame bursting will be disabled when there is more than one active client.
on — Frame bursting mode is always enabled.
off — Frame bursting mode is always disabled.

fields.name: smart-antenna
fields.description:
Enable smart antenna to allow smart antenna polarization. This feature helps optimize
the selection of antenna polarization values based on data collected from the training of polarization pattern
combinations . This feature identifies the clients most likely to benefit from smart antenna polarization, based on

fields.description:
Enable broadcasting two kinds (HELD and SUPL) of links to client in Access Network Query Protocol (ANQP)
element 267. HELD means Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) enabled location delivery (HELD) and SUPL means
Secure User Plane Location.

fields.name: auth-req-thresh
fields.description: SNR threshold below which incoming authentication requests are ignored. Use this parameter instead of the local probe request threshold parameter to filter out low SNR authentication request.

fields.name: cdc
fields.description: Advertizes the Cellular Data Capability (CDC) attribute of an MBO.

fields.name: disable-on-6ghz-mesh
fields.description: This is used when there are more than 3 6GHz SSIDs are created. It has to be set so that AP can know which SSID needs to be disabled when mesh enabled. This might be no use later.

fields.name: dot11k
fields.description: Enables 802.11k roaming on the SSID profile.The 802.11k protocol enables APs and clients to dynamically measure the available radio resources.

fields.name: dot11k-profile-name
fields.description: To set the bound dot11k profile name

fields.name: dot11r
fields.description: Enables 802.11r on the SSID profile.802.11r or fast BSS FT is an IEEE standard that permits continuous connectivity across wireless devices during client mobility. Fast BSS Transition mechanism minimizes the delay in roaming when a client transitions from one BSS to another within the same cluster.

fields.name: dot11r-key-duration

fields.name: dot11r-ondemand-keyfetch
fields.description: Enables 802.11r on demand key fetch from cloud key management service when the AP's local key cache lookup fails for client matching pairwise key to complete fast roaming.

fields.name: dot11v

fields.name: dtim-period
fields.description: The DTIM interval determines how often the AP should deliver the buffered broadcast and multicast frames to associated clients in the powersaving mode. When configured, the client checks for buffered data on the AP at the specified number of beacons. You can also configure a higher value for DTIM interval for power saving.

fields.name: essid

level-1: for support for dynamic fragments that are
contained within a S-MPDU, no support for dynamic
fragments within an A-MPDU that is not a S-MPDU.
level-2: for support for dynamic fragments that are
contained within a S-MPDU and support for up to one
dynamic fragment for each MSDU within an A-MPDU.
level-3: for support for dynamic fragments that are
contained within a S-MPDU and support for up to four
dynamic fragment for each MSDU within an A-MPDU. Note:
Further limited by each AP's radio HW capabilities

fields.name: high-throughput
fields.description: High Throughput (HT): Introduced in 802.11n (Wi-Fi 4), includes features like wider channels (up to 40 MHz),  MIMO (up to 4 spatial streams), 64-QAM, short guard interval, and frame aggregation to increase data rates and performance. Very High Throughput (VHT): Introduced in 802.11ac (Wi-Fi 5), includes features like even wider channels (up to 160 MHz),  higher modulation (256-QAM), more spatial streams (up to 8), MU-MIMO, and beamforming to further enhance data rates and network efficiency. This configures high-throughput (HT) and very-high-throughput (VHT) related settings. These features collectively enhance the data rates, capacity, and overall performance of wireless networks, making them capable of handling large amounts of data efficiently.

fields.description:
A list of Modulation Coding Scheme (MCS) values or ranges of values to be supported on this SSID.
The MCS you choose determines the channel width (20 MHz vs. 40 MHz) and the number of spatial streams used by the mesh node.
To specify a series of different values, separate each value with a comma.

fields.name: temporal-diversity
fields.description:
Enable temporal diversity. When this setting is enabled and the client is not responding to 802.11 packets, the
AP will launch two hardware retries; if the hardware retries are not successful then it attempts software retries.

fields.name: very-high-throughput
fields.description: Enable support for VHT (802.11ac ) on the SSID.

fields.name: vht-mu-txbf
fields.description:
Enable VHT Multi-User Transmit Beamforming. If this parameter is disabled,
all other Multi-User Transmit Beamforming configuration parameters have no effect.

fields.name: vht-supported-mcs-map
fields.description:
Comma separated list of maximum supported MCS for spatial streams 1 through 4.
Valid values for maximum MCS are 7, 8, 9, and '-' (if spatial stream is not supported).
Maximum MCS of a spatial stream cannot be higher than the previous streams.
If an MCS is not valid for a particular combination of bandwidth and number of spatial streams,
it will not be used for Tx and Rx. Only '-' is not supported.

fields.name: vht-txbf-explicit
fields.description:
Enable VHT Explicit Transmit Beamforming for the 802.11ac-capable APs.
When this feature is enabled, the AP requests information about the MIMO channel and
uses that information to transmit data over multiple transmit streams using a calculated steering matrix.
The result is higher throughput due to improved signal at the beamformee (the receiving client).
If this parameter is disabled, all other transmit beamforming settings will not take effect.

fields.description: Time in seconds before client can associate after MFP try again later reject

fields.description: When enabled, the SSID only supports MFP capable clients.

fields.name: qos-management
fields.description: Wi-Fi Quality of Service (QoS) Management certification delivers a standardized approach to QoS for devices and applications to prioritize traffic flows for both client devices and APs. This includes configuring QoS Management related configuration.

fields.name: scs
fields.description:
Enable/Disable Stream Classification Service (SCS) feature.
SCS: enables classification and Wi-Fi QoS treatment of specific IP flows, including flows to and from 5G core networks,
allowing sensitive traffic such as gaming, voice, and video to be prioritized over bulk data traffic

fields.name: rrm-quiet-ie
fields.description: Enable Radio Resource Management (RRM) IE profile to define the information elements advertised by an AP.

fields.name: rts-threshold
fields.description: Wireless clients transmitting frames larger than this threshold must issue RTS and wait for the AP to respond with CTS. This helps prevent mid-air collisions for wireless clients that are not within wireless peer range and cannot detect when other wireless clients are transmitting.

fields.name: short-preamble
fields.description: Enables short preamble for 802.11b/g radios. Network performance may be higher when short preamble is enabled. In mixed radio environments, some 802.11b wireless client stations may experience difficulty associating with the AP using short preamble. To use only long preamble, disable short preamble. Legacy client devices that use only long preamble generally can be updated to support short preamble.

fields.name: ssid-utf8
fields.description: Encodes the SSID. When enabled, the SSID name is displayed in the UTF-8 format.SSIDs are not encoded by default.

fields.name: wmm-cfg
fields.description: Wi-Fi Multimedia (WMM) refers to a Wi-Fi Alliance interoperability certification, based on the IEEE 802.11e standard. It provides basic QoS features to IEEE 802.11 networks. WMM prioritizes traffic according to four Access Categories (ACs): voice (AC_VO), video (AC_VI), best effort (AC_BE), and background (AC_BK). This includes configuring Enhanced Distributed Channel Access (EDCA) parameters for each AC of AP and Station (STA), mapping between WMM ACs and Differentiated Services Codepoint (DSCP) tags.

fields.name: ap-background
fields.description: Configures the EDCA parameters for AC_BK of AP.

fields.description: The delimiter between mac address and SSID. For example, the delimiter is dash. The called-station-id like aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff-wlanssid.

fields.name: mac-address-delimiter
fields.description: By default, called-station-id is AP MAC Address string and no delimiter, when configure mac-address-delimiter, AP MAC Address will be added delimiter in authentication packet.

fields.name: type

Configure the called-station-id types.
For AP, The type includes AP group, AP MAC address, AP name, AP IP or user vlan. The default value is AP MAC address.

fields.name: upper-case

fields.name: machine-auth
fields.description: Configure a machine authentication rule. When a Windows device boots, it logs onto the network domain using a machine account. Within the domain, the device is authenticated before computer group policies and software settings can be executed; this process is known as machine authentication. Machine authentication ensures that only authorized devices are allowed on the network. You can configure 802.1X for both user and machine authentication. This tightens the authentication process further, since both the device and user need to be authenticated. This feature is applicable for 802.1x authenticaion and it is only applicable for AP.

Default 0. level-0: not support dynamic fragmentation.
level-1: for support for dynamic fragments that are
contained within a S-MPDU, no support for dynamic
fragments within an A-MPDU that is not a S-MPDU.
level-2: for support for dynamic fragments that are
contained within a S-MPDU and support for up to one
dynamic fragment for each MSDU within an A-MPDU.
level-3: for support for dynamic fragments that are
contained within a S-MPDU and support for up to four
dynamic fragment for each MSDU within an A-MPDU. Note:
Further limited by each AP's radio HW capabilities

fields.name: high-throughput
fields.description: High Throughput (HT): Introduced in 802.11n (Wi-Fi 4), includes features like wider channels (up to 40 MHz),  MIMO (up to 4 spatial streams), 64-QAM, short guard interval, and frame aggregation to increase data rates and performance. Very High Throughput (VHT): Introduced in 802.11ac (Wi-Fi 5), includes features like even wider channels (up to 160 MHz),  higher modulation (256-QAM), more spatial streams (up to 8), MU-MIMO, and beamforming to further enhance data rates and network efficiency. This configures high-throughput (HT) and very-high-throughput (VHT) related settings. These features collectively enhance the data rates, capacity, and overall performance of wireless networks, making them capable of handling large amounts of data efficiently.

AP will launch two hardware retries; if the hardware retries are not successful then it attempts software retries.

Valid values for maximum MCS are 7, 8, 9, and '-' (if spatial stream is not supported).
Maximum MCS of a spatial stream cannot be higher than the previous streams.
If an MCS is not valid for a particular combination of bandwidth and number of spatial streams,
it will not be used for Tx and Rx. Only '-' is not supported.

fields.name: vht-txbf-explicit
fields.description:
Enable VHT Explicit Transmit Beamforming for the 802.11ac-capable APs.
When this feature is enabled, the AP requests information about the MIMO channel and
uses that information to transmit data over multiple transmit streams using a calculated steering matrix.
The result is higher throughput due to improved signal at the beamformee (the receiving client).
If this parameter is disabled, all other transmit beamforming settings will not take effect.

fields.name: high-throughput.vht-supported-mcs-map
fields.description: Comma separated list of maximum supported MCS for spatial streams 1 through 4. Valid values for maximum MCS are 7, 8, 9, and '-' (if spatial stream is not supported). Maximum MCS of a spatial stream cannot be higher than the previous streams. If an MCS is not valid for a particular combination of bandwidth and number of spatial streams, it will not be used for Tx and Rx. Only '-' is not supported.

fields.name: high-throughput.vht-txbf-explicit
fields.description: Enable VHT Explicit Transmit Beamforming for the 802.11ac-capable APs. When this feature is enabled, the AP requests information about the MIMO channel and uses that information to transmit data over multiple transmit streams using a calculated steering matrix. The result is higher throughput due to improved signal at the beamformee (the receiving client). If this parameter is disabled, all other transmit beamforming settings will not take effect.

fields.name: inactivity-timeout
fields.description: Configures a timeout value for the inactive client sessions. When a client session is inactive for the specified duration, the session expires and the clients are required to log in again.

fields.name: local-probe-req-thresh
fields.description: RSSI (Received Signal Strength Indicator) threshold value to limit the number of incoming probe requests. When enabled, controls the system response to the broadcast probe requests sent by clients to search for the available SSIDs and ignores the probe request if required.

fields.name: max-clients-threshold
fields.description: Maximum number of wireless clients for the AP. This parameter is limited to 1024 clients per radio. Default value for this parameter is the maximum number of clients supported by the AP.

fields.name: max-retries
fields.description: Maximum number of retries allowed for the AP to send a frame.

fields.name: mbo
fields.description: Enables the Agile Multiband Operations (MBO). Enables the mfp-capable, 802.11k and 802.11u-interworking implicitly on the AP.

fields.name: mfp-association-comeback-time
fields.description: Time in seconds before client can associate after MFP try again later reject

fields.name: mfp-capable
fields.description: When enabled, the SSID supports management frame protection (MFP) capable clients and traditional clients.

fields.name: mfp-required
fields.description: When enabled, the SSID only supports MFP capable clients.

fields.name: mobility-domain-id
fields.description: Mobility Domain Identifier. An  AP uses this parameter to announce that it is a part of the AP group that constitutes a mobility domain.

fields.name: qbss-load
fields.description: Enables the AP to advertise the QBSS load element.

fields.name: qos-management
fields.description: Wi-Fi Quality of Service (QoS) Management certification delivers a standardized approach to QoS for devices and applications to prioritize traffic flows for both client devices and APs. This includes configuring QoS Management related configuration.

fields.name: scs
fields.description:
Enable/Disable Stream Classification Service (SCS) feature.
SCS: enables classification and Wi-Fi QoS treatment of specific IP flows, including flows to and from 5G core networks,
allowing sensitive traffic such as gaming, voice, and video to be prioritized over bulk data traffic

fields.name: qos-management.scs
fields.description: Enable/Disable Stream Classification Service (SCS) feature. SCS: enables classification and Wi-Fi QoS treatment of specific IP flows, including flows to and from 5G core networks, allowing sensitive traffic such as gaming, voice, and video to be prioritized over bulk data traffic

fields.name: refresh-direction
fields.description: The refresh direction of WLAN SSID profile.

fields.name: rf-band
fields.description: Radio frequency band on which this SSID will be broadcast. You can select one of the following options:

fields.name: rrm-quiet-ie
fields.description: Enable Radio Resource Management (RRM) IE profile to define the information elements advertised by an AP.

fields.name: rts-threshold
fields.description: Wireless clients transmitting frames larger than this threshold must issue RTS and wait for the AP to respond with CTS. This helps prevent mid-air collisions for wireless clients that are not within wireless peer range and cannot detect when other wireless clients are transmitting.

fields.name: short-preamble
fields.description: Enables short preamble for 802.11b/g radios. Network performance may be higher when short preamble is enabled. In mixed radio environments, some 802.11b wireless client stations may experience difficulty associating with the AP using short preamble. To use only long preamble, disable short preamble. Legacy client devices that use only long preamble generally can be updated to support short preamble.

fields.name: ssid-utf8
fields.description: Encodes the SSID. When enabled, the SSID name is displayed in the UTF-8 format.SSIDs are not encoded by default.

fields.name: wmm-cfg
fields.description: Wi-Fi Multimedia (WMM) refers to a Wi-Fi Alliance interoperability certification, based on the IEEE 802.11e standard. It provides basic QoS features to IEEE 802.11 networks. WMM prioritizes traffic according to four Access Categories (ACs): voice (AC_VO), video (AC_VI), best effort (AC_BE), and background (AC_BK). This includes configuring Enhanced Distributed Channel Access (EDCA) parameters for each AC of AP and Station (STA), mapping between WMM ACs and Differentiated Services Codepoint (DSCP) tags.

fields.description: Configure this parameter to be sent with the RADIUS attribute Called Station ID for authentication and accounting requests. For AP, this API is applicable for WLAN profile and AP port profile. For GW, this API is applicable for the authentication server profile. This feature is applicable for AP and GW.

fields.description: Include SSID in called-station-id attribute.

fields.name: include-ssid-delimiter
fields.description: The delimiter between mac address and SSID. For example, the delimiter is dash. The called-station-id like aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff-wlanssid.

fields.name: mac-address-delimiter
fields.description: By default, called-station-id is AP MAC Address string and no delimiter, when configure mac-address-delimiter, AP MAC Address will be added delimiter in authentication packet.

fields.name: type

Configure the called-station-id types.
For AP, The type includes AP group, AP MAC address, AP name, AP IP or user vlan. The default value is AP MAC address.

aruba_central_config_create_named_condit.summary: Create a new named condition with unique name for Traffic Class

fields.name: association
fields.description: Association context for the named condition, defining the scope and application domain where this traffic classification rule will be active. The association type determines how the named condition integrates with different policy network contexts within the system.  Association types typically include interface-specific or role-based contexts, allowing for control over where traffic classification rules are applied.

fields.name: condition-rule
fields.description: Ordered list of traffic classification rules that collectively define the named condition (Traffic Class). Each rule specifies matching criteria for network traffic using various protocol headers and application characteristics.  All rules within this list must conform to the same classification type as specified in the parent named condition's rules-type field.

fields.name: count
fields.description: Enable packet counting for traffic matching this rule.

fields.name: description
fields.description: Optional user-defined description or comment for this rule entry.

fields.name: ignore
fields.description:
When set to true, this rule is ignored during traffic
classification processing and no further action will be taken except
for log and count.

fields.name: log
fields.description:
Enable logging for traffic matching this rule when used in access control contexts.
This option is available only for network ACL rule types (Ethernet, IP, IPv6).
When enabled, matching traffic events are recorded in the system logs, providing
audit trails for security monitoring and troubleshooting.

fields.name: position
fields.description:
Sequential position number for this rule within the named condition's rule list.
Position determines the order of rule evaluation, with lower numbers processed
first. This ordering is critical for traffic classification logic where multiple
rules might match the same traffic flow. Position values must be unique within
the named condition and should allow.

fields.name: description
fields.description: Optional user-defined description or comment for the Named Condition (Traffic Class).

fields.name: name
fields.description: Unique identifier for the named condition, which becomes the Traffic Class name on the device. This name must be unique within the system and follows standard naming conventions for network device objects. The Traffic Class name is used by policies to reference this traffic classification rule.

fields.name: reverse-named-condition
fields.description: Boolean flag to enable reverse functionality for role-based policies. When enabled, this creates bidirectional traffic classification for role-based access control, allowing policies to automatically apply matching rules in both directions of communication flows.

fields.name: rules-type
fields.description: Classification type for the named condition, determining which protocol layers and fields are available for traffic matching.  Available types include: - IP-based conditions: Match on network layer protocols and addressing - Ethernet-based conditions: Match on data link layer MAC and VLAN information - Application-based conditions: Match on identified applications and services  All rules within a single named condition must use the same classification type.

fields.name: alg-config
fields.description: Application Layer Gateway (ALG) configuration for Distributed Services Switches (DSS). This container is only available when alg-service is set to ICMP, DNS, FTP, MSRPC, or SUNRPC. Each ALG type exposes its own sub-container with protocol-specific configuration options.

fields.name: icmp-alg
fields.description:
Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP) ALG configuration
for Distributed Services Switches (DSS). Allows filtering
ICMP traffic by specific message type and code.

fields.name: code
fields.description:
ICMP code that provides additional detail for the specified
ICMP type. This is a required field. For example, for type 3
(Destination Unreachable), code 0 means Network Unreachable
and code 1 means Host Unreachable. Valid range: 0-18.

fields.name: type
fields.description:
ICMP message type number. This is a required field. Common
values include 0 (Echo Reply), 3 (Destination Unreachable),
8 (Echo Request), and 11 (Time Exceeded). Valid range: 0-255.

fields.name: dns-alg
fields.description:
Domain Name System (DNS) ALG configuration for Distributed
Services Switches (DSS). Enables inspection of DNS packets
with options to drop anomalous packets and limit message size.

fields.name: drop-large-domain-name-packets
fields.description:
When set to true, drops DNS packets where any label length
is 64 bytes or higher, exceeding the DNS specification limit.
Default: false.

fields.name: drop-long-label-packets
fields.description:
When set to true, drops DNS packets where the total domain
name size exceeds 255 bytes. Default: false.

fields.name: drop-multi-question-packets
fields.description:
When set to true, drops DNS packets that contain more than
one question in the query section. This helps prevent
certain DNS-based attacks. Default: false.

fields.name: max-message-length
fields.description:
Maximum allowed DNS message length in bytes. Messages
exceeding this length are dropped. Valid range: 1-8129.
Default: 512 bytes.

fields.name: ftp-alg
fields.description:
File Transfer Protocol (FTP) ALG configuration for Distributed
Services Switches (DSS). Enables inspection of FTP control
connections to correctly handle dynamic data port negotiation.
The net-service protocol must be TCP (protocol 6 or IP_TCP).

fields.name: allow-mismatch-ip-address
fields.description:
When set to true, allows FTP data connections where the IP
address in the FTP PORT/PASV command payload differs from
the IP header source address. This is useful in NAT
environments. Default: false.

fields.name: msrpc-alg
fields.description:
Microsoft Remote Procedure Call (MSRPC) ALG configuration for
Distributed Services Switches (DSS). Enables inspection of
MSRPC endpoint mapper traffic to correctly handle dynamic
port assignments. The net-service protocol must be TCP or UDP
and the port must be 135 (endpoint mapper).

fields.name: program-uuids
fields.description:
List of MSRPC program UUIDs to inspect. Each UUID identifies
a specific MSRPC service interface.

fields.name: timeout
fields.description:
Timeout in seconds for tracking MSRPC endpoint bindings.
After this period, dynamically learned port mappings are
removed. Default: 60 seconds.

fields.name: sunrpc-alg
fields.description:
SUN Remote Procedure Call (SUNRPC) ALG configuration for
Distributed Services Switches (DSS). Enables inspection of
SUNRPC portmapper traffic to correctly handle dynamic port
assignments. The net-service protocol must be TCP or UDP
and the port must be 111 (portmapper).

fields.name: program-ids
fields.description:
List of RPC program identifiers to inspect. Each program ID
corresponds to a specific RPC service (e.g., NFS is 100003).

fields.name: timeout
fields.description:
Timeout in seconds for tracking SUNRPC program identifier
bindings. After this period, dynamically learned port
mappings are removed. Default: 60 seconds.

fields.name: alg-config.icmp-alg
fields.description: Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP) ALG configuration for Distributed Services Switches (DSS). Allows filtering ICMP traffic by specific message type and code.

fields.name: code
fields.description:
ICMP code that provides additional detail for the specified
ICMP type. This is a required field. For example, for type 3
(Destination Unreachable), code 0 means Network Unreachable
and code 1 means Host Unreachable. Valid range: 0-18.

fields.name: type
fields.description:
ICMP message type number. This is a required field. Common
values include 0 (Echo Reply), 3 (Destination Unreachable),
8 (Echo Request), and 11 (Time Exceeded). Valid range: 0-255.

fields.name: alg-config.icmp-alg.code
fields.description: ICMP code that provides additional detail for the specified ICMP type. This is a required field. For example, for type 3 (Destination Unreachable), code 0 means Network Unreachable and code 1 means Host Unreachable. Valid range: 0-18.

fields.name: alg-config.icmp-alg.type
fields.description: ICMP message type number. This is a required field. Common values include 0 (Echo Reply), 3 (Destination Unreachable), 8 (Echo Request), and 11 (Time Exceeded). Valid range: 0-255.

fields.name: alg-config.dns-alg
fields.description: Domain Name System (DNS) ALG configuration for Distributed Services Switches (DSS). Enables inspection of DNS packets with options to drop anomalous packets and limit message size.

fields.name: drop-large-domain-name-packets
fields.description:
When set to true, drops DNS packets where any label length
is 64 bytes or higher, exceeding the DNS specification limit.
Default: false.

fields.name: drop-long-label-packets
fields.description:
When set to true, drops DNS packets where the total domain
name size exceeds 255 bytes. Default: false.

fields.name: drop-multi-question-packets
fields.description:
When set to true, drops DNS packets that contain more than
one question in the query section. This helps prevent
certain DNS-based attacks. Default: false.

fields.name: max-message-length
fields.description:
Maximum allowed DNS message length in bytes. Messages
exceeding this length are dropped. Valid range: 1-8129.
Default: 512 bytes.

fields.name: alg-service
fields.description: Specifies the Application Layer Gateway (ALG) service type for this net-service. ALG enables deep packet inspection for application-specific protocols, allowing the firewall to handle dynamic port negotiation and NAT traversal. The selected ALG must be compatible with the configured protocol (TCP, UDP, or other). See the must constraint for valid protocol/ALG combinations.

fields.name: description
fields.description: An optional human-readable description for this net-service. Can be used to document the purpose or intended use. Maximum length is 128 characters.

fields.name: http-proxy
fields.description: When set to true, marks this net-service port as an HTTP proxy port for web traffic interception. Only applicable when no ALG service is configured. Default: false.

fields.name: https-proxy
fields.description: When set to true, marks this net-service port as an HTTPS proxy port for secure web traffic interception. Only applicable when no ALG service is configured. Default: false.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Unique name of the net-service. This is a required key field. Maximum length is 63 characters.

fields.name: port-range
fields.description: Port range specification for this net-service. If operator is COMPARISON_RANGE, both min and max values define the range. If operator is COMPARISON_EQ, only the min value is used as the exact port match. Cannot be used together with the ports leaf-list.

fields.name: max
fields.description:
Upper bound of port range. Only applicable when operator
is COMPARISON_RANGE. Must be greater than min. Protocol
must be TCP or UDP.

fields.name: min
fields.description:
Port value or lower bound of port range. When operator
is COMPARISON_EQ, this is the exact port to match. When
operator is COMPARISON_RANGE, this is the lower bound.
Protocol must be TCP or UDP.

fields.name: operator
fields.description:
Comparison operator for port matching. When set to
COMPARISON_EQ, matches a single port (min). When set
to COMPARISON_RANGE, matches all ports between min
and max inclusive. Protocol must be TCP or UDP.

fields.name: port-range.max
fields.description: Upper bound of port range. Only applicable when operator is COMPARISON_RANGE. Must be greater than min. Protocol must be TCP or UDP.

fields.name: port-range.min
fields.description: Port value or lower bound of port range. When operator is COMPARISON_EQ, this is the exact port to match. When operator is COMPARISON_RANGE, this is the lower bound. Protocol must be TCP or UDP.

fields.name: port-range.operator
fields.description: Comparison operator for port matching. When set to COMPARISON_EQ, matches a single port (min). When set to COMPARISON_RANGE, matches all ports between min and max inclusive. Protocol must be TCP or UDP.

fields.name: ports
fields.description: List of individual port numbers for this net-service. Cannot be used together with port-range. The protocol must be TCP or UDP when ports are specified.

items.description:
List of individual port numbers for this net-service. Cannot
be used together with port-range. The protocol must be TCP
or UDP when ports are specified.

fields.description: Specifies the IP protocol for this net-service, expressed either as an IP protocol number or a named identity (e.g., IP_TCP for 6, IP_UDP for 17). This determines which transport protocol the service matches. Must not be set when alg-service is ICMP.

fields.name: called-station-id
fields.description: Configure this parameter to be sent with the RADIUS attribute Called Station ID for authentication and accounting requests. For AP, this API is applicable for WLAN profile and AP port profile. For GW, this API is applicable for the authentication server profile. This feature is applicable for AP and GW.

fields.name: include-ssid
fields.description: Include SSID in called-station-id attribute.

fields.name: include-ssid-delimiter
fields.description: The delimiter between mac address and SSID. For example, the delimiter is dash. The called-station-id like aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff-wlanssid.

fields.name: mac-address-delimiter
fields.description: By default, called-station-id is AP MAC Address string and no delimiter, when configure mac-address-delimiter, AP MAC Address will be added delimiter in authentication packet.

fields.name: type
fields.description:
Configure the called-station-id types.
For AP, The type includes AP group, AP MAC address, AP name, AP IP or user vlan. The default value is AP MAC address.

fields.name: upper-case
fields.description: By default, called-station-id is AP MAC Address string, when enabled upper-case, AP MAC Address will be changed to upper case in authentication packet.
