fields.name: lte-modem
fields.description: Uplink LTE Modem, this feature is used to configure modem parameters for 3G or 4G uplink and only applies to AP, the 3G and 4G modems can be used to extend connectivity to places and enables the AP to automatically choose the available network in a specific region. This feature supports configuring both 3rd party modem and aruba modem, but only one modem can be used as the uplink.

fields.name: backup-link
fields.description: Mark uplink as a hot-standby uplink.

fields.name: aruba-skylark
fields.description: Enables the pre-configured profile for Aruba Skylark LTE modems. When enabled, this creates and activates the ARUBA_USB_LTE profile optimized for Skylark hardware and disables configurations for other modem types. Gateway devices only.

fields.name: auto-upgrade
fields.description: Automatic firmware upgrade for Aruba modem, this API is AP specific and only for Aruba modem.

fields.name: billing-start-date
fields.description: The day of the month when the cellular billing cycle begins. Used in conjunction with data-rate-limit to track monthly data usage. The data usage counter resets on this date each month.

fields.name: data-rate-limit
fields.description: The maximum monthly data usage limit for the cellular connection in megabits per second.

fields.name: frequency
fields.description:
Cellular frequency band configuration for the modem. Groups generation (3G/4G) and
frequency-range settings that together configure the cellular modem's frequency band.

fields.name: frequency-range
fields.description: The specific radio frequency band to use for cellular communication. Restricting to specific bands can optimize connectivity in regions where certain frequencies have better coverage or performance. Used in conjunction with generation parameter.

fields.name: generation
fields.description: The cellular technology generation (3G or 4G) used to filter available frequency bands. Used in conjunction with frequency-range to specify precise radio frequency bands for the modem.

fields.name: gps
fields.description: Enable the GPS on the Aruba modem, this API is AP specific and only for Aruba modem

fields.name: internal-lte
fields.description: Enable or disable internal LTE modem. When true, enables internal-lte. When false, disables internal-lte.

fields.name: modem-apn
fields.description:
Modem APN(Access Point Name) Configuration is used by modem to connect to a mobile network
for internet access, this configuration help the modem identify the correct network and establish a data connection.

fields.name: apn
fields.description: The Access Point Name (APN) provided by your mobile carrier to establish the data connection. The APN identifies the packet data network (PDN) that the modem should connect to. Valid only when using Aruba modems.

fields.name: apn-authentication
fields.description: The authentication protocol used to verify credentials with the mobile carrier. Valid only when APN password is configured. Supported values: 0 (No authentication), 1 (PAP - Password Authentication Protocol, sends credentials in clear text), 2 (CHAP - Challenge Handshake Authentication Protocol, uses hashed credentials), 3 (MSCHAPv2 - Microsoft CHAP version 2, enhanced security).

fields.name: apn-password
fields.description: APN password

fields.name: apn-username
fields.description: APN usernmae

fields.name: id
fields.description: APN-profile-id number.

fields.name: isp-name
fields.description: ISP Access point name.

fields.name: modem-e3372
fields.description: Enables the pre-configured profile optimized for Huawei E3372h-320 USB LTE modems. When enabled, the system applies modem-specific initialization and connection parameters. Gateway devices only.

fields.name: network-mode
fields.description: The preferred cellular network generation for connection. AUTO allows the modem to select the best available technology (3G/4G), while fixed modes (MODE_3G, MODE_4G) restrict connectivity to a specific generation. Forcing a specific mode can improve stability in areas with weak higher-generation signals. Valid only when using Aruba modems. Aruba modems support AUTO, MODE_3G, and MODE_4G.

fields.name: plmn
fields.description: The Public Land Mobile Network (PLMN) identifier used to manually select a specific mobile operator network. PLMN consists of Mobile Country Code (MCC) and Mobile Network Code (MNC). Valid only when using Aruba modems. Accepts 5-6 digits for AP, GW.

fields.name: prefer-modem
fields.description: The preferred modem, this API is AP specific and only for Aruba modem.

fields.name: sim-failover
fields.description: Enables automatic failover between SIM card slots when the active SIM loses connectivity. When enabled, the system will switch to the alternate SIM slot if the primary connection fails, ensuring continuous cellular uplink availability. Applicable to 9004-LTE only.

fields.name: sim-slot
fields.description: Selects the active SIM card slot (applicable for 9004-LTE only). Use SIM1 or SIM2 to specify which SIM card should be used for cellular connectivity.

fields.name: tp-cell-auth
fields.description:
Cellular authentication parameters,these parameters are important credentials used to verify user identity,
these parameters are typically provided by ISP to ensure that only authorized users can access the network.

fields.name: password
fields.description:
The password for the account associated with the subscriber of the selected Internet Service Provider,
this API is AP specific and only for 3rd party modem.

fields.name: type
fields.description:
The authentication type for modem, this API is AP specific and only for 3rd party modem.
Range: PAP, CHAP

fields.name: username
fields.description:
The username of subscriber of selected Internet Service Provider,
this API is AP specific and only for 3rd party modem.

fields.name: tp-country
fields.description: The country for the deployment, this API is AP specific and only for 3rd party modem.

fields.name: tp-device-id
fields.description: The device ID of the modem, this API is AP specific and only for 3rd party modem.

fields.name: tp-device-tty
fields.description: The modem TTY port, this API is AP specific and only for 3rd party modem.

fields.name: tp-dial-cmd
fields.description: The parameter to dial the cell tower, this API is AP specific and only for 3rd party modem.

fields.name: tp-driver-type
fields.description:
The device driver required for 3G or 4G modem, this API is AP specific and only for 3rd party modem.
Range: OPTION, ACM, AIRPRIME, HSO, SIERRA_EVDO, SIERRA_GSM, PANTECH_3G, ETHER_3G, SIERRA_NET,
RNDIS_U770, RNDIS_L800, HUAWEI_CDC, NOVATEL_U620, RNDIS_UML295, SIERRA_GOBI, ZTE_CDC, ARUBA_GOBI

fields.name: tp-init-parameters
fields.description: The parameter name to initialize the modem, this API is AP specific and only for 3rd party modem.

fields.name: tp-isp
fields.description:
The name of the Internet Service Provider to connect, this API is AP specific and only for 3rd party modem.
Range: CINCINNATI_BELL, VIRGIN, TELECOM, TELENOR, VODAFONE_SMARTONE, O2, SFR, ORANGE, HUTCH, OPTUS,
SINGTEL, HKCSL, VERIZON, RELIANCE, TATA_INDICOM, AIRTEL_3G, NOKIA_CS_10, NTT, KDDI, MOVISTAR, CHINA_TELECOM,
CHINA_UNICOM, VODAFONE, NETCOM, T_MOBILE, MOBILY, EMOBILE, SPRINT, CRICKET, VODAFONE_3G, AIRTEL, ATT,
BELL, DEUTSCH_TELEKOM, ICE, TELSTRA, CHINA_MOBILE

fields.name: tp-modeswitch-cmd
fields.description:
The parameter used to switch modem from storage mode to modem mode,
this API is AP specific and only for 3rd party modem.

fields.name: lte-modem.network-mode
fields.description: The preferred cellular network generation for connection. AUTO allows the modem to select the best available technology (3G/4G), while fixed modes (MODE_3G, MODE_4G) restrict connectivity to a specific generation. Forcing a specific mode can improve stability in areas with weak higher-generation signals. Valid only when using Aruba modems. Aruba modems support AUTO, MODE_3G, and MODE_4G.

the AP periodically tries to use a higher priority uplink, and switches to a higher priority uplink even if the current uplink is active.

fields.name: enable
fields.description:
Enables uplink switchover based on the availability of the Internet. When enabled, the
AP continuously sends ICMP packets to some well-known Internet servers. If the request
is timed out due to a bad uplink connection or uplink interface failure, and the public
Internet is not reachable from the current uplink, the AP switches to a different connection.

fields.description: Configures the Internet failover IP address for a cellular 3G/4G uplink.

fields.name: pkt-lost-cnt
fields.description:
Configures the number of packets that are to be lost when verifying the uplink availability
using the Internet.

fields.name: pkt-send-freq
fields.description:
Configures the frequency in seconds, at which the ICMP packets are sent to verify the
uplink availability using the Internet.

fields.name: timeout
fields.description: Configures the number of seconds after which the Internet based uplink verification times out.

fields.name: vpn-timeout
fields.description: Configures a duration to wait for an uplink switch based on VPN status.

fields.name: lte-modem
fields.description: Uplink LTE Modem, this feature is used to configure modem parameters for 3G or 4G uplink and only applies to AP, the 3G and 4G modems can be used to extend connectivity to places and enables the AP to automatically choose the available network in a specific region. This feature supports configuring both 3rd party modem and aruba modem, but only one modem can be used as the uplink.

fields.name: backup-link
fields.description: Mark uplink as a hot-standby uplink.

fields.name: aruba-skylark
fields.description: Enables the pre-configured profile for Aruba Skylark LTE modems. When enabled, this creates and activates the ARUBA_USB_LTE profile optimized for Skylark hardware and disables configurations for other modem types. Gateway devices only.

fields.name: auto-upgrade
fields.description: Automatic firmware upgrade for Aruba modem, this API is AP specific and only for Aruba modem.

fields.name: billing-start-date
fields.description: The day of the month when the cellular billing cycle begins. Used in conjunction with data-rate-limit to track monthly data usage. The data usage counter resets on this date each month.

fields.name: data-rate-limit
fields.description: The maximum monthly data usage limit for the cellular connection in megabits per second.

fields.name: frequency
fields.description:
Cellular frequency band configuration for the modem. Groups generation (3G/4G) and
frequency-range settings that together configure the cellular modem's frequency band.

fields.name: frequency-range
fields.description: The specific radio frequency band to use for cellular communication. Restricting to specific bands can optimize connectivity in regions where certain frequencies have better coverage or performance. Used in conjunction with generation parameter.

fields.name: generation
fields.description: The cellular technology generation (3G or 4G) used to filter available frequency bands. Used in conjunction with frequency-range to specify precise radio frequency bands for the modem.

fields.name: gps
fields.description: Enable the GPS on the Aruba modem, this API is AP specific and only for Aruba modem

fields.name: internal-lte
fields.description: Enable or disable internal LTE modem. When true, enables internal-lte. When false, disables internal-lte.

fields.name: modem-apn
fields.description:
Modem APN(Access Point Name) Configuration is used by modem to connect to a mobile network
for internet access, this configuration help the modem identify the correct network and establish a data connection.

fields.name: apn
fields.description: The Access Point Name (APN) provided by your mobile carrier to establish the data connection. The APN identifies the packet data network (PDN) that the modem should connect to. Valid only when using Aruba modems.

fields.name: apn-authentication
fields.description: The authentication protocol used to verify credentials with the mobile carrier. Valid only when APN password is configured. Supported values: 0 (No authentication), 1 (PAP - Password Authentication Protocol, sends credentials in clear text), 2 (CHAP - Challenge Handshake Authentication Protocol, uses hashed credentials), 3 (MSCHAPv2 - Microsoft CHAP version 2, enhanced security).

fields.name: apn-password
fields.description: APN password

fields.name: apn-username
fields.description: APN usernmae

fields.name: id
fields.description: APN-profile-id number.

fields.name: isp-name
fields.description: ISP Access point name.

fields.name: modem-e3372
fields.description: Enables the pre-configured profile optimized for Huawei E3372h-320 USB LTE modems. When enabled, the system applies modem-specific initialization and connection parameters. Gateway devices only.

fields.name: network-mode
fields.description: The preferred cellular network generation for connection. AUTO allows the modem to select the best available technology (3G/4G), while fixed modes (MODE_3G, MODE_4G) restrict connectivity to a specific generation. Forcing a specific mode can improve stability in areas with weak higher-generation signals. Valid only when using Aruba modems. Aruba modems support AUTO, MODE_3G, and MODE_4G.

fields.name: plmn
fields.description: The Public Land Mobile Network (PLMN) identifier used to manually select a specific mobile operator network. PLMN consists of Mobile Country Code (MCC) and Mobile Network Code (MNC). Valid only when using Aruba modems. Accepts 5-6 digits for AP, GW.

fields.name: prefer-modem
fields.description: The preferred modem, this API is AP specific and only for Aruba modem.

fields.name: sim-failover
fields.description: Enables automatic failover between SIM card slots when the active SIM loses connectivity. When enabled, the system will switch to the alternate SIM slot if the primary connection fails, ensuring continuous cellular uplink availability. Applicable to 9004-LTE only.

fields.name: sim-slot
fields.description: Selects the active SIM card slot (applicable for 9004-LTE only). Use SIM1 or SIM2 to specify which SIM card should be used for cellular connectivity.

fields.name: poe
fields.description: Power-over-ethernet(PoE) configurations. The power-over-ethernet (PoE) manages the power supplied to devices using standard Ethernet data cables.

fields.name: allocation-method
fields.description:
Power allocation method. By default, power allocation is automatic based on device usage.
Allowed configurable values are 'usage' or 'class' or 'value'

fields.name: assigned-class
fields.description:
Limit PoE power based on the assigned class.
Class 3 (13W max at powered device (PD))
Class 4 (25.5W max at powered device (PD))
Class 6 (51W max at  powered device (PD))
Class 8 (71.3W max at  powered device (PD))

fields.name: cycle-timeout
fields.description: Timeout value in units of seconds to control POE power delivery.

fields.name: enabled
fields.description:
Enable/Disable power-over-ethernet on the interface.
PoE on each port can be Enabled/Disabled individually.

fields.name: lldp-detect
fields.description:
Allow the link partner to specify power allocation using LLDP.
By default, LLDP power information is ignored.

fields.name: pd-class-override
fields.description:
The pd-class-override enables a device to draw power more than the
the power limit specified in IEEE classification.
By default,it is disabled. Power allocation method should be set
to 'class' when override needs to be enabled.

fields.name: poe-cisco
fields.description: Enable or disable PoE Cisco in the ethernet interface.

fields.name: power-pairs
fields.description:
Configure what cable pairs deliver power.
A 2-Pair power sourcing equipment (PSE) will source power on just one pairset, Alt-A or Alt-B.
A 4-Pair power sourcing equipment (PSE) will source power on both pairsets Alt-A and Alt-B

fields.name: pre-std-detect
fields.description:
Enable detection of pre-standard PoE devices. When 'pre-std-detect' is enabled,
power will be delivered on 'alt-a' pair only. By default 'pre-std-detect' is disabled.

fields.name: priority
fields.description:
Configure PoE priority in the event of power over-subscription.
Configurable values for priority on the interface are low, critical or high. Default priority is low

fields.name: value
fields.description:
Set the maximum power allocation for the port.
Applicable only when 'poe-allocate-by' is set to 'value'.

fields.description: Power allocation method. By default, power allocation is automatic based on device usage. Allowed configurable values are 'usage' or 'class' or 'value'

fields.name: interface-mode
fields.description:
Interface access or trunk mode for VLANs.
The access-vlan should be set to null for configuring trunk mode and
native-vlan, trunk-vlan-ranges and trunk-vlan-all should be set to null while configuring access mode
Eg: switchport: {interface-mode: ACCESS, access-vlan: 600, native-vlan: null,
trunk-vlan-all: null, trunk-vlan-ranges: null}
switchport: {interface-mode: TRUNK, access-vlan: null, native-vlan: NATIVE_VLAN,
trunk-vlan-all: false, trunk-vlan-ranges: [ 1000 ]}

fields.description:
A port with a VLAN translation configuration allows traffic only for the translated VLAN and the native VLAN;
if it is a member of more VLANS, it does not allow traffic for them.
A translated VLAN must be present on the switch before the rule is created; the original VLAN need not be present.
VLAN translation and MVRP cannot be enabled on the same interface.

fields.description: QoS interface parameters for the physical interface or port channel.

fields.name: burst
fields.description:
The burst size in units of kilobytes for the maximum egress traffic rate.
Valid when egress-rate is specified.

fields.name: cos
fields.description:
COS remark value for all packets arriving on the port. The new value
will be reflected in the outgoing VLAN tag.

AOSCX: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon transmit. The active
port trust mode must be 'None' before any cos remark value can be
configured. If cos remark is applied with any other trust config on
the port, then the config will be rejected by the device. In order
to fix this, either remove the cos remark config or change the trust
config on the port to NONE.
PVOS: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon arriving, which will
affect queueing.

fields.name: dscp
fields.description:
The DSCP remark for the port. The new value will be reflected in any
outgoing IP packet headers.

AOSCX: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon transmit. The active
port trust mode must be 'None' before any dscp remark value can be
configured. If dscp remark is applied with any other trust config on
the port, then the config will be rejected by the device. In order
to fix this, either remove the dscp remark config or change the trust
config on the port to NONE.
PVOS: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon arrival, which will
affect queueing.

fields.description:
Enable transmission of flood traffic (broadcast, multicast and
unknown unicast) out authentication enabled interfaces with no
authenticated client.

fields.name: auth-mode
fields.description:
The mode determining how each client on the interface can gain access
to the network.

fields.description: BPDUs that can trigger authentication.

fields.name: cdp
fields.description: Enable CDP packets to trigger authentication.

fields.name: lldp
fields.description: Enable LLDP packets to trigger authentication.

fields.description:
MAC address to use when authentication is triggered by an
LLDP frame. This is applicable only when LLDP packets are
allowed to trigger authentication.

fields.name: bpdu-bypass
fields.description:
BPDUs to be serviced by the device before authentication is
successful on the interface.

fields.name: cdp
fields.description:
Enable CDP packets to be serviced by the device before
authentication is successful on the interface.

fields.name: lldp
fields.description:
Enable LLDP packets to be serviced by the device before
authentication is successful on the interface.

fields.name: bpdu-proxy-logoff
fields.description:
Proxy logoff the client based on the interface status in BPDU packets.
Device will clear authentication session of the client if it receives
an interface down status in the BPDU packet.
When not configured, no action is taken.

fields.name: cdp
fields.description: Enable CDP based proxy-logoff.

fields.name: client-limit
fields.description: Maximum number of clients that can be authenticated on the interface.

fields.name: device-profile-secure
fields.description: Enable device-profile with security.

fields.name: auth-precedence
fields.description:
Precedence order for port-access authentication. Auth-precedence must
contain either 0 or 2 elements. If empty, the default precedence
order of dot1x followed by mac-auth will be used.

fields.name: auth-priority
fields.description:
Priority order for port-access authentication. Auth-priority must
contain either 0 or 2 elements. If not set, priority will follow
the 'auth-precedence' order.

fields.name: client-auto-logoff-enable
fields.description:
The list of reasons when a client can be automatically logged off by
the device.

fields.name: client-move
fields.description: The client move configuration.

fields.name: cloud-auth
fields.description: Enable cloud authentication.

fields.name: concurrent-onboarding
fields.description:
Enable authentication methods to start concurrently for faster
onboarding. If not set, clients are onboarded based on the order
specified by 'onboarding-precedence'.

fields.name: controlled-direction
fields.description:
Configure how traffic is controlled on non-authenticated ports: in both directions (ingress and egress) or ingress only.
Default is BOTH.

fields.name: dot1xauth-server-group
fields.description: 802.1X authentication server group.

fields.name: macauth-server-group
fields.description: MAC authentication server group

fields.name: mda-data-clients-limit
fields.description:
Maximum number of 'data' clients that can be authenticated on the
interface when multi-domain is enabled. If the number of 'data' clients
on the interface exceeds this client limit, it will be considered as a
violation and the configured threshold-violation action is taken.

fields.name: onboarding-precedence
fields.description:
Precedence order when onboarding a client. Onboarding-precedence must
contain either 0 or 2 elements. If empty, the default precedence order
of AAA followed by device-profile will be used.

fields.description:

on the other end before considering the link to be non 802.1X capable
and opening the interface on the data-plane.
On a timeout, the device will not use the authentication result to
determine the forwarding behavior of the interface until a link flap.
If not configured, the device will wait for the 802.1X authentication
cycle to complete before determining the forwarding state of the
interface.

authenticated without a role assigned from the RADIUS server.

fields.description:
Enable automatic creation of a VLAN for authenticated clients if the
VLAN is not already available on the device.

fields.description:
Enables caching authenticated clients and their associated
role information on the interface. Clients are assigned to their
previously authenticated role.

fields.name: critical-auth-role
fields.description:
The role to be applied for clients, that failed authentication
due to unreachable authentication servers.
When not set, no role is applied for clients that could not
complete authentication due to RADIUS server being unreachable.

fields.name: critical-data-vlan
fields.description: Configure critical-auth VLAN as data VLAN.

fields.name: critical-voice-role
fields.description:
The role to be applied to 'voice' client that have failed
re-authentication due to servers being unreachable.
When not set, no role will be applied for voice clients when they
fail re-authentication due to server being unreachable.

fields.name: default-vlan-type
fields.description: Type of default vlan.

fields.name: fallback-role
fields.description:

assigned a role via any of the onboarding methods.
When not set, no role is applied for the client.

fields.name: open-data-vlan
fields.description: Configure open-auth VLAN as data VLAN.

fields.name: open-voice-vlan
fields.description: Configure open-auth VLAN as voice VLAN.

fields.name: pre-auth-role
fields.description:
The role to be applied for clients that are yet to be authenticated.
When not set, no role is applied for clients while the
authentication is in progress for the client.

fields.name: radius-override-enable
fields.description:
Enable RADIUS override support. When enabled, RADIUS attributes
received from the server will override corresponding attributes
configured in the role assigned to the client.

fields.name: reject-role
fields.description:
The role to be applied for clients that failed authentication.
When not set, for AOS-CX devices, no role is applied for clients that fail authentication.
A default denyall role is applied on AOS-S devices.

fields.name: ubt-fallback-role
fields.description:
For any client,for which the corresponding UBT zone reachability
is failed, ubt-fallback role is applied. The client on ubt-fallback
role is automatically reverted to the previous role whenever UBT zone
status is back to reachable state.

Enable Opportunistic Key Caching (WPA2/WPA3 Only).By default, the 802.1X authentication profile enables a
cached pairwise master key (PMK) derived via a client and
an associated AP and used when the client roams to a new AP.
This allows clients faster roaming without a full 802.1x authentication.

fields.name: validate-pmkid
fields.description:
PMK (Pairwise Master Key) identifier (WPA2/WPA3 Only).
This parameter instructs the controller to check the pairwise master key (PMK) ID
sent by the client. When this option is enabled,
the client must send a PMKID in the associate or reassociate frame to indicate that it supports OKC or PMK caching;
otherwise, full 802.1x authentication takes place.

fields.name: discovery-timeout
fields.description:
Time period (in seconds) to wait for a potential 802.1X authenticator
on the other end before considering the link to be non 802.1X capable
and opening the interface on the data-plane.
On a timeout, the device will not use the authentication result to
determine the forwarding behavior of the interface until a link flap.
If not configured, the device will wait for the 802.1X authentication
cycle to complete before determining the forwarding state of the
interface.

fields.description:

determine the forwarding behavior of the interface until a link flap.

cycle to complete before determining the forwarding state of the
interface.

fields.name: auth-role
fields.description:
The role to be applied for clients that have been authenticated
but not received any specific role or attribute from the authentication
server.
When not set, no role is applied for clients that successfully
authenticated without a role assigned from the RADIUS server.

fields.name: auto-vlan-enable
fields.description:
Enable automatic creation of a VLAN for authenticated clients if the
VLAN is not already available on the device.

fields.name: cached-critical-role-enable
fields.description:
Enables caching authenticated clients and their associated
role information on the interface. Clients are assigned to their
previously authenticated role.

fields.name: critical-auth-role
fields.description:
The role to be applied for clients, that failed authentication
due to unreachable authentication servers.
When not set, no role is applied for clients that could not
complete authentication due to RADIUS server being unreachable.

fields.name: critical-data-vlan
fields.description: Configure critical-auth VLAN as data VLAN.

fields.name: critical-voice-role
fields.description:
The role to be applied to 'voice' client that have failed
re-authentication due to servers being unreachable.
When not set, no role will be applied for voice clients when they
fail re-authentication due to server being unreachable.

fields.name: critical-voice-vlan
fields.description: Configure critical-auth VLAN as voice VLAN.

fields.name: default-vlan-type
fields.description: Type of default vlan.

fields.name: fallback-role
fields.description:
The role that will be applied to clients that have not been
assigned a role via any of the onboarding methods.
When not set, no role is applied for the client.

fields.name: open-data-vlan
fields.description: Configure open-auth VLAN as data VLAN.

fields.name: open-voice-vlan
fields.description: Configure open-auth VLAN as voice VLAN.

fields.name: pre-auth-role
fields.description:
The role to be applied for clients that are yet to be authenticated.
When not set, no role is applied for clients while the
authentication is in progress for the client.

fields.name: radius-override-enable
fields.description:
Enable RADIUS override support. When enabled, RADIUS attributes
received from the server will override corresponding attributes
configured in the role assigned to the client.

fields.name: reject-role
fields.description:
The role to be applied for clients that failed authentication.
When not set, for AOS-CX devices, no role is applied for clients that fail authentication.
A default denyall role is applied on AOS-S devices.

fields.name: ubt-fallback-role
fields.description:
For any client,for which the corresponding UBT zone reachability
is failed, ubt-fallback role is applied. The client on ubt-fallback
role is automatically reverted to the previous role whenever UBT zone
status is back to reachable state.

fields.name: aaa.authorization.auth-role
fields.description: The role to be applied for clients that have been authenticated but not received any specific role or attribute from the authentication server. When not set, no role is applied for clients that successfully authenticated without a role assigned from the RADIUS server.

fields.name: aaa.authorization.auto-vlan-enable
fields.description: Enable automatic creation of a VLAN for authenticated clients if the VLAN is not already available on the device.

fields.name: aaa.authorization.cached-critical-role-enable
fields.description: Enables caching authenticated clients and their associated role information on the interface. Clients are assigned to their previously authenticated role.

fields.name: aaa.authorization.critical-auth-role
fields.description: The role to be applied for clients, that failed authentication due to unreachable authentication servers. When not set, no role is applied for clients that could not complete authentication due to RADIUS server being unreachable.

fields.name: aaa.authorization.critical-data-vlan

fields.name: duplex
fields.description: Configures the duplex mode for the Ethernet interface. Full-duplex allows simultaneous bidirectional communication for maximum throughput. Half-duplex only permits one direction at a time and is rarely used in modern networks. Auto-negotiation (default) automatically selects the best duplex mode supported by both devices. Manual settings must match on both ends of the link to avoid connectivity issues.

Gateway profiles provide template-based configuration for firewall rules, AAA settings, and other gateway-specific features. When assigned, profile settings override local interface configurations unless the retain-profile-configs option is enabled.

fields.name: jumbo-mtu
fields.description: Enables support for Jumbo frames (Ethernet frames larger than the standard 1500-byte MTU, typically up to 9000 bytes). Jumbo frames improve network throughput and reduce CPU overhead for large data transfers such as storage traffic, backups, and virtualization workloads. All devices in the network path must support Jumbo frames to prevent fragmentation. Corresponds to the jumbo command on gateway devices.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Unique identifier for the Ethernet or USB interface. Supported formats include slot-based naming (e.g., 0/0/1 for slot 0, module 0, port 1) and logical naming (e.g., enet0, usb0). Device models enforce specific port ranges through capability constraints (e.g., gateway model GW_7005 supports 0/0/[0-3], GW_7205 supports 0/0/[0-5]). This field is mandatory and serves as the primary key for the interface instance.

fields.name: port-monitor
fields.description: Configures this interface as a monitoring port that receives mirrored traffic from another source interface (SPAN/port mirroring). The source can be a physical GigabitEthernet interface or a Port-Channel/LAG. All traffic from the source interface is duplicated and sent to this monitoring port for analysis, troubleshooting, or security monitoring purposes. Gateway devices only.

fields.name: enable
fields.description: Enables or disables port monitoring (SPAN/traffic mirroring) on this interface. When enabled, this interface receives a copy of all traffic from the specified source interface for analysis. Operational constraints: Only one monitoring session can be active on the device at a time. LLDP must be disabled on the monitoring port (enforced by system). Neither the monitoring port nor the monitored source port can be part of a Link Aggregation Control Protocol (LACP) group or port-channel. The source interface must be different from the monitoring interface. Use this for network troubleshooting, traffic analysis, or security monitoring.

fields.name: src-interface-id
fields.description: Identifies the source interface to be monitored. For physical ports, use slot/module/port format (e.g., 0/0/1). For port-channels, use the LAG number (e.g., 5). This must be different from the monitoring interface identifier to prevent loops. The system enforces that source and destination interfaces cannot be the same.

fields.name: src-interface-type
fields.description: Specifies the type of source interface whose traffic will be mirrored to this monitoring port. GIGABIT_ETHERNET mirrors traffic from a single physical Ethernet port. PORT_CHANNEL mirrors aggregated traffic from all member ports in a Link Aggregation Group (LAG).

fields.name: port-monitor.enable
fields.description: Enables or disables port monitoring (SPAN/traffic mirroring) on this interface. When enabled, this interface receives a copy of all traffic from the specified source interface for analysis. Operational constraints: Only one monitoring session can be active on the device at a time. LLDP must be disabled on the monitoring port (enforced by system). Neither the monitoring port nor the monitored source port can be part of a Link Aggregation Control Protocol (LACP) group or port-channel. The source interface must be different from the monitoring interface. Use this for network troubleshooting, traffic analysis, or security monitoring.

fields.name: port-monitor.src-interface-id
fields.description: Identifies the source interface to be monitored. For physical ports, use slot/module/port format (e.g., 0/0/1). For port-channels, use the LAG number (e.g., 5). This must be different from the monitoring interface identifier to prevent loops. The system enforces that source and destination interfaces cannot be the same.

fields.name: port-monitor.src-interface-type
fields.description: Specifies the type of source interface whose traffic will be mirrored to this monitoring port. GIGABIT_ETHERNET mirrors traffic from a single physical Ethernet port. PORT_CHANNEL mirrors aggregated traffic from all member ports in a Link Aggregation Group (LAG).

fields.name: port-type
fields.description: Designates the interface as either a WAN (Wide Area Network) or LAN (Local Area Network) port. WAN ports typically connect to external networks or service providers and may apply different security policies, NAT rules, and routing behaviors. LAN ports connect to internal trusted networks. This designation affects firewall rules, routing decisions, and security policy enforcement.

fields.name: portchannel-lag
fields.description: Attach a link aggreagatioin group (LAG) to physical interface.

fields.name: retain-profile-configs
fields.description: To decide whether or not to retain profile configs on an interface when the profile is removed from the said interface

fields.name: speed
fields.description: Configures the link speed for the Ethernet interface. When set to SPEED_AUTO (default), the interface automatically negotiates the highest supported speed with the connected device. Manual speed settings force the interface to operate at a specific rate, which may require matching configuration on the peer device.

fields.name: speed-mode
fields.description: Configures the operational speed mode for multi-rate capable interfaces. Only supported on 7280 hardware. Determines whether the interface operates in 40Gbps, 10Gbps, or 1Gbps mode. Changing this setting may affect port availability or require a reboot. Consult hardware documentation for supported speed modes per interface.

fields.name: sw-profile
fields.description: Switch Port Profile (if any) associated with the interface.

fields.name: trusted
fields.description: Marks the interface as trusted for security policy purposes. Trusted interfaces bypass certain security checks and firewall rules, allowing unrestricted communication. Typically applied to internal management interfaces or connections to known secure networks. Use with caution as this reduces security enforcement on the interface.

fields.name: tunneled-node-port
fields.description: Enables tunneled node functionality on the interface, allowing it to participate in overlay network tunneling. When enabled, traffic received on this port can be automatically encapsulated and forwarded through SD-WAN or VPN tunnels based on routing policies. Typically used for branch office deployments where local devices need transparent access to central resources over secure tunnels.

fields.name: poe
fields.description: Power-over-ethernet(PoE) configurations. The power-over-ethernet (PoE) manages the power supplied to devices using standard Ethernet data cables.

fields.name: allocation-method
fields.description:
Power allocation method. By default, power allocation is automatic based on device usage.
Allowed configurable values are 'usage' or 'class' or 'value'

fields.name: assigned-class
fields.description:
Limit PoE power based on the assigned class.
Class 3 (13W max at powered device (PD))
Class 4 (25.5W max at powered device (PD))
Class 6 (51W max at  powered device (PD))
Class 8 (71.3W max at  powered device (PD))

fields.name: cycle-timeout
fields.description: Timeout value in units of seconds to control POE power delivery.

fields.name: enabled
fields.description:
Enable/Disable power-over-ethernet on the interface.
PoE on each port can be Enabled/Disabled individually.

fields.name: lldp-detect
fields.description:
Allow the link partner to specify power allocation using LLDP.
By default, LLDP power information is ignored.

fields.name: pd-class-override
fields.description:
The pd-class-override enables a device to draw power more than the
the power limit specified in IEEE classification.
By default,it is disabled. Power allocation method should be set
to 'class' when override needs to be enabled.

fields.name: poe-cisco
fields.description: Enable or disable PoE Cisco in the ethernet interface.

fields.name: power-pairs
fields.description:
Configure what cable pairs deliver power.
A 2-Pair power sourcing equipment (PSE) will source power on just one pairset, Alt-A or Alt-B.
A 4-Pair power sourcing equipment (PSE) will source power on both pairsets Alt-A and Alt-B

fields.name: pre-std-detect
fields.description:
Enable detection of pre-standard PoE devices. When 'pre-std-detect' is enabled,
power will be delivered on 'alt-a' pair only. By default 'pre-std-detect' is disabled.

fields.name: priority
fields.description:
Configure PoE priority in the event of power over-subscription.
Configurable values for priority on the interface are low, critical or high. Default priority is low

fields.name: value
fields.description:
Set the maximum power allocation for the port.
Applicable only when 'poe-allocate-by' is set to 'value'.

fields.name: cable-length
fields.description: Specifies the cable-length auto-detection mode or the value  in meters used to compute the headroom limit for lossless traffic  arriving on the interface. The default value is 350 meters.

fields.name: flow-control-mode
fields.description: Flow-control mode for the interface: Link Level Flow Control (LLFC), Priority Flow Control (PFC), or none. On some platforms, memory pools must first be configured (using the aruba-qos-pool yang model) before any interface flow-control configuration will take effect.

fields.name: llfc-flow-control
fields.description: Configuration for 802.3x link-level flow control (LLFC). On some platforms, a memory pool must first be created (using the aruba-qos-pool yang model) that matches the llfc-pool-id value before any 802.3X link-level Tx or RxTx flow-control configuration will take effect.

fields.name: direction
fields.description:
This mandatory field specifies whether the interface is enabled to
handle received flow-control frames, to transmit flow-control frames,
or both. This setting only applies to 802.3X link-level flow control.

fields.name: llfc-pool-id
fields.description:
The pool ID for arriving lossless LLFC packets. On some platforms, a
memory pool with the same pool ID value must first be configured
(using the aruba-qos-pool yang model) before any 802.3X link-level Tx
or RxTx flow-control configuration will take effect.

fields.name: override-negotiation
fields.description:
Enables overriding link-negotiation results and using
the locally-specified flow-control mode instead.

fields.name: llfc-flow-control.direction
fields.description: This mandatory field specifies whether the interface is enabled to handle received flow-control frames, to transmit flow-control frames, or both. This setting only applies to 802.3X link-level flow control.

fields.name: llfc-flow-control.llfc-pool-id
fields.description: The pool ID for arriving lossless LLFC packets. On some platforms, a memory pool with the same pool ID value must first be configured (using the aruba-qos-pool yang model) before any 802.3X link-level Tx or RxTx flow-control configuration will take effect.

fields.name: llfc-flow-control.override-negotiation
fields.description: Enables overriding link-negotiation results and using the locally-specified flow-control mode instead.

fields.name: lossless-buffer-based-link-level-flow-control
fields.description: Buffer threshold configuration for 802.3x link-level flow control, including XOF and XON limits, headroom, and other parameters.

fields.name: headroom
fields.description:
The maximum amount of headroom-buffer memory allowed to
 be consumed by in-flight traffic after the traffic has been PAUSED.

fields.name: xoff-dynamic-threshold-alpha
fields.description: The alpha value used in computing the limit when the XOFF limit-type is dynamic.

fields.name: xoff-static-threshold
fields.description: The fixed buffer-limit in kilobytes when the XOFF limit-type is static.

fields.name: xon-delta
fields.description:
The buffer utilization decrease-amount below the XOFF limit
 that will trigger a RESUME of traffic when it is PAUSED.

fields.name: lossless-buffer-based-link-level-flow-control.headroom

fields.name: lossless-buffer-based-link-level-flow-control.xon-delta

fields.name: lossless-buffer-based-priority-flow-control

fields.name: pfc-watchdog

fields.name: priority-flow-control

fields.name: interface-mode

Interface access or trunk mode for VLANs.
The access-vlan should be set to null for configuring trunk mode and
native-vlan, trunk-vlan-ranges and trunk-vlan-all should be set to null while configuring access mode
Eg: switchport: {interface-mode: ACCESS, access-vlan: 600, native-vlan: null,
trunk-vlan-all: null, trunk-vlan-ranges: null}
switchport: {interface-mode: TRUNK, access-vlan: null, native-vlan: NATIVE_VLAN,
trunk-vlan-all: false, trunk-vlan-ranges: [ 1000 ]}

fields.description:
The burst size in units of kilobytes for the maximum egress traffic rate.
Valid when egress-rate is specified.

fields.name: cos
fields.description:
COS remark value for all packets arriving on the port. The new value
will be reflected in the outgoing VLAN tag.

AOSCX: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon transmit. The active
port trust mode must be 'None' before any cos remark value can be
configured. If cos remark is applied with any other trust config on
the port, then the config will be rejected by the device. In order
to fix this, either remove the cos remark config or change the trust
config on the port to NONE.
PVOS: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon arriving, which will
affect queueing.

fields.name: dscp
fields.description:
The DSCP remark for the port. The new value will be reflected in any
outgoing IP packet headers.

AOSCX: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon transmit. The active
port trust mode must be 'None' before any dscp remark value can be
configured. If dscp remark is applied with any other trust config on
the port, then the config will be rejected by the device. In order
to fix this, either remove the dscp remark config or change the trust
config on the port to NONE.
PVOS: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon arrival, which will
affect queueing.

For AOSCX devices, when no trust mode is applied on the port,
the trust mode configured in the aruba-qos-global profile takes precedence.
If no trust mode is configured in the aruba-qos-global profile,
trust NONE is used.

If dscp remark is applied with any other trust config on the port, then the config will be rejected by the device. In order to fix this, either remove the dscp remark config or change the trust config on the port to NONE. PVOS: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon arrival, which will affect queueing.

fields.name: canned-eap-success-enable
fields.description:
Allow the device to send a canned EAP success packet to the supplicant
to indicate a successful authentication when:
1. The authentication fails due to a RADIUS server reject, but
the interface on which the client on-boarded has a reject-role
configured.
2. The authentication fails due to a RADIUS server timeout, but
the interface on which the client on-boarded has a critical-role
configured.

fields.name: validate-pmkid
fields.description:
PMK (Pairwise Master Key) identifier (WPA2/WPA3 Only).
This parameter instructs the controller to check the pairwise master key (PMK) ID
sent by the client. When this option is enabled,
the client must send a PMKID in the associate or reassociate frame to indicate that it supports OKC or PMK caching;
otherwise, full 802.1x authentication takes place.

fields.name: discovery-timeout
fields.description:
Time period (in seconds) to wait for a potential 802.1X authenticator
on the other end before considering the link to be non 802.1X capable
and opening the interface on the data-plane.
On a timeout, the device will not use the authentication result to
determine the forwarding behavior of the interface until a link flap.
If not configured, the device will wait for the 802.1X authentication
cycle to complete before determining the forwarding state of the
interface.

fields.name: auth-role
fields.description:
The role to be applied for clients that have been authenticated
but not received any specific role or attribute from the authentication
server.
When not set, no role is applied for clients that successfully
authenticated without a role assigned from the RADIUS server.

fields.name: auto-vlan-enable
fields.description:
Enable automatic creation of a VLAN for authenticated clients if the
VLAN is not already available on the device.

fields.name: cached-critical-role-enable
fields.description:
Enables caching authenticated clients and their associated
role information on the interface. Clients are assigned to their
previously authenticated role.

fields.name: critical-auth-role
fields.description:
The role to be applied for clients, that failed authentication
due to unreachable authentication servers.
When not set, no role is applied for clients that could not
complete authentication due to RADIUS server being unreachable.

fields.name: critical-data-vlan
fields.description: Configure critical-auth VLAN as data VLAN.

fields.name: critical-voice-role
fields.description:
The role to be applied to 'voice' client that have failed
re-authentication due to servers being unreachable.
When not set, no role will be applied for voice clients when they
fail re-authentication due to server being unreachable.

fields.name: critical-voice-vlan
fields.description: Configure critical-auth VLAN as voice VLAN.

fields.name: default-vlan-type
fields.description: Type of default vlan.

fields.name: fallback-role
fields.description:
The role that will be applied to clients that have not been
assigned a role via any of the onboarding methods.
When not set, no role is applied for the client.

fields.name: open-data-vlan
fields.description: Configure open-auth VLAN as data VLAN.

fields.name: open-voice-vlan
fields.description: Configure open-auth VLAN as voice VLAN.

fields.name: pre-auth-role
fields.description:
The role to be applied for clients that are yet to be authenticated.
When not set, no role is applied for clients while the
authentication is in progress for the client.

fields.name: radius-override-enable
fields.description:
Enable RADIUS override support. When enabled, RADIUS attributes
received from the server will override corresponding attributes
configured in the role assigned to the client.

fields.name: reject-role
fields.description:
The role to be applied for clients that failed authentication.
When not set, for AOS-CX devices, no role is applied for clients that fail authentication.
A default denyall role is applied on AOS-S devices.

fields.name: ubt-fallback-role
fields.description:
For any client,for which the corresponding UBT zone reachability
is failed, ubt-fallback role is applied. The client on ubt-fallback
role is automatically reverted to the previous role whenever UBT zone
status is back to reachable state.

fields.name: alternate-linkup
fields.description: Enables Direct Attach Copper (DAC) alternate link detection mechanism for improved cable compatibility. This feature helps resolve link-up issues with certain DAC cables by using an alternative link establishment method. Useful for troubleshooting connectivity problems with passive copper cables. Corresponds to the dac-alternate-linkup command on gateway devices.

fields.name: description
fields.description: Description of the interface. AOS-CX: length: 1-64

fields.name: duplex
fields.description: Configures the duplex mode for the Ethernet interface. Full-duplex allows simultaneous bidirectional communication for maximum throughput. Half-duplex only permits one direction at a time and is rarely used in modern networks. Auto-negotiation (default) automatically selects the best duplex mode supported by both devices. Manual settings must match on both ends of the link to avoid connectivity issues.

fields.name: forbid-vlans
fields.description: Forbid vlans for interface.

items.description: Forbid vlans for interface.

fields.name: gw-profile
fields.description: References an existing Gateway Port Profile to apply centrally managed port policies to this interface. Gateway profiles provide template-based configuration for firewall rules, AAA settings, and other gateway-specific features. When assigned, profile settings override local interface configurations unless the retain-profile-configs option is enabled.

fields.name: isolated-vlans
fields.description: Isolated VLAN ID for the interface.

items.description: Isolated VLAN ID for the interface.

fields.name: jumbo-mtu
fields.description: Enables support for Jumbo frames (Ethernet frames larger than the standard 1500-byte MTU, typically up to 9000 bytes). Jumbo frames improve network throughput and reduce CPU overhead for large data transfers such as storage traffic, backups, and virtualization workloads. All devices in the network path must support Jumbo frames to prevent fragmentation. Corresponds to the jumbo command on gateway devices.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Unique identifier for the Ethernet or USB interface. Supported formats include slot-based naming (e.g., 0/0/1 for slot 0, module 0, port 1) and logical naming (e.g., enet0, usb0). Device models enforce specific port ranges through capability constraints (e.g., gateway model GW_7005 supports 0/0/[0-3], GW_7205 supports 0/0/[0-5]). This field is mandatory and serves as the primary key for the interface instance.

fields.name: port-monitor
fields.description: Configures this interface as a monitoring port that receives mirrored traffic from another source interface (SPAN/port mirroring). The source can be a physical GigabitEthernet interface or a Port-Channel/LAG. All traffic from the source interface is duplicated and sent to this monitoring port for analysis, troubleshooting, or security monitoring purposes. Gateway devices only.

fields.name: enable
fields.description: Enables or disables port monitoring (SPAN/traffic mirroring) on this interface. When enabled, this interface receives a copy of all traffic from the specified source interface for analysis. Operational constraints: Only one monitoring session can be active on the device at a time. LLDP must be disabled on the monitoring port (enforced by system). Neither the monitoring port nor the monitored source port can be part of a Link Aggregation Control Protocol (LACP) group or port-channel. The source interface must be different from the monitoring interface. Use this for network troubleshooting, traffic analysis, or security monitoring.

fields.name: src-interface-id
fields.description: Identifies the source interface to be monitored. For physical ports, use slot/module/port format (e.g., 0/0/1). For port-channels, use the LAG number (e.g., 5). This must be different from the monitoring interface identifier to prevent loops. The system enforces that source and destination interfaces cannot be the same.

fields.name: src-interface-type
fields.description: Specifies the type of source interface whose traffic will be mirrored to this monitoring port. GIGABIT_ETHERNET mirrors traffic from a single physical Ethernet port. PORT_CHANNEL mirrors aggregated traffic from all member ports in a Link Aggregation Group (LAG).

fields.name: port-monitor.enable
fields.description: Enables or disables port monitoring (SPAN/traffic mirroring) on this interface. When enabled, this interface receives a copy of all traffic from the specified source interface for analysis. Operational constraints: Only one monitoring session can be active on the device at a time. LLDP must be disabled on the monitoring port (enforced by system). Neither the monitoring port nor the monitored source port can be part of a Link Aggregation Control Protocol (LACP) group or port-channel. The source interface must be different from the monitoring interface. Use this for network troubleshooting, traffic analysis, or security monitoring.

fields.name: port-monitor.src-interface-id
fields.description: Identifies the source interface to be monitored. For physical ports, use slot/module/port format (e.g., 0/0/1). For port-channels, use the LAG number (e.g., 5). This must be different from the monitoring interface identifier to prevent loops. The system enforces that source and destination interfaces cannot be the same.

fields.name: port-monitor.src-interface-type
fields.description: Specifies the type of source interface whose traffic will be mirrored to this monitoring port. GIGABIT_ETHERNET mirrors traffic from a single physical Ethernet port. PORT_CHANNEL mirrors aggregated traffic from all member ports in a Link Aggregation Group (LAG).

fields.name: port-type
fields.description: Designates the interface as either a WAN (Wide Area Network) or LAN (Local Area Network) port. WAN ports typically connect to external networks or service providers and may apply different security policies, NAT rules, and routing behaviors. LAN ports connect to internal trusted networks. This designation affects firewall rules, routing decisions, and security policy enforcement.

fields.name: portchannel-lag
fields.description: Attach a link aggreagatioin group (LAG) to physical interface.

fields.name: retain-profile-configs
fields.description: To decide whether or not to retain profile configs on an interface when the profile is removed from the said interface

fields.name: speed
fields.description: Configures the link speed for the Ethernet interface. When set to SPEED_AUTO (default), the interface automatically negotiates the highest supported speed with the connected device. Manual speed settings force the interface to operate at a specific rate, which may require matching configuration on the peer device.

fields.name: speed-mode
fields.description: Configures the operational speed mode for multi-rate capable interfaces. Only supported on 7280 hardware. Determines whether the interface operates in 40Gbps, 10Gbps, or 1Gbps mode. Changing this setting may affect port availability or require a reboot. Consult hardware documentation for supported speed modes per interface.

fields.name: sw-profile
fields.description: Switch Port Profile (if any) associated with the interface.

fields.name: trusted
fields.description: Marks the interface as trusted for security policy purposes. Trusted interfaces bypass certain security checks and firewall rules, allowing unrestricted communication. Typically applied to internal management interfaces or connections to known secure networks. Use with caution as this reduces security enforcement on the interface.

fields.name: tunneled-node-port
fields.description: Enables tunneled node functionality on the interface, allowing it to participate in overlay network tunneling. When enabled, traffic received on this port can be automatically encapsulated and forwarded through SD-WAN or VPN tunnels based on routing policies. Typically used for branch office deployments where local devices need transparent access to central resources over secure tunnels.

native-vlan and trunk-vlan-ranges should be set to null while configuring access mode
Eg: switchport: {interface-mode: ACCESS, access-vlan: 600, native-vlan: null,

switchport: {interface-mode: TRUNK, access-vlan: null, native-vlan: NATIVE_VLAN,

fields.name: burst
fields.description:
The burst size in units of kilobytes for the maximum egress traffic rate.
Valid when egress-rate is specified.

fields.name: cos
fields.description:
COS remark value for all packets arriving on the port. The new value
will be reflected in the outgoing VLAN tag.

AOSCX: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon transmit. The active
port trust mode must be 'None' before any cos remark value can be
configured. If cos remark is applied with any other trust config on
the port, then the config will be rejected by the device. In order
to fix this, either remove the cos remark config or change the trust
config on the port to NONE.
PVOS: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon arriving, which will
affect queueing.

fields.name: dscp
fields.description:
The DSCP remark for the port. The new value will be reflected in any
outgoing IP packet headers.

AOSCX: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon transmit. The active
port trust mode must be 'None' before any dscp remark value can be
configured. If dscp remark is applied with any other trust config on
the port, then the config will be rejected by the device. In order
to fix this, either remove the dscp remark config or change the trust
config on the port to NONE.
PVOS: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon arrival, which will
affect queueing.

fields.name: schedule-profile
fields.description:
QoS interface schedule profile. The schedule profile must
first be configured using the aruba-qos-schedule yang model, and must be
valid for the platform on which the port resides. In addition, the
schedule profile must match the configured number of queues and queue ID
values in the globally-applied queue profile.

fields.name: threshold-profile

must be supportable by the platform on which the port resides.

fields.name: trust
fields.description:
QoS Trust Mode Configuration for the port.
For AOSCX devices, when no trust mode is applied on the port,
the trust mode configured in the aruba-qos-global profile takes precedence.
If no trust mode is configured in the aruba-qos-global profile,
trust NONE is used.

fields.name: burst
fields.description:
The burst size in units of kilobytes for the maximum egress traffic rate.
Valid when egress-rate is specified.

fields.name: cos
fields.description:
COS remark value for all packets arriving on the port. The new value
will be reflected in the outgoing VLAN tag.

AOSCX: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon transmit. The active
port trust mode must be 'None' before any cos remark value can be
configured. If cos remark is applied with any other trust config on
the port, then the config will be rejected by the device. In order
to fix this, either remove the cos remark config or change the trust
config on the port to NONE.
PVOS: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon arriving, which will
affect queueing.

fields.name: dscp
fields.description:
The DSCP remark for the port. The new value will be reflected in any
outgoing IP packet headers.

AOSCX: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon transmit. The active
port trust mode must be 'None' before any dscp remark value can be
configured. If dscp remark is applied with any other trust config on
the port, then the config will be rejected by the device. In order
to fix this, either remove the dscp remark config or change the trust
config on the port to NONE.
PVOS: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon arrival, which will
affect queueing.

fields.name: schedule-profile
fields.description:
QoS interface schedule profile. The schedule profile must
first be configured using the aruba-qos-schedule yang model, and must be
valid for the platform on which the port resides. In addition, the
schedule profile must match the configured number of queues and queue ID
values in the globally-applied queue profile.

fields.name: threshold-profile

QoS interface threshold profile. The threshold profile must
first be configured using the aruba-qos-threshold-profile yang model, and
must be supportable by the platform on which the port resides.

fields.name: trust
fields.description:
QoS Trust Mode Configuration for the port.
For AOSCX devices, when no trust mode is applied on the port,
the trust mode configured in the aruba-qos-global profile takes precedence.
If no trust mode is configured in the aruba-qos-global profile,
trust NONE is used.

fields.name: aos-s-switch-chassis-automatic

This container provides a simplified configuration approach for chassis switches, applying consistent Interface Profile settings across all installed line cards. It is ideal for homogeneous chassis deployments where all modules serve similar functions in the network.

fields.name: aos-s-switch-model

for switches across different form factors and capabilities. Each model
type corresponds to a specific hardware platform with predetermined port
counts, uplink configurations, and features like PoE support. This leaf
is used to target Interface Profile configurations to specific hardware models.
This field cannot be edited once created. Allowed model is 5400R.

fields.name: vlan-translate
fields.description: VLAN translations.

fields.name: origin
fields.description:
A port with a VLAN translation configuration allows traffic only for the translated VLAN and the native VLAN;
if it is a member of more VLANS, it does not allow traffic for them.
A translated VLAN must be present on the switch before the rule is created; the original VLAN need not be present.
VLAN translation and MVRP cannot be enabled on the same interface.

fields.name: translated
fields.description: Translated VLAN identifier and not allowed on native VLAN 1.

fields.name: qos
fields.description: QoS interface parameters for the physical interface or port channel. For port channels, the same configuration is applied to all members.

fields.name: burst
fields.description:
The burst size in units of kilobytes for the maximum egress traffic rate.
Valid when egress-rate is specified.

fields.name: cos
fields.description:
COS remark value for all packets arriving on the port. The new value
will be reflected in the outgoing VLAN tag.

AOSCX: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon transmit. The active
port trust mode must be 'None' before any cos remark value can be
configured. If cos remark is applied with any other trust config on
the port, then the config will be rejected by the device. In order
to fix this, either remove the cos remark config or change the trust
config on the port to NONE.
PVOS: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon arriving, which will
affect queueing.

fields.name: dscp
fields.description:
The DSCP remark for the port. The new value will be reflected in any
outgoing IP packet headers.

AOSCX: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon transmit. The active
port trust mode must be 'None' before any dscp remark value can be
configured. If dscp remark is applied with any other trust config on
the port, then the config will be rejected by the device. In order
to fix this, either remove the dscp remark config or change the trust
config on the port to NONE.
PVOS: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon arrival, which will
affect queueing.

fields.name: max-rate-units

fields.name: priority-mapping-bandwidth-scheduler
fields.description:
Priority-mapping bandwidth-scheduler interface profile. Profiles must
first be created using the aruba-gw-scheduler yang model.

fields.name: schedule-profile
fields.description:
QoS interface schedule profile. The schedule profile must
first be configured using the aruba-qos-schedule yang model, and must be
valid for the platform on which the port resides. In addition, the
schedule profile must match the configured number of queues and queue ID
values in the globally-applied queue profile.

fields.name: threshold-profile
fields.description:
QoS interface threshold profile. The threshold profile must
first be configured using the aruba-qos-threshold-profile yang model, and
must be supportable by the platform on which the port resides.

fields.name: trust
fields.description:
QoS Trust Mode Configuration for the port.
For AOSCX devices, when no trust mode is applied on the port,
the trust mode configured in the aruba-qos-global profile takes precedence.
If no trust mode is configured in the aruba-qos-global profile,
trust NONE is used.

fields.name: qos.cos
fields.description: COS remark value for all packets arriving on the port. The new value will be reflected in the outgoing VLAN tag.  AOSCX: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon transmit. The active port trust mode must be 'None' before any cos remark value can be configured. If cos remark is applied with any other trust config on the port, then the config will be rejected by the device. In order to fix this, either remove the cos remark config or change the trust config on the port to NONE. PVOS: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon arriving, which will affect queueing.

fields.name: qos.dscp
fields.description: The DSCP remark for the port. The new value will be reflected in any outgoing IP packet headers.  AOSCX: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon transmit. The active port trust mode must be 'None' before any dscp remark value can be configured. If dscp remark is applied with any other trust config on the port, then the config will be rejected by the device. In order to fix this, either remove the dscp remark config or change the trust config on the port to NONE. PVOS: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon arrival, which will affect queueing.

Interface access or trunk mode for VLANs.
The access-vlan should be set to null for configuring trunk mode and
native-vlan, trunk-vlan-ranges and trunk-vlan-all should be set to null while configuring access mode
Eg: switchport: {interface-mode: ACCESS, access-vlan: 600, native-vlan: null,
trunk-vlan-all: null, trunk-vlan-ranges: null}
switchport: {interface-mode: TRUNK, access-vlan: null, native-vlan: NATIVE_VLAN,
trunk-vlan-all: false, trunk-vlan-ranges: [ 1000 ]}

fields.name: vlan-translate
fields.description: VLAN translations.

fields.name: origin
fields.description:
A port with a VLAN translation configuration allows traffic only for the translated VLAN and the native VLAN;
if it is a member of more VLANS, it does not allow traffic for them.
A translated VLAN must be present on the switch before the rule is created; the original VLAN need not be present.
VLAN translation and MVRP cannot be enabled on the same interface.

fields.name: translated
fields.description: Translated VLAN identifier and not allowed on native VLAN 1.

fields.name: qos
fields.description: QoS interface parameters for the physical interface or port channel. For port channels, the same configuration is applied to all members.

fields.name: burst
fields.description:
The burst size in units of kilobytes for the maximum egress traffic rate.
Valid when egress-rate is specified.

fields.name: cos
fields.description:
COS remark value for all packets arriving on the port. The new value
will be reflected in the outgoing VLAN tag.

AOSCX: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon transmit. The active
port trust mode must be 'None' before any cos remark value can be
configured. If cos remark is applied with any other trust config on
the port, then the config will be rejected by the device. In order
to fix this, either remove the cos remark config or change the trust
config on the port to NONE.
PVOS: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon arriving, which will
affect queueing.

fields.name: dscp
fields.description:
The DSCP remark for the port. The new value will be reflected in any
outgoing IP packet headers.

AOSCX: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon transmit. The active
port trust mode must be 'None' before any dscp remark value can be
configured. If dscp remark is applied with any other trust config on
the port, then the config will be rejected by the device. In order
to fix this, either remove the dscp remark config or change the trust
config on the port to NONE.
PVOS: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon arrival, which will
affect queueing.

fields.description:
Priority-mapping bandwidth-scheduler interface profile. Profiles must
first be created using the aruba-gw-scheduler yang model.

fields.name: schedule-profile
fields.description:
QoS interface schedule profile. The schedule profile must
first be configured using the aruba-qos-schedule yang model, and must be
valid for the platform on which the port resides. In addition, the
schedule profile must match the configured number of queues and queue ID
values in the globally-applied queue profile.

fields.name: threshold-profile
fields.description:
QoS interface threshold profile. The threshold profile must
first be configured using the aruba-qos-threshold-profile yang model, and
must be supportable by the platform on which the port resides.

fields.name: trust
fields.description:
QoS Trust Mode Configuration for the port.
For AOSCX devices, when no trust mode is applied on the port,
the trust mode configured in the aruba-qos-global profile takes precedence.
If no trust mode is configured in the aruba-qos-global profile,
trust NONE is used.

fields.description: Switchport configuration. This configuration is valid only on a layer2 interface.

fields.name: access-vlan
fields.description: Assign the access VLAN to the access port.

fields.name: interface-mode
fields.description:
Interface access or trunk mode for VLANs.
The access-vlan should be set to null for configuring trunk mode and
native-vlan, trunk-vlan-ranges and trunk-vlan-all should be set to null while configuring access mode
Eg: switchport: {interface-mode: ACCESS, access-vlan: 600, native-vlan: null,
trunk-vlan-all: null, trunk-vlan-ranges: null}
switchport: {interface-mode: TRUNK, access-vlan: null, native-vlan: NATIVE_VLAN,
trunk-vlan-all: false, trunk-vlan-ranges: [ 1000 ]}

fields.name: native-vlan
fields.description:
Native VLAN id for untagged frames arriving on
a trunk interface.  Tagged frames sent on an interface
configured with a native VLAN should have their tags
stripped prior to transmission. This configuration is only
valid on a trunk interface.

fields.name: tag
fields.description:
This configuration is only valid on a trunk interface and the configured interface
does not accept untagged frames coming in and configured to be tagged on all VLANs.

fields.name: trunk-vlan-all
fields.description:
When interface mode is trunk allow all VLANs for trunk mode interface.
On CX devices, includes new VLANs as they are configured.

fields.name: trunk-vlan-ranges
fields.description:
VLAN ranges that the interface may carry when in trunk mode.
On CX devices, only applies currently configured VLANs.

Interface access or trunk mode for VLANs.
The access-vlan should be set to null for configuring trunk mode and
native-vlan, trunk-vlan-ranges and trunk-vlan-all should be set to null while configuring access mode
Eg: switchport: {interface-mode: ACCESS, access-vlan: 600, native-vlan: null,
trunk-vlan-all: null, trunk-vlan-ranges: null}
switchport: {interface-mode: TRUNK, access-vlan: null, native-vlan: NATIVE_VLAN,
trunk-vlan-all: false, trunk-vlan-ranges: [ 1000 ]}

stripped prior to transmission. This configuration is only
valid on a trunk interface.

fields.name: burst
fields.description:
The burst size in units of kilobytes for the maximum egress traffic rate.
Valid when egress-rate is specified.

fields.name: cos
fields.description:
COS remark value for all packets arriving on the port. The new value
will be reflected in the outgoing VLAN tag.

AOSCX: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon transmit. The active
port trust mode must be 'None' before any cos remark value can be
configured. If cos remark is applied with any other trust config on
the port, then the config will be rejected by the device. In order
to fix this, either remove the cos remark config or change the trust
config on the port to NONE.
PVOS: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon arriving, which will
affect queueing.

fields.name: dscp
fields.description:
The DSCP remark for the port. The new value will be reflected in any
outgoing IP packet headers.

AOSCX: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon transmit. The active
port trust mode must be 'None' before any dscp remark value can be
configured. If dscp remark is applied with any other trust config on
the port, then the config will be rejected by the device. In order
to fix this, either remove the dscp remark config or change the trust
config on the port to NONE.
PVOS: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon arrival, which will
affect queueing.

trust NONE is used.

fields.name: cos
fields.description:
COS remark value for all packets arriving on the port. The new value
will be reflected in the outgoing VLAN tag.

AOSCX: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon transmit. The active
port trust mode must be 'None' before any cos remark value can be
configured. If cos remark is applied with any other trust config on
the port, then the config will be rejected by the device. In order
to fix this, either remove the cos remark config or change the trust
config on the port to NONE.
PVOS: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon arriving, which will
affect queueing.

fields.name: dscp
fields.description:
The DSCP remark for the port. The new value will be reflected in any
outgoing IP packet headers.

AOSCX: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon transmit. The active
port trust mode must be 'None' before any dscp remark value can be
configured. If dscp remark is applied with any other trust config on
the port, then the config will be rejected by the device. In order
to fix this, either remove the dscp remark config or change the trust
config on the port to NONE.
PVOS: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon arrival, which will
affect queueing.

fields.name: schedule-profile

first be configured using the aruba-qos-schedule yang model, and must be
valid for the platform on which the port resides. In addition, the
schedule profile must match the configured number of queues and queue ID
values in the globally-applied queue profile.

fields.name: threshold-profile

first be configured using the aruba-qos-threshold-profile yang model, and
must be supportable by the platform on which the port resides.

fields.name: trust
fields.description:
QoS Trust Mode Configuration for the port.
For AOSCX devices, when no trust mode is applied on the port,
the trust mode configured in the aruba-qos-global profile takes precedence.
If no trust mode is configured in the aruba-qos-global profile,
trust NONE is used.

fields.name: burst
fields.description:
The burst size in units of kilobytes for the maximum egress traffic rate.
Valid when egress-rate is specified.

fields.name: cos
fields.description:
COS remark value for all packets arriving on the port. The new value
will be reflected in the outgoing VLAN tag.

AOSCX: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon transmit. The active
port trust mode must be 'None' before any cos remark value can be
configured. If cos remark is applied with any other trust config on
the port, then the config will be rejected by the device. In order
to fix this, either remove the cos remark config or change the trust
config on the port to NONE.
PVOS: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon arriving, which will
affect queueing.

fields.name: dscp
fields.description:
The DSCP remark for the port. The new value will be reflected in any
outgoing IP packet headers.

AOSCX: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon transmit. The active
port trust mode must be 'None' before any dscp remark value can be
configured. If dscp remark is applied with any other trust config on
the port, then the config will be rejected by the device. In order
to fix this, either remove the dscp remark config or change the trust
config on the port to NONE.
PVOS: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon arrival, which will
affect queueing.

fields.name: max-rate-units
fields.description: Traffic rate units. Required when egress-rate is specified.
