fields.description: Guaranteed minimum bandwidth.

fields.name: priority-mapping-bandwidth-scheduler
fields.description:
Priority-mapping bandwidth-scheduler interface profile. Profiles must
first be created using the aruba-gw-scheduler yang model.

fields.name: schedule-profile
fields.description:
QoS interface schedule profile. The schedule profile must
first be configured using the aruba-qos-schedule yang model, and must be
valid for the platform on which the port resides. In addition, the
schedule profile must match the configured number of queues and queue ID
values in the globally-applied queue profile.

fields.name: threshold-profile
fields.description:
QoS interface threshold profile. The threshold profile must
first be configured using the aruba-qos-threshold-profile yang model, and
must be supportable by the platform on which the port resides.

fields.name: trust
fields.description:
QoS Trust Mode Configuration for the port.
For AOSCX devices, when no trust mode is applied on the port,
the trust mode configured in the aruba-qos-global profile takes precedence.
If no trust mode is configured in the aruba-qos-global profile,
trust NONE is used.

or RxTx flow-control configuration will take effect.

fields.name: interface-mode
fields.description:
Interface access or trunk mode for VLANs.
The access-vlan should be set to null for configuring trunk mode and
native-vlan, trunk-vlan-ranges and trunk-vlan-all should be set to null while configuring access mode
Eg: switchport: {interface-mode: ACCESS, access-vlan: 600, native-vlan: null,
trunk-vlan-all: null, trunk-vlan-ranges: null}
switchport: {interface-mode: TRUNK, access-vlan: null, native-vlan: NATIVE_VLAN,
trunk-vlan-all: false, trunk-vlan-ranges: [ 1000 ]}

fields.name: native-vlan
fields.description:

configured with a native VLAN should have their tags
stripped prior to transmission. This configuration is only
valid on a trunk interface.

fields.name: tag

fields.name: trunk-vlan-all
fields.description:
When interface mode is trunk allow all VLANs for trunk mode interface.
On CX devices, includes new VLANs as they are configured.

fields.name: trunk-vlan-ranges
fields.description:
VLAN ranges that the interface may carry when in trunk mode.
On CX devices, only applies currently configured VLANs.

fields.name: origin
fields.description:
A port with a VLAN translation configuration allows traffic only for the translated VLAN and the native VLAN;
if it is a member of more VLANS, it does not allow traffic for them.
A translated VLAN must be present on the switch before the rule is created; the original VLAN need not be present.
VLAN translation and MVRP cannot be enabled on the same interface.

fields.name: qos
fields.description: QoS interface parameters for the physical interface or port channel.

fields.name: burst
fields.description:
The burst size in units of kilobytes for the maximum egress traffic rate.
Valid when egress-rate is specified.

fields.name: cos
fields.description:
COS remark value for all packets arriving on the port. The new value
will be reflected in the outgoing VLAN tag.

AOSCX: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon transmit. The active
port trust mode must be 'None' before any cos remark value can be
configured. If cos remark is applied with any other trust config on
the port, then the config will be rejected by the device. In order
to fix this, either remove the cos remark config or change the trust
config on the port to NONE.
PVOS: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon arriving, which will
affect queueing.

fields.name: dscp
fields.description:
The DSCP remark for the port. The new value will be reflected in any
outgoing IP packet headers.

AOSCX: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon transmit. The active
port trust mode must be 'None' before any dscp remark value can be
configured. If dscp remark is applied with any other trust config on
the port, then the config will be rejected by the device. In order
to fix this, either remove the dscp remark config or change the trust
config on the port to NONE.
PVOS: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon arrival, which will
affect queueing.

fields.name: schedule-profile
fields.description:
QoS interface schedule profile. The schedule profile must
first be configured using the aruba-qos-schedule yang model, and must be
valid for the platform on which the port resides. In addition, the
schedule profile must match the configured number of queues and queue ID
values in the globally-applied queue profile.

fields.name: threshold-profile
fields.description:
QoS interface threshold profile. The threshold profile must
first be configured using the aruba-qos-threshold-profile yang model, and
must be supportable by the platform on which the port resides.

fields.name: trust
fields.description:
QoS Trust Mode Configuration for the port.
For AOSCX devices, when no trust mode is applied on the port,
the trust mode configured in the aruba-qos-global profile takes precedence.
If no trust mode is configured in the aruba-qos-global profile,
trust NONE is used.

fields.name: trunk-type
fields.description:
Type of trunk.
 For gateways, the aggregation types supported are TRUNK for static and LACP for dynamic.
 The change of LAG type is not allowed without deleting the members in it. All the members need to be
 deleted before changing the LAG type

fields.name: unknown-vlans
fields.description:
Configure GVRP unknown VLANs handling mode for port channel interface.
 Learn: Accept join requests for new VLANs and propagate through GVRP.
 Block: Process GVRP packets for known VLANs only, ignore new VLANs.
 Disable: Ignore all GVRP packets.

fields.description: QoS interface parameters for the physical interface or port channel.

fields.name: burst
fields.description:
The burst size in units of kilobytes for the maximum egress traffic rate.
Valid when egress-rate is specified.

fields.name: cos
fields.description:
COS remark value for all packets arriving on the port. The new value
will be reflected in the outgoing VLAN tag.

AOSCX: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon transmit. The active
port trust mode must be 'None' before any cos remark value can be
configured. If cos remark is applied with any other trust config on
the port, then the config will be rejected by the device. In order
to fix this, either remove the cos remark config or change the trust
config on the port to NONE.
PVOS: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon arriving, which will
affect queueing.

fields.name: dscp
fields.description:
The DSCP remark for the port. The new value will be reflected in any
outgoing IP packet headers.

AOSCX: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon transmit. The active
port trust mode must be 'None' before any dscp remark value can be
configured. If dscp remark is applied with any other trust config on
the port, then the config will be rejected by the device. In order
to fix this, either remove the dscp remark config or change the trust
config on the port to NONE.
PVOS: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon arrival, which will
affect queueing.

fields.name: egress-rate
fields.description:
The maximum egress traffic rate for the interface.
To configure this, the type of max-rate-units must be specified.

fields.name: max-rate-units
fields.description: Traffic rate units. Required when egress-rate is specified.

fields.name: minimum-bandwidth
fields.description: Guaranteed minimum bandwidth settings

fields.name: bandwidth
fields.description: Guaranteed minimum bandwidth.

fields.name: priority-mapping-bandwidth-scheduler
fields.description:
Priority-mapping bandwidth-scheduler interface profile. Profiles must
first be created using the aruba-gw-scheduler yang model.

fields.name: schedule-profile
fields.description:
QoS interface schedule profile. The schedule profile must
first be configured using the aruba-qos-schedule yang model, and must be
valid for the platform on which the port resides. In addition, the
schedule profile must match the configured number of queues and queue ID
values in the globally-applied queue profile.

fields.name: threshold-profile
fields.description:
QoS interface threshold profile. The threshold profile must
first be configured using the aruba-qos-threshold-profile yang model, and
must be supportable by the platform on which the port resides.

fields.name: trust
fields.description:
QoS Trust Mode Configuration for the port.
For AOSCX devices, when no trust mode is applied on the port,
the trust mode configured in the aruba-qos-global profile takes precedence.
If no trust mode is configured in the aruba-qos-global profile,
trust NONE is used.

fields.name: lag.qos-lag.cos
fields.description: COS remark value for all packets arriving on the port. The new value will be reflected in the outgoing VLAN tag.  AOSCX: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon transmit. The active port trust mode must be 'None' before any cos remark value can be configured. If cos remark is applied with any other trust config on the port, then the config will be rejected by the device. In order to fix this, either remove the cos remark config or change the trust config on the port to NONE. PVOS: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon arriving, which will affect queueing.

fields.name: lag.qos-lag.dscp
fields.description: The DSCP remark for the port. The new value will be reflected in any outgoing IP packet headers.  AOSCX: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon transmit. The active port trust mode must be 'None' before any dscp remark value can be configured. If dscp remark is applied with any other trust config on the port, then the config will be rejected by the device. In order to fix this, either remove the dscp remark config or change the trust config on the port to NONE. PVOS: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon arrival, which will affect queueing.

fields.description: Configure parameters for GPS (Global Positioning System) function. Available on firmware versions 8.10.0 to 10.0.0, and 10.4.0 and later.

fields.name: dynamic-model
fields.description:
Dynamic model of GPS, in which it includes options: AIRBORNEV1/AIRBORNEV2/AIRBORNEV4
/AUTOMOTIVE/BIKE/PEDESTRIAN/PORTABLE/SEA/STATIONARY/WRIST.
STATIONARY is default.

fields.name: ellipse-report-interval
fields.description:
Interval for ellipse report when FCO response is received.
Range is from 60 to 1440 in minutes, 360 by default.

fields.name: enable
fields.description: Enable GPS function.

fields.name: height
fields.description:
Height of device over ground, which supports 16 fractions at most.
In meters.

fields.name: height-alias
fields.description: Alias for AP height of GPS.

fields.name: indoor-sp-location
fields.description:
An enhancement for Standard Power(SP) APs to obtain GPS ellipse data. When enabled,
APs are able to broadcast their GPS ellipse data in wireless packets, then neighbor APs with
poor GPS signal can use the received infomation to compute their own ellipses.

fields.name: max-relay-distance
fields.description:
A limit for accumulated distance from the AP that broadcasts original ellipse data.
If the distance is over this limit, AP will not choose this ellipse.

fields.name: max-samples
fields.description:
Maximum number of samples for GPS ellipse report, which is from 30 to 600, 100 by default.
This value means the maxmum samples saved on APs.

fields.name: min-samples
fields.description:
Minimum number of GPS samples for the fisrt report, its value is from 1 to 100, 30 by default.
A step for the next report till the max number. For example, first reporting happens
when there are 30 samples, the nex report happens when 60 (30 + 30) samples.

fields.name: retry
fields.description:
Whether AP sends GPS reports when number of samples reaches the maximum, but no reply
from FCO (Automatic Frequency Coordination) service. This service applies channel list
and power level to enable AP 6G radio within the USA.
Disabled by default.

fields.name: sampling-interval
fields.description:
Interval to read GPS data from chip, an integer that from 1 to 3600, in seconds.
Deault value is 10 second.
Available on firmware versions 10.7.0 and later.

fields.name: state
fields.description: Configure GPS function with options AUTO/ENABLE/DISABLE, AUTO is the default config.

fields.name: advanced-zone
fields.description: Enable or disable the advanced zone feature that can configure up to 32 SSIDs. Since the mapping method of the WLAN index and BSSID index are different, when you change the advanced zone configuration, the BSSID is removed and created again. When advanced zone is enabled:  The WLAN SSID profile will remain inactive without the zone.  The WLAN SSID profile will remain inactive without the zone.  A zone can be assigned to a maximum of up to 16 SSIDs.  However, if the extended SSID is disabled,  a zone can be assigned to a maximum of up to 14 SSIDs wherein the first two virtual APs are reserved for mesh.

fields.name: advertise-ap-health-ie
fields.description: Control AP to enable/disable 'Over the Air AP Rescue' feature. This feature is enabled by default. 'Over the Air AP Rescue' feature controls AP to broadcast the AP health IE through the wireless SSIDs. The AP health IE contains many flags that can reflect current AP status like uplink status, Central connectivity status. Once AP lost Central connection, this AP health IE can be broadcast through wireless beacons so that our Aruba APs nearby can hear this beacon and send the AP health IE to Central. This will allow the user or engineer to understand the status of the issue AP and take measures to rescue it.

fields.name: dynamic-model
fields.description:
Dynamic model of GPS, in which it includes options: AIRBORNEV1/AIRBORNEV2/AIRBORNEV4
/AUTOMOTIVE/BIKE/PEDESTRIAN/PORTABLE/SEA/STATIONARY/WRIST.
STATIONARY is default.

fields.name: ellipse-report-interval
fields.description:
Interval for ellipse report when FCO response is received.
Range is from 60 to 1440 in minutes, 360 by default.

fields.name: enable
fields.description: Enable GPS function.

fields.name: height
fields.description:
Height of device over ground, which supports 16 fractions at most.
In meters.

fields.name: height-alias
fields.description: Alias for AP height of GPS.

fields.name: indoor-sp-location
fields.description:
An enhancement for Standard Power(SP) APs to obtain GPS ellipse data. When enabled,
APs are able to broadcast their GPS ellipse data in wireless packets, then neighbor APs with
poor GPS signal can use the received infomation to compute their own ellipses.

fields.name: max-relay-distance
fields.description:
A limit for accumulated distance from the AP that broadcasts original ellipse data.
If the distance is over this limit, AP will not choose this ellipse.

fields.name: max-samples
fields.description:
Maximum number of samples for GPS ellipse report, which is from 30 to 600, 100 by default.
This value means the maxmum samples saved on APs.

fields.name: min-samples
fields.description:
Minimum number of GPS samples for the fisrt report, its value is from 1 to 100, 30 by default.
A step for the next report till the max number. For example, first reporting happens
when there are 30 samples, the nex report happens when 60 (30 + 30) samples.

fields.name: retry
fields.description:
Whether AP sends GPS reports when number of samples reaches the maximum, but no reply
from FCO (Automatic Frequency Coordination) service. This service applies channel list
and power level to enable AP 6G radio within the USA.
Disabled by default.

fields.name: sampling-interval
fields.description:
Interval to read GPS data from chip, an integer that from 1 to 3600, in seconds.
Deault value is 10 second.
Available on firmware versions 10.7.0 and later.

fields.name: state
fields.description: Configure GPS function with options AUTO/ENABLE/DISABLE, AUTO is the default config.

fields.description: Dynamic model of GPS, in which it includes options: AIRBORNEV1/AIRBORNEV2/AIRBORNEV4 /AUTOMOTIVE/BIKE/PEDESTRIAN/PORTABLE/SEA/STATIONARY/WRIST. STATIONARY is default.

fields.description: A limit for accumulated distance from the AP that broadcasts original ellipse data. If the distance is over this limit, AP will not choose this ellipse.

fields.description: Configure AP local network key fetch for fast roaming. This feature enables APs to fetch PMK keys locally from the Home AP using L2 broadcast messages as an alternative to KMS on-demand key fetch. This helps reduce roaming latency and improves client connectivity when the AP-Central connection is down or KMS latency is high.

fields.name: advanced-zone
fields.description: Enable or disable the advanced zone feature that can configure up to 32 SSIDs. Since the mapping method of the WLAN index and BSSID index are different, when you change the advanced zone configuration, the BSSID is removed and created again. When advanced zone is enabled:  The WLAN SSID profile will remain inactive without the zone.  The WLAN SSID profile will remain inactive without the zone.  A zone can be assigned to a maximum of up to 16 SSIDs.  However, if the extended SSID is disabled,  a zone can be assigned to a maximum of up to 14 SSIDs wherein the first two virtual APs are reserved for mesh.

fields.name: advertise-ap-health-ie
fields.description: Control AP to enable/disable 'Over the Air AP Rescue' feature. This feature is enabled by default. 'Over the Air AP Rescue' feature controls AP to broadcast the AP health IE through the wireless SSIDs. The AP health IE contains many flags that can reflect current AP status like uplink status, Central connectivity status. Once AP lost Central connection, this AP health IE can be broadcast through wireless beacons so that our Aruba APs nearby can hear this beacon and send the AP health IE to Central. This will allow the user or engineer to understand the status of the issue AP and take measures to rescue it.

fields.name: aaa-timers
fields.description: Configures timeout intervals for AAA (Authentication, Authorization, and Accounting) operations including server failure detection, user idle sessions, logon attempts, and RADIUS accounting updates.

fields.name: dead-time
fields.description:
Dead time interval in minutes for a down authentication server.
Value of 0 disables dead time.

fields.name: idle-timeout
fields.description: Inactivity timeout for authenticated users in minutes. If no traffic is detected from a user for this duration, the session is terminated and re-authentication is required. This parameter is mutually exclusive with idle-timeout-seconds.

fields.name: idle-timeout-seconds
fields.description:
User idle timeout in seconds.
Valid range is 30-15300 seconds in multiples of 30 seconds.
This field can be configured only if idle-timeout is not configured.

fields.name: logon-lifetime
fields.description: Maximum session duration for captive portal or web-authenticated users in minutes. After this time expires, the user must re-authenticate via the captive portal even if the session is active. Value of 0 disables the maximum lifetime, allowing sessions to persist until idle timeout or explicit logout.

fields.name: stats-timeout
fields.description: Interval for sending RADIUS Interim-Update accounting messages in minutes. These updates provide periodic usage statistics (bytes transferred, session duration) to the RADIUS server for active user sessions. Mutually exclusive with stats-timeout-seconds.

fields.name: stats-timeout-seconds
fields.description: User Interim stats timeout value in seconds. This field can be configured only if stats-timeout is not configured.

fields.name: aaa-timers.dead-time
fields.description: Dead time interval in minutes for a down authentication server. Value of 0 disables dead time.

fields.name: aaa-timers.idle-timeout
fields.description: Inactivity timeout for authenticated users in minutes. If no traffic is detected from a user for this duration, the session is terminated and re-authentication is required. This parameter is mutually exclusive with idle-timeout-seconds.

fields.name: aaa-timers.idle-timeout-seconds
fields.description: User idle timeout in seconds. Valid range is 30-15300 seconds in multiples of 30 seconds. This field can be configured only if idle-timeout is not configured.

fields.name: aaa-timers.logon-lifetime
fields.description: Maximum session duration for captive portal or web-authenticated users in minutes. After this time expires, the user must re-authenticate via the captive portal even if the session is active. Value of 0 disables the maximum lifetime, allowing sessions to persist until idle timeout or explicit logout.

fields.name: aaa-timers.stats-timeout
fields.description: Interval for sending RADIUS Interim-Update accounting messages in minutes. These updates provide periodic usage statistics (bytes transferred, session duration) to the RADIUS server for active user sessions. Mutually exclusive with stats-timeout-seconds.

fields.name: aaa-timers.stats-timeout-seconds
fields.description: User Interim stats timeout value in seconds. This field can be configured only if stats-timeout is not configured.

fields.name: auth-trace-loglevel
fields.description: Enable authentication tracing with specified syslog level threshold. All authentication-related syslog messages at or above this severity will be traced.

fields.name: contact

fields.name: cpdns-disable
fields.description: Disables the gateway's automatic DNS redirection for captive portal detection. When enabled, the gateway will not intercept DNS queries from unauthenticated clients to force captive portal discovery. Mutually exclusive with cpdns-ip.

fields.name: cpdns-ip
fields.description: Specifies a custom IP address returned in DNS responses to unauthenticated clients, forcing redirection to the captive portal. This overrides the default behavior of returning the gateway's own IP address. Mutually exclusive with cpdns-disable. Corresponds to the `ip cp-redirect-address` CLI command.

fields.name: firewall
fields.description: Defines device-wide firewall behaviors that apply to all traffic regardless of user role or VLAN. These settings control inter-user traffic isolation, jumbo frame support, and VoIP QoS trust models.

fields.name: deny-inter-user-bridging
fields.description:
Prevents the forwarding of Layer2 traffic between wired or wireless users.
You can configure user role policies that prevent Layer3 traffic between users or networks but this does not block Layer2 traffic.
This option can be used to prevent traffic, such as Appletalk or IPX from being forwarded.
If enabled, traffic (all nonIP traffic) to untrusted port or tunnel is also blocked.

fields.name: deny-inter-user-bridging-allowed-addresses
fields.description: Configure IPv4/IPv6 addresses to be exempted when deny-inter-user-bridging is enabled. Total IPv4 and IPv6 allowed addresses can't exceed 256

fields.name: deny-inter-user-traffic
fields.description:
Denies downstream traffic between users in a wireless network (untrusted users) by disallowing layer2 and layer3 traffic.
This parameter does not depend on the deny-inter-userbridging parameter being enabled or disabled.

fields.name: drop-ipv4-options
fields.description: When enabled, all IPv4 packets with options are dropped. You should not enable this option unless instructed to do so by an Aruba representative

fields.name: enable-stateful-icmp
fields.description: Enables stateful ICMP processing. This parameter create sessions for ICMP errors and denies unidirectional replies. Disabled by default.

fields.name: enforce-tcp-handshake
fields.description: Prevents data from passing between two clients until the three-way TCP handshake has been performed. This option should be disabled when you have mobile clients on the network as enabling this option will cause mobility to fail. You can enable this option if there are no mobile clients on the network.

fields.name: enforce-tcp-sequence
fields.description: Enforces the TCP sequence numbers for all packets. Disabled by default

fields.name: jumbo
fields.description: Enable Jumbo frames processing with default MTU value 9216

fields.name: jumbo-mtu
fields.description: Enable Jumbo frames processing with custom MTU value. Valid range is 1789-9216

fields.name: ipv4-configuration
fields.description: System IPv4 configurations, allows you to set either the loopback interface or a specific VLAN interface address. If the system IPv4 is not configured, then the first configured VLAN interface address is selected by the device.

fields.name: device-interface-type
fields.description:
Specifies the interface type used for the system controller IPv4 address.
When set to VLAN, the device-vlan or device-vlan-alias parameter must also be specified to identify which VLAN interface to use. Corresponds to the `controller-ip` CLI command.

fields.name: device-vlan
fields.description: References an existing VLAN Interface profile by ID. The primary IPv4 address configured on this VLAN will be used as the controller-ip. Valid only when device-interface-type is set to VLAN.

fields.name: device-vlan-alias
fields.description:
Alias for device VLAN identifier, only applicable when device type is set to VLAN.
It cannot co-exist with device VLAN identifier field.

fields.name: ipv4-configuration.device-interface-type
fields.description: Specifies the interface type used for the system controller IPv4 address. When set to VLAN, the device-vlan or device-vlan-alias parameter must also be specified to identify which VLAN interface to use. Corresponds to the `controller-ip` CLI command.

fields.name: ipv4-configuration.device-vlan
fields.description: References an existing VLAN Interface profile by ID. The primary IPv4 address configured on this VLAN will be used as the controller-ip. Valid only when device-interface-type is set to VLAN.

fields.name: ipv4-configuration.device-vlan-alias
fields.description: Alias for device VLAN identifier, only applicable when device type is set to VLAN. It cannot co-exist with device VLAN identifier field.

fields.name: ipv6-certification-mode
fields.description: Enables IPv6 certification test mode for compliance validation. This mode adjusts protocol timers and behaviors to match IPv6 conformance test requirements (e.g., IPv6 Ready Logo testing). Should only be enabled in test environments.

fields.name: ipv6-configuration
fields.description: System IPv6 configurations, allows you to set either the loopback interface or a specific VLAN interface address. If the system IPv6 is not configured, then the first configured VLAN interface address is selected by the device.

fields.name: device-address
fields.description:
Specific IPv6 address to use as the controller-ipv6 identifier. This address must be pre-configured on the VLAN interface specified in device-vlan.
Valid only when device-interface-type is set to VLAN. This parameter is restricted to device-level scope and cannot be applied at site or global levels.
It cannot co-exist with ipv6-device-vlan-alias.

fields.name: device-interface-type
fields.description: Device interface type to indicate either loopback or VLAN interface.

fields.name: device-vlan
fields.description:
Device VLAN identifier, only applicable when device type is set to VLAN.
It cannot co-exist with ipv6-device-vlan-alias.

fields.name: ipv6-configuration.device-address
fields.description: Specific IPv6 address to use as the controller-ipv6 identifier. This address must be pre-configured on the VLAN interface specified in device-vlan. Valid only when device-interface-type is set to VLAN. This parameter is restricted to device-level scope and cannot be applied at site or global levels. It cannot co-exist with ipv6-device-vlan-alias.

fields.description: Device interface type to indicate either loopback or VLAN interface.

fields.name: ipv6-device-vlan-alias
fields.description: Alias for IPv6 device VLAN and address configuration, only applicable when device interface type is VLAN. It cannot co-exist with direct device-vlan and device-address.

fields.name: ipv6-enable
fields.description: Master enable for IPv6 protocol support on the gateway. When disabled, the device will drop all IPv6 packets and will not participate in IPv6 routing or forwarding.

fields.name: ipv6-proxy-ra
fields.description: Configures the gateway to act as an IPv6 router advertisement proxy, forwarding RA messages between network segments. This allows IPv6 clients on downstream VLANs to receive router advertisements from upstream routers without direct Layer 2 connectivity.

fields.name: advertise-interval
fields.description: Interval for sending unsolicited IPv6 Router Advertisement messages in seconds. Per RFC 4861, this value must be between 180 and 1800 seconds.

fields.name: ipv6-proxy-ra.advertise-interval
fields.description: Interval for sending unsolicited IPv6 Router Advertisement messages in seconds. Per RFC 4861, this value must be between 180 and 1800 seconds.

fields.name: ipv6-transition-mode
fields.description: Enable IPv6 transition-mode. Supported modes: NAT64.

fields.name: logging
fields.description: Controls local log message verbosity by module type, process, and severity level. This affects what diagnostic information is captured in the device's internal log buffers and forwarded to external syslog servers.

fields.name: module
fields.description: Defines per-module logging rules combining type, process, severity, and optional filtering by process, subcategory, or trace identifier. Each rule controls the minimum subcategory level for messages from specific system components.

fields.name: logging.module
fields.description: Defines per-module logging rules combining type, process, severity, and optional filtering by process, subcategory, or trace identifier. Each rule controls the minimum subcategory level for messages from specific system components.

fields.name: type

fields.name: radius
fields.description: Configures the gateway's behavior as a RADIUS client including the NAS-IP-Address sent in RADIUS packets, the source interface for RADIUS communication, and the UDP port for receiving RFC 3576 (Dynamic Authorization) messages from RADIUS servers.

fields.name: nas-ip
fields.description: Radius client NAS IP address. This field can be configured only if nas-vlan is not configured.

fields.name: nas-vlan
fields.description: References an existing VLAN Interface profile by ID. The primary IP address configured on this VLAN will be used as the RADIUS client NAS-IP-Address attribute. Mutually exclusive with nas-ip.

fields.name: port
fields.description: This field configures UDP port to receive RFC 3576 server requests.

fields.name: src-interface-loopback
fields.description:
IP address of loopback interface will be used as source address in Radius packets.
This field can be configured only if radius src-interface-vlan is not configured.

fields.name: src-interface-vlan
fields.description:
Source VLAN ID. IP address from this vlan interface will be used as source address in Radius packets.
This field can be configured only if radius src-interface-loopback is not configured.

fields.name: radius.nas-ip
fields.description: Radius client NAS IP address. This field can be configured only if nas-vlan is not configured.

fields.name: radius.nas-vlan
fields.description: References an existing VLAN Interface profile by ID. The primary IP address configured on this VLAN will be used as the RADIUS client NAS-IP-Address attribute. Mutually exclusive with nas-ip.

fields.name: radius.port
fields.description: This field configures UDP port to receive RFC 3576 server requests.

fields.name: radius.src-interface-loopback
fields.description: IP address of loopback interface will be used as source address in Radius packets. This field can be configured only if radius src-interface-vlan is not configured.

fields.name: radius.src-interface-vlan
fields.description: Source VLAN ID. IP address from this vlan interface will be used as source address in Radius packets. This field can be configured only if radius src-interface-loopback is not configured.

fields.name: tacacs
fields.description: Configures the gateway's behavior as a TACACS+ client, specifically controlling the source interface used for TACACS+ authentication and authorization requests to TACACS+ servers.

fields.name: src-interface-loopback
fields.description:
IP address of loopback interface will be used as source address in TACACS packets.
This field can be configured only if tacacs src-interface-vlan is not configured.

fields.name: src-interface-vlan
fields.description:
Source VLAN ID. IP address from this vlan interface will be used as source address in TACACS packets.
This field can be configured only if tacacs src-interface-loopback is not configured.

fields.name: tacacs.src-interface-loopback
fields.description: IP address of loopback interface will be used as source address in TACACS packets. This field can be configured only if tacacs src-interface-vlan is not configured.

fields.name: tacacs.src-interface-vlan
fields.description: Source VLAN ID. IP address from this vlan interface will be used as source address in TACACS packets. This field can be configured only if tacacs src-interface-loopback is not configured.

fields.name: timezone
fields.description: Configures the device's timezone offset from UTC for accurate timestamp representation in logs, SNMP traps, and the LCD display. The combined hour and minute offsets determine the local time zone.

fields.name: hour-offset
fields.description: Hours offset from the UTC

fields.name: minute-offset
fields.description: Minutes offset from the UTC

fields.name: name
fields.description: Timezone name.

fields.name: timezone.hour-offset
fields.description: Hours offset from the UTC

fields.name: timezone.minute-offset
fields.description: Minutes offset from the UTC

fields.name: timezone.name
fields.description: Timezone name.

fields.name: tunnel-loop-prevention
fields.description: Prevents Layer 2 forwarding loops that can occur when traffic is encapsulated between multiple tunnels terminating on the same gateway. When enabled, the gateway tracks tunnel packet origins and drops packets that would create circular forwarding paths between GRE, IPsec, or L2TPv3 tunnels.

fields.name: vpn-session-acl
fields.description: Security policy applied to VPNC Overlay traffic.

aruba_central_config_update_gw_system.summary: Update existing gateway system profile configurations

fields.name: aaa-timers
fields.description: Configures timeout intervals for AAA (Authentication, Authorization, and Accounting) operations including server failure detection, user idle sessions, logon attempts, and RADIUS accounting updates.

fields.name: dead-time
fields.description:
Dead time interval in minutes for a down authentication server.
Value of 0 disables dead time.

fields.name: idle-timeout
fields.description: Inactivity timeout for authenticated users in minutes. If no traffic is detected from a user for this duration, the session is terminated and re-authentication is required. This parameter is mutually exclusive with idle-timeout-seconds.

fields.name: idle-timeout-seconds
fields.description:
User idle timeout in seconds.
Valid range is 30-15300 seconds in multiples of 30 seconds.
This field can be configured only if idle-timeout is not configured.

fields.name: logon-lifetime
fields.description: Maximum session duration for captive portal or web-authenticated users in minutes. After this time expires, the user must re-authenticate via the captive portal even if the session is active. Value of 0 disables the maximum lifetime, allowing sessions to persist until idle timeout or explicit logout.

fields.name: stats-timeout
fields.description: Interval for sending RADIUS Interim-Update accounting messages in minutes. These updates provide periodic usage statistics (bytes transferred, session duration) to the RADIUS server for active user sessions. Mutually exclusive with stats-timeout-seconds.

fields.name: stats-timeout-seconds
fields.description: User Interim stats timeout value in seconds. This field can be configured only if stats-timeout is not configured.

fields.name: aaa-timers.dead-time
fields.description: Dead time interval in minutes for a down authentication server. Value of 0 disables dead time.

fields.name: aaa-timers.idle-timeout
fields.description: Inactivity timeout for authenticated users in minutes. If no traffic is detected from a user for this duration, the session is terminated and re-authentication is required. This parameter is mutually exclusive with idle-timeout-seconds.

fields.name: aaa-timers.idle-timeout-seconds
fields.description: User idle timeout in seconds. Valid range is 30-15300 seconds in multiples of 30 seconds. This field can be configured only if idle-timeout is not configured.

fields.name: aaa-timers.logon-lifetime
fields.description: Maximum session duration for captive portal or web-authenticated users in minutes. After this time expires, the user must re-authenticate via the captive portal even if the session is active. Value of 0 disables the maximum lifetime, allowing sessions to persist until idle timeout or explicit logout.

fields.name: aaa-timers.stats-timeout
fields.description: Interval for sending RADIUS Interim-Update accounting messages in minutes. These updates provide periodic usage statistics (bytes transferred, session duration) to the RADIUS server for active user sessions. Mutually exclusive with stats-timeout-seconds.

fields.name: aaa-timers.stats-timeout-seconds
fields.description: User Interim stats timeout value in seconds. This field can be configured only if stats-timeout is not configured.

fields.name: auth-trace-loglevel
fields.description: Enable authentication tracing with specified syslog level threshold. All authentication-related syslog messages at or above this severity will be traced.

fields.name: contact
fields.description: Device contact information, often an email.

fields.name: cpdns-disable
fields.description: Disables the gateway's automatic DNS redirection for captive portal detection. When enabled, the gateway will not intercept DNS queries from unauthenticated clients to force captive portal discovery. Mutually exclusive with cpdns-ip.

fields.name: cpdns-ip
fields.description: Specifies a custom IP address returned in DNS responses to unauthenticated clients, forcing redirection to the captive portal. This overrides the default behavior of returning the gateway's own IP address. Mutually exclusive with cpdns-disable. Corresponds to the `ip cp-redirect-address` CLI command.

fields.name: datapath-energy-efficiency
fields.description: Minimizes idle CPU spinning. It is applicable only on x86 based platforms. Not supported on Gateway models: 7005, 7008, 7010, 7024, 7030, 7205, 7210, 7220, 7240, 7240XM, 7280.

fields.name: description
fields.description: System profile description.

fields.name: dns-query-interval
fields.description: Interval for re-resolving DNS hostnames configured in RADIUS and authentication server profiles. This ensures the gateway maintains current IP addresses for servers specified by FQDN rather than static IP.

fields.name: dos-profile
fields.description: Reference to DOS profile from gw-system profile. This config option will not pushed to the device.

fields.name: fips
fields.description: Enable the Fips knob on the Aruba Gateway.

fields.name: firewall
fields.description: Defines device-wide firewall behaviors that apply to all traffic regardless of user role or VLAN. These settings control inter-user traffic isolation, jumbo frame support, and VoIP QoS trust models.

fields.name: deny-inter-user-bridging
fields.description:
Prevents the forwarding of Layer2 traffic between wired or wireless users.
You can configure user role policies that prevent Layer3 traffic between users or networks but this does not block Layer2 traffic.
This option can be used to prevent traffic, such as Appletalk or IPX from being forwarded.
If enabled, traffic (all nonIP traffic) to untrusted port or tunnel is also blocked.

fields.name: deny-inter-user-bridging-allowed-addresses
fields.description: Configure IPv4/IPv6 addresses to be exempted when deny-inter-user-bridging is enabled. Total IPv4 and IPv6 allowed addresses can't exceed 256

fields.name: deny-inter-user-traffic
fields.description:
Denies downstream traffic between users in a wireless network (untrusted users) by disallowing layer2 and layer3 traffic.
This parameter does not depend on the deny-inter-userbridging parameter being enabled or disabled.

fields.name: drop-ipv4-options
fields.description: When enabled, all IPv4 packets with options are dropped. You should not enable this option unless instructed to do so by an Aruba representative

fields.name: enable-stateful-icmp
fields.description: Enables stateful ICMP processing. This parameter create sessions for ICMP errors and denies unidirectional replies. Disabled by default.

fields.name: enforce-tcp-handshake
fields.description: Prevents data from passing between two clients until the three-way TCP handshake has been performed. This option should be disabled when you have mobile clients on the network as enabling this option will cause mobility to fail. You can enable this option if there are no mobile clients on the network.

fields.name: enforce-tcp-sequence
fields.description: Enforces the TCP sequence numbers for all packets. Disabled by default

fields.name: jumbo
fields.description: Enable Jumbo frames processing with default MTU value 9216

fields.name: jumbo-mtu
fields.description: Enable Jumbo frames processing with custom MTU value. Valid range is 1789-9216

fields.name: voip-qos-trusted
fields.description: Prioritizes the RTP traffic based on the DSCP value set by the end user device

fields.description: Enable the GPS function on the Aruba modem. Available only on 9004-LTE (Gateway with integrated cellular modem)

fields.name: ipv4-configuration
fields.description: System IPv4 configurations, allows you to set either the loopback interface or a specific VLAN interface address. If the system IPv4 is not configured, then the first configured VLAN interface address is selected by the device.

fields.name: device-interface-type
fields.description:
Specifies the interface type used for the system controller IPv4 address.
When set to VLAN, the device-vlan or device-vlan-alias parameter must also be specified to identify which VLAN interface to use. Corresponds to the `controller-ip` CLI command.

fields.name: device-vlan
fields.description: References an existing VLAN Interface profile by ID. The primary IPv4 address configured on this VLAN will be used as the controller-ip. Valid only when device-interface-type is set to VLAN.

fields.name: device-vlan-alias
fields.description:
Alias for device VLAN identifier, only applicable when device type is set to VLAN.
It cannot co-exist with device VLAN identifier field.

fields.name: ipv4-configuration.device-interface-type
fields.description: Specifies the interface type used for the system controller IPv4 address. When set to VLAN, the device-vlan or device-vlan-alias parameter must also be specified to identify which VLAN interface to use. Corresponds to the `controller-ip` CLI command.

fields.name: ipv4-configuration.device-vlan
fields.description: References an existing VLAN Interface profile by ID. The primary IPv4 address configured on this VLAN will be used as the controller-ip. Valid only when device-interface-type is set to VLAN.

fields.name: ipv4-configuration.device-vlan-alias
fields.description: Alias for device VLAN identifier, only applicable when device type is set to VLAN. It cannot co-exist with device VLAN identifier field.

fields.name: ipv6-certification-mode
fields.description: Enables IPv6 certification test mode for compliance validation. This mode adjusts protocol timers and behaviors to match IPv6 conformance test requirements (e.g., IPv6 Ready Logo testing). Should only be enabled in test environments.

fields.name: ipv6-configuration
fields.description: System IPv6 configurations, allows you to set either the loopback interface or a specific VLAN interface address. If the system IPv6 is not configured, then the first configured VLAN interface address is selected by the device.

fields.name: device-address
fields.description:
Specific IPv6 address to use as the controller-ipv6 identifier. This address must be pre-configured on the VLAN interface specified in device-vlan.
Valid only when device-interface-type is set to VLAN. This parameter is restricted to device-level scope and cannot be applied at site or global levels.
It cannot co-exist with ipv6-device-vlan-alias.

fields.name: device-interface-type
fields.description: Device interface type to indicate either loopback or VLAN interface.

fields.name: device-vlan
fields.description:
Device VLAN identifier, only applicable when device type is set to VLAN.
It cannot co-exist with ipv6-device-vlan-alias.

fields.name: ipv6-configuration.device-address
fields.description: Specific IPv6 address to use as the controller-ipv6 identifier. This address must be pre-configured on the VLAN interface specified in device-vlan. Valid only when device-interface-type is set to VLAN. This parameter is restricted to device-level scope and cannot be applied at site or global levels. It cannot co-exist with ipv6-device-vlan-alias.

fields.name: ipv6-configuration.device-interface-type
fields.description: Device interface type to indicate either loopback or VLAN interface.

fields.name: ipv6-configuration.device-vlan
fields.description: Device VLAN identifier, only applicable when device type is set to VLAN. It cannot co-exist with ipv6-device-vlan-alias.

fields.name: ipv6-device-vlan-alias
fields.description: Alias for IPv6 device VLAN and address configuration, only applicable when device interface type is VLAN. It cannot co-exist with direct device-vlan and device-address.

fields.name: ipv6-enable
fields.description: Master enable for IPv6 protocol support on the gateway. When disabled, the device will drop all IPv6 packets and will not participate in IPv6 routing or forwarding.

fields.name: ipv6-proxy-ra
fields.description: Configures the gateway to act as an IPv6 router advertisement proxy, forwarding RA messages between network segments. This allows IPv6 clients on downstream VLANs to receive router advertisements from upstream routers without direct Layer 2 connectivity.

fields.name: advertise-interval
fields.description: Interval for sending unsolicited IPv6 Router Advertisement messages in seconds. Per RFC 4861, this value must be between 180 and 1800 seconds.

fields.name: ipv6-proxy-ra.advertise-interval
fields.description: Interval for sending unsolicited IPv6 Router Advertisement messages in seconds. Per RFC 4861, this value must be between 180 and 1800 seconds.

fields.name: ipv6-transition-mode
fields.description: Enable IPv6 transition-mode. Supported modes: NAT64.

fields.name: lcd

Available only on Gateway models with LCD displays: 7010, 7030, 7024, 7205, 7210, 7220, 7240, 7240XM, 7280, 9240. Restricting menu options prevents unauthorized physical access to factory reset, system halt, and image upgrade functions.

fields.name: eject-slot0

fields.name: eject-slot1

fields.name: main-factory-default

Controls visibility of the factory-default option in the LCD maintenance menu. When enabled (true), the option is visible and accessible.
When disabled (false), factory reset cannot be initiated from the physical LCD panel, providing protection against accidental or unauthorized device resets.

fields.name: location
fields.description: Free-form text describing the physical location of the device. This value is exposed via SNMP sysLocation OID (1.3.6.1.2.1.1.6). Maximum length is platform-dependent.

fields.name: logging
fields.description: Controls local log message verbosity by module type, process, and severity level. This affects what diagnostic information is captured in the device's internal log buffers and forwarded to external syslog servers.

fields.name: module
fields.description: Defines per-module logging rules combining type, process, severity, and optional filtering by process, subcategory, or trace identifier. Each rule controls the minimum subcategory level for messages from specific system components.

fields.name: logging.module
fields.description: Defines per-module logging rules combining type, process, severity, and optional filtering by process, subcategory, or trace identifier. Each rule controls the minimum subcategory level for messages from specific system components.

fields.name: process
fields.description: Name of the debug process.

fields.name: severity
fields.description: Minimum severity for logging.

fields.name: subcategory
fields.description: Name of the debug subcategory type.

fields.name: trace
fields.description: For ap-debug type: the debug string name (1-63 chars). For arm-user-debug, peer-debug, or user-debug type: MAC address or identifier for targeted debugging. Filters log messages to only those associated with the specified client, peer device, or AP debug session.

fields.name: type
fields.description: Logging type.

fields.name: type-process-subcategory
fields.description:
key for module. This key is the combination of type, process and subcategory separated by ~
type        - Logging type.
process     - Logging process.
subcategory - Logging subcategory.

For a CX device, the range is 0..32 for firmware versions 10.12 and earlier. For PVOS device, valid values range from 2 to 15 lowercase characters, with a default of 2.

fields.name: password-complexity.min-char-difference
fields.description: Minimum number of character that the new password differes from old password. For a CX device, the default value is 8 characters. For a CX device, the range is 1..32 for firmware versions 10.12 and earlier, 1..64 otherwise. For PVOS device, valid values range from 8 to 64.

fields.name: password-complexity.minimum-length
fields.description: Minimum password length required. For a Gateway device, the default value is 6 characters and the range of values is 6-128 characters. For a CX device, the default minimum length of the password is 8 characters. For a CX device, the range is 1..32 for firmware versions 10.12 and earlier, 1..64 otherwise. For PVOS device, valid values range from 0 to 64.

fields.name: password-complexity.numeric-count
fields.description: Minimum number of numeric count in a password. For a Gateway device, the range of values is 0-10 numeric digits and the default value is 0. For a CX device, the default value is 1 character. For a CX device, the range is 0..32 for firmware versions 10.12 and earlier. For PVOS device, valid values range from 2 to 15 numeric digits, with a default of 2.

fields.name: password-complexity.password-lock-out
fields.description: Configuring the number of failed attempts within 3 minute window to lockout the user. Provides ability to reduce the number of passwords that can be guessed in a short time. Automatically clears the lockout after configured 'lock-out' minutes. A value of 0 indicates that lockout of users is disabled.

fields.name: password-complexity.password-lock-out-time

fields.name: password-complexity.password-update-interval

fields.name: password-complexity.repeat-char-check
fields.description: Password repeat character check ensures password does not contain three of the same characters used consecutively.

fields.name: password-complexity.repeat-password-check
fields.description: Password repeat check ensures same password is not allowed.

fields.name: password-complexity.repeat-username-check
fields.description: Password repeat username check ensures same username or reverse of username is not set as password.

fields.name: password-complexity.special-char-count
fields.description: Minimum number of special character count in a password. For a Gateway device, the special characters are !, @, #, $, %, ^, &, *, <, >, {, }, [, ], :, ., comma, |, +, ~, `. The range of values is 0-10 special characters. A value of 0 indicates that the minimum number of special character required is disabled by default. The following ( ')', '(' ;, -, space, =, /, ?) are dis-allowed. For a CX device, the default value is 1 character. For a CX device, the range is 0..32 for firmware versions 10.12 and earlier. For PVOS device, valid values range from 2 to 15 special characters, with a default of 2.

fields.name: password-complexity.uppercase-count
fields.description: Minimum number of uppercase count in a password. For a Gateway device, the range of values is 0-10 minimum upper case characters. A value of 0 indicates that minimum number of upper case required is disabled by default. For a CX device, the default value is 1 character. For a CX device, the range is 0..32 for firmware versions 10.12 and earlier. For PVOS device, valid values range from 2 to 15 uppercase characters, with a default of 2.

fields.name: host
fields.description: Specifies the syslog server destination as a fully qualified domain name (FQDN), hostname, or IP address (IPv4/IPv6). Platform-Specific Behavior: AP Devices support IPv4 or IPv6 addresses with a maximum of 3 remote syslog servers per AP device. Gateway Devices require the host value to include both the IP address and logging category separated by '~' (e.g., 192.0.2.1~SECURITY). Supported categories: AP_DEBUG, NETWORK, SECURITY, SYSTEM, USER, USER_DEBUG, WIRELESS (case-sensitive). CX/PVOS Devices support standard FQDN, hostname, or IP formats without additional syntax requirements.

aruba_central_config_create_rmon_alarm.summary: Create a new rmon-alarm by unique name

fields.name: description
fields.description: The RMON alarm table periodically takes statistical samples from the SNMP MIB objects in the probe and compares them to previously configured thresholds. A hysteresis mechanism is implemented to limit the generation of alarm. This mechanism generates one event as a threshold is crossed in the appropriate direction for the SNMP MIB object. No more events are generated for that threshold until the opposite threshold is reached.

fields.name: enable-all
fields.description: Enables all RMON alarm.

fields.name: name
fields.description: RMON alarm profile name.

fields.name: rmon
fields.description: RMON alarm parameters for given index.

fields.name: enable
fields.description: Enables RMON alarm.

fields.name: falling-threshold
fields.description:
Falling threshold to be compared against the current value
to trigger the SNMP alarm.

fields.name: index
fields.description: An index that uniquely identifies the RMON alarm.

fields.name: interval
fields.description:
The interval in seconds, over which the snmp-oid is sampled
and compared with the rising and falling thresholds.

fields.name: owner
fields.description: Owner name for this alarm.

fields.name: rising-threshold
fields.description:
Rising threshold to be compared against the current value
to trigger the SNMP alarm.

fields.name: sample-type
fields.description: The method of sampling of the variable.

fields.name: snmp-oid
fields.description:
The object identifier to be monitored.
Only variables that resolve to an ASN.1 primitive type of INTEGER
(INTEGER, Integer32,Counter32, Counter64, Gauge32, or TimeTicks)
will be monitored.

fields.description: MPSK profile.

fields.name: password-auto-expire
fields.description:
password-auto-expire is an automatic expiration interval (ISO 8601 duration)
that is applied whenever an owned MPSK is created or the password is reset.

An active Central NAC subscription is required to set this field.

This field applies to end-user provisioned MPSK only. It does not apply to
administrator Named MPSK or operations.

fields.name: password-minimum-age
fields.description:
password-minimum-age is a password minimum age (ISO 8601 duration) that limits
how often an end user can reset a password.

password-minimum-age duration must be at least one day less than the
password-auto-expire duration, in the case that both are set.

An active Central NAC subscription is required to set this field.

This field applies to end-user provisioned MPSK only. It does not apply to
administrator Named MPSK or operations.

fields.name: password-minimum-history
fields.description:
password-minimum-history is a password history length that enforces password
uniqueness for the specified number of password resets.

An active Central NAC subscription is required to set this field.

This field applies to end-user provisioned MPSK only. It does not apply to
administrator Named MPSK or operations.

fields.name: captive-portal
fields.description: Captive Portal authentication profile

fields.name: anonymous-password
fields.description:
Password for the anonymous user sign in, if required.

The anonymous-password field can only be configured when authentication-mode is ANONYMOUS.

fields.name: sponsor-domains
fields.description:
Allowed domain names for sponsor email addresses.

The maximum number of sponsor-domains allowed is 50.

When a user is registering an account that requires sponsor approval (see require-sponsor-approval), they must provide the email address of a valid sponsor.

Anyone who has an email address in one of these domains is a valid sponsor.

The sponsor-domains list can only be configured when require-sponsor-approval is true.

At least one sponsor domain (see sponsor-domains), or sponsor email (see sponsor-emails), must be configured when require-sponsor-approval is true.

See also the sponsor-emails field for configuring specific email addresses as valid sponsors.

Both the sponsor-domains and sponsor-emails lists define valid sponsors.

fields.name: sponsor-emails
fields.description:
Allowed sponsor email addresses.

The maximum number of sponsor-emails allowed is 100.

When a user is registering an account that requires sponsor approval (see require-sponsor-approval), they must provide the email address of a valid sponsor.

Any one of these email addresses is a valid sponsor.

The sponsor-emails list can only be configured when require-sponsor-approval is true.

At least one sponsor domain (see sponsor-domains), or sponsor email (see sponsor-emails), must be configured when require-sponsor-approval is true.

See also the sponsor-domains field for configuring an entire domain as valid sponsors.

Both the sponsor-domains and sponsor-emails lists define valid sponsors.

fields.name: register-accept-email
fields.description:
Allow users to register using an email address.

The register-accept-email field can only be configured when enable-registration is true.

At least one of register-accept-email and register-accept-phone must be true when enable-registration is true.

fields.name: register-accept-phone
fields.description:
Allow users to register using a phone number.

The register-accept-phone field can only be configured when enable-registration is true.

At least one of register-accept-email and register-accept-phone must be true when enable-registration is true.

fields.name: register-auto-expire
fields.description:
Automatically set a registered account to expire after the specified duration (ISO 8601 duration).

The register-auto-expire field can only be configured when enable-registration is true.

fields.name: registration-identity-store
fields.description:
Reference to the identity store to be used for user registrations.

The registration-identity-store must be configured when enable-registration is true.

The registration-identity-store must be a member of the authentication profile's list of identity-stores when enable-registration is true.

The registration-identity-store must be a LOCAL identity store when enable-registration is true.

fields.name: require-sponsor-approval
fields.description:
Require sponsor approval for self-registrations.

If enabled, when a user is registering an account, they must provide the email address of a valid sponsor.
The sponsor will receive an email with a link to then review and approve the registration request.

The require-sponsor-approval field can only be configured when enable-registration is true.

At least one sponsor domain (see sponsor-domains), or sponsor email (see sponsor-emails), must be configured when require-sponsor-approval is true.

fields.name: verify-registration
fields.description:
Verify that the user actually owns the registered identity (e.g. email address or phone number) by sending an access code that must then be entered to complete registration.

The verify-registration field can only be configured when enable-registration is true.

fields.name: enable-registration
fields.description:
Allow users to register for an account.

The enable-registration field can only be configured when authentication-mode is AUTHENTICATED.

At least one of register-accept-email and register-accept-phone must be true when enable-registration is true.

The registration-identity-store must be configured when enable-registration is true.

fields.name: allow-internet-on-service-unavailable
fields.description: Allow internet access when the authentication service (RADIUS/RadSec) is unavailable

fields.name: cna-policy
fields.description: CNA (Captive Network Assistant) accept/bypass policy

fields.name: final-redirection-url
fields.description: A URL to redirect the client to after they have completed the login workflow

fields.name: network-login-host-override
fields.description:
Override the expected host that the Central NAC captive portal should redirect back
to after it has authenticated the user.

The network access device (e.g. an Access Point), at this domain name, will then
complete the final phase of user authentication.

It is recommended to only set this override when using a custom server certificate
on the network access device. This is so that, when the user's web browser is
redirected back to the network access device, the host matches one of the valid
domain names in the certificate (e.g. a subject-alt-name, or the common name).

If set, this value must be a valid domain name.

fields.name: pre-auth-access-rules
fields.description:
Additional access rules added to the captive portal pre-authentication role.
Use these rules to provide the user with access to HTTP/HTTPS resources before
they have completed the authentication process.

The maximum number of pre-auth-access-rules allowed is 10.

fields.name: authentication-mode

When the authentication mode is AUTHENTICATED, the authentication profile's
identity-stores must reference at least one identity store.

When the authentication mode is ANONYMOUS, the authentication profile's
identity-stores must not reference any identity stores.

fields.name: password-auto-expire
fields.description:
password-auto-expire is an automatic expiration interval (ISO 8601 duration)
that is applied whenever an owned MPSK is created or the password is reset.

An active Central NAC subscription is required to set this field.

This field applies to end-user provisioned MPSK only. It does not apply to
administrator Named MPSK or operations.

fields.name: password-minimum-age
fields.description:
password-minimum-age is a password minimum age (ISO 8601 duration) that limits
how often an end user can reset a password.

password-minimum-age duration must be at least one day less than the
password-auto-expire duration, in the case that both are set.

An active Central NAC subscription is required to set this field.

This field applies to end-user provisioned MPSK only. It does not apply to
administrator Named MPSK or operations.

fields.name: password-minimum-history
fields.description:
password-minimum-history is a password history length that enforces password
uniqueness for the specified number of password resets.

An active Central NAC subscription is required to set this field.

This field applies to end-user provisioned MPSK only. It does not apply to
administrator Named MPSK or operations.

fields.description: Captive Portal authentication profile

fields.name: anonymous-password
fields.description:
Password for the anonymous user sign in, if required.

The anonymous-password field can only be configured when authentication-mode is ANONYMOUS.

fields.name: sponsor-domains
fields.description:
Allowed domain names for sponsor email addresses.

The maximum number of sponsor-domains allowed is 50.

When a user is registering an account that requires sponsor approval (see require-sponsor-approval), they must provide the email address of a valid sponsor.

Anyone who has an email address in one of these domains is a valid sponsor.

The sponsor-domains list can only be configured when require-sponsor-approval is true.

At least one sponsor domain (see sponsor-domains), or sponsor email (see sponsor-emails), must be configured when require-sponsor-approval is true.

See also the sponsor-emails field for configuring specific email addresses as valid sponsors.

Both the sponsor-domains and sponsor-emails lists define valid sponsors.

fields.name: sponsor-emails
fields.description:
Allowed sponsor email addresses.

The maximum number of sponsor-emails allowed is 100.

When a user is registering an account that requires sponsor approval (see require-sponsor-approval), they must provide the email address of a valid sponsor.

Any one of these email addresses is a valid sponsor.

The sponsor-emails list can only be configured when require-sponsor-approval is true.

At least one sponsor domain (see sponsor-domains), or sponsor email (see sponsor-emails), must be configured when require-sponsor-approval is true.

See also the sponsor-domains field for configuring an entire domain as valid sponsors.

Both the sponsor-domains and sponsor-emails lists define valid sponsors.

fields.name: register-accept-email
fields.description:
Allow users to register using an email address.

The register-accept-email field can only be configured when enable-registration is true.

At least one of register-accept-email and register-accept-phone must be true when enable-registration is true.

fields.name: register-accept-phone
fields.description:
Allow users to register using a phone number.

The register-accept-phone field can only be configured when enable-registration is true.

At least one of register-accept-email and register-accept-phone must be true when enable-registration is true.

fields.name: register-auto-expire
fields.description:
Automatically set a registered account to expire after the specified duration (ISO 8601 duration).

The register-auto-expire field can only be configured when enable-registration is true.

fields.name: registration-identity-store
fields.description:
Reference to the identity store to be used for user registrations.

The registration-identity-store must be configured when enable-registration is true.

The registration-identity-store must be a member of the authentication profile's list of identity-stores when enable-registration is true.

The registration-identity-store must be a LOCAL identity store when enable-registration is true.

fields.name: require-sponsor-approval
fields.description:
Require sponsor approval for self-registrations.

If enabled, when a user is registering an account, they must provide the email address of a valid sponsor.
The sponsor will receive an email with a link to then review and approve the registration request.

The require-sponsor-approval field can only be configured when enable-registration is true.

At least one sponsor domain (see sponsor-domains), or sponsor email (see sponsor-emails), must be configured when require-sponsor-approval is true.

fields.name: verify-registration
fields.description:
Verify that the user actually owns the registered identity (e.g. email address or phone number) by sending an access code that must then be entered to complete registration.

The verify-registration field can only be configured when enable-registration is true.

fields.name: enable-registration
fields.description:
Allow users to register for an account.

The enable-registration field can only be configured when authentication-mode is AUTHENTICATED.

At least one of register-accept-email and register-accept-phone must be true when enable-registration is true.

The registration-identity-store must be configured when enable-registration is true.

fields.name: allow-internet-on-service-unavailable
fields.description: Allow internet access when the authentication service (RADIUS/RadSec) is unavailable

fields.name: cna-policy
fields.description: CNA (Captive Network Assistant) accept/bypass policy

fields.name: final-redirection-url
fields.description: A URL to redirect the client to after they have completed the login workflow

fields.name: network-login-host-override
fields.description:
Override the expected host that the Central NAC captive portal should redirect back
to after it has authenticated the user.

The network access device (e.g. an Access Point), at this domain name, will then
complete the final phase of user authentication.

It is recommended to only set this override when using a custom server certificate
on the network access device. This is so that, when the user's web browser is
redirected back to the network access device, the host matches one of the valid
domain names in the certificate (e.g. a subject-alt-name, or the common name).

If set, this value must be a valid domain name.

fields.name: pre-auth-access-rules
fields.description:
Additional access rules added to the captive portal pre-authentication role.
Use these rules to provide the user with access to HTTP/HTTPS resources before
they have completed the authentication process.

The maximum number of pre-auth-access-rules allowed is 10.

fields.name: authentication-mode
fields.description:
How users are to be authenticated.

When the authentication mode is AUTHENTICATED, the authentication profile's
identity-stores must reference at least one identity store.

When the authentication mode is ANONYMOUS, the authentication profile's
identity-stores must not reference any identity stores.

fields.name: periodic-data-quota
fields.description:
Maximum IO per day allowed for the account, or device, before active sessions should be terminated.

Limiting by account, or by device, is controlled by the periodic-quota-subject.

Null for no limit or a minimum of 1 (one).

Units are in MB (1,048,576 bytes).

fields.name: periodic-quota-subject
fields.description: Controls whether daily time and IO quotas are to be enforced on a per-account or per-device basis.

fields.name: periodic-time-quota
fields.description:

Limiting by account, or by device, is controlled by the periodic-quota-subject.

Null for no limit or a minimum of 1 (one).

Units are in seconds.

fields.name: session-data-quota
fields.description:

Null for no limit or a minimum of 1 (one).

Units are in MB (1,048,576 bytes).

fields.name: session-timeout
fields.description:
Maximum time allowed for the session before it should be terminated.

Null for the default session timeout or a minimum of 1 (one).

The default session timeout is 28,800 seconds (i.e. 8 hours).

Units are in seconds.

fields.name: simultaneous-use
fields.description:
Maximum number of simultaneous network sessions allowed for each account.

Null for no limit or a minimum of 1 (one).

Note that this limit is per-account only.

aruba_central_config_create_dhcp_relay.summary: Create profile for DHCPv4/DHCPv6 Relay configurations

fields.name: ipv4
fields.description: DHCPv4 Relay Configurations

fields.name: option-82
fields.description: Option 82 Configurations

fields.name: enable
fields.description:
Enables the use of the configured source-interface for DHCPv4 relay agent.
When set to true, the configured source-interface is used as source IP address while
sending DHCPv4 relay messages to server.

fields.name: policy
fields.description: Policy to be applied on the client DHCP packets with option 82.

fields.name: remote-id
fields.description:
Option 82 remote ID sub-option to be sent in the DHCP packet to server.
It is used to identify the relay agent device.

fields.name: source-interface
fields.description:
Enables the use of the configured source-interface for DHCPv4 relay agent communication.
When set to true, the configured source-interface will be used for sending DHCPv4 relay messages.

fields.name: validate
fields.description: Validates option 82 information in the DHCP server response packets.

fields.name: enable
fields.description:
Enables DHCPv4 relay globally. The functionality is effective
  	 only after the port level helper configuration.

fields.name: hop-count-increment
fields.description: Enables hop count increment in the relayed DHCPv4 requests.

fields.name: l2vpn-clients
fields.description: Enables DHCPv4 relay for remote L2 VPN clients.

fields.name: option-xml
fields.description:
IPv4 DHCP relay option XML file. The XML file is used as the input from the user and is validated
against an XSD file in the controller. The format in the XML file is parsed and stored in the DHCP
relay which is used to insert Option-82 related values in the DHCP request packets sent from the
client to the server.

fields.name: reply-overwrite-source-ip
fields.description: Enables DHCPv4 relay overwrite source IP.

fields.name: smart-relay
fields.description:
Enables DHCPv4 smart relay globally. When multiple IPv4 addresses are configured on an
interface, the primary IP address is used first as the gateway IP (GIADDR) for DHCP relay.
If the DHCP server does not have available IP addresses in the pool corresponding to the primary
IP's subnet, the secondary IP address is used as a fallback. This ensures that the DHCP relay
remains functional by switching to a secondary IP address when the primary IP's subnet pool
is exhausted.

fields.name: authoritative-mode
fields.description:
If authoritative mode is set, server will become sole authority for
the configured network. DHCPv4 server will respond with DHCPNAK messages
for the DHCP requests received for unknown leases from unknown hosts.
DHCPv6 server will respond to the clients with Advertise messages with
priority or preference set to 255.

fields.name: q-profile
fields.description: Queue profile to apply in combination with the specified schedule profile. Queue profiles must first be configured using the aruba-qos-queue yang model, and must be valid for the platform to which the profile is being applied.  Queue profiles cannot be modified while they are applied. The number of queues and queue ID values must also match those in the paired schedule profile. If an applied queue profile is modified, the configuration will be rejected. To apply the modified queue profile, follow the following sequence of operations:  1. If sched-profile in aruba-qos-global is set to DEFAULT, set q-profile to DEFAULT. Otherwise, remove both q-profile and sched-profile. This will cause the factory-default profiles to be applied. 2. For PVOS devices, ensure that the traffic-template leaf is not set to the same profile as the queue-profile being modified. If it is, delete the traffic-template by setting the traffic-template leaf to null. 3. Modify the queue profile. 4. If both q-profile and sched-profile were removed in step 1, apply them again together in the same transaction. If q-profile was set to DEFAULT in step 1, apply only the queue profile. 5. For PVOS devices, if the traffic template was removed as part of this process, apply it again after the queue profile has been modified.

fields.name: sched-profile
fields.description: Schedule profile to apply in combination with the specified queue profile. Schedule profiles must first be configured using the aruba-qos-schedule yang model, and must be valid for the platform to which the profile is being applied. The number of queues and queue ID values must also match those in the paired queue profile.

aruba_central_config_create_gw_cluster.summary: Create a gateway cluster profile configuration

fields.name: auto-cluster
fields.description: With this knob enabled, gateways will be added to the auto-cluster/removed from the auto-cluster automatically by the System. This knob should be set to false while creating the manual cluster profiles.

fields.name: coa-vrrp
fields.description: CoA-VRRP configuration

fields.name: id
fields.description: This is an optional parameter which specifies the starting VRRP ID for cluster members. If this is not configured, system automatically configures VRRP groups starting with default VRRP ID of 220. This is only applicable while configuring VRRP for COA [Change of Authorization]. CoA-VRRP VLAN needs to be configured for coa-vrrp id configuration.

fields.name: passphrase
fields.description: VRRP Passphrase. CoA-VRRP VLAN needs to be configured for passphrase configuration.

fields.name: vlan
fields.description: VRRP VLAN corresponding to the VIP. Used for COA operations.

fields.name: coa-vrrp.id
fields.description: This is an optional parameter which specifies the starting VRRP ID for cluster members. CoA-VRRP VLAN needs to be configured for coa-vrrp id configuration.

fields.name: coa-vrrp.passphrase
fields.description: VRRP Passphrase. CoA-VRRP VLAN needs to be configured for passphrase configuration.

fields.name: coa-vrrp.vlan
fields.description: VRRP VLAN corresponding to the VIP. Used for COA operations.

fields.name: description
fields.description: User comment.

fields.name: heartbeat-threshold
fields.description: Gateway will wait for heartbeat threshold time (ms) before declaring a peer cluster node as dead.

fields.name: ipv4-gateways
fields.description: Upto 12 gateways can be configured in a profile. Based on the combination of Gateway platforms, system will restrict Gateway addition to the profile. Ex: Presence of 70xx model gateway in the profile will reduce the Gateway count to 4.

fields.name: ipv6-enable
fields.description: Enable or disable the ipv6 mode in cluster profiles. ipv6-enable knob can not be toggled once the cluster profile is created.

fields.name: ipv6-gateways
fields.description: Upto 12 gateways can be configured in a profile. Based on the combination of Gateway platforms, system will restrict Gateway addition to the profile. Ex: Presence of 70xx model gateway in the profile will reduce the Gateway count to 4.

fields.name: multicast-vlan
fields.description: VLAN to be used for forwarding multicast traffic to upstream router.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Gateway Cluster Profile name. Manual cluster profile name should not start with auto_ prefix and it should not contain space.

fields.name: one-to-one-redundancy
fields.description: Enable/disable one-to-one-redundancy mode for the cluster profile. With this knob enabled, only 2 gateways are allowed in the cluster profile. Leader is active and non-leader is standby.

fields.name: uplink-tracking
fields.description: Enable/disable uplink tracking for the cluster profile. With this knob enabled, Cluster leader will be selected based on number of active uplinks. Applicable only when one-to-one-redundancy knob is enabled.
