fields.name: sync-features
fields.description: VSX configuration that syncs to both primary and secondary.

fields.name: linkup-delay-timer
fields.description:
Number of seconds that multi-chassis LAGs should be held down after the ISL is
considered to be fully established and VSX switches are synchronized. Comes into
effect on new ISL deployments, ISL flaps or full device reboot.

fields.name: split-recovery-disable
fields.description:
Disables split brain recovery.
By default, split-recovery mode is enabled. When ISL goes out-of-sync and if
Keep-alive is established then secondary vsx lags will be brought down.
Subsequently if Keep-alive also fails it causes split condition. In this case
if split-recovery mode is enabled secondary will make its vsx lags up else
secondary will continue to keep its vsx lags down.

fields.name: system-mac
fields.description:
System MAC address to be used by L2 control plane protocols.
A pair of VSX switches must have the same system MAC.
If system MAC is not configured, L2 control plane protocols
will use the VSX Primary device MAC address as their
Bridge Identifier. MAC address will be in
[0-9a-fA-F]{2}(:[0-9a-fA-F]{2}){5} format.

fields.name: l3-vlans
fields.description: List of VLANs to be created on both primary and secondary.

fields.name: inter-switch-link-timers
fields.description: Inter-Switch-Link timer configuration common to primary and secondary.

fields.name: dead-interval
fields.description:
Inter-switch link dead interval. The dead interval is the amount of time to wait for
hellos from peer before declaring the peer to be missing. Lesser dead-intervals might cause
ISL flap due to dead-interval expiry during scenarios like redundancy switchover.

fields.name: hello-interval
fields.description: Inter-switch link hello interval.

fields.name: hold-time
fields.description:
Inter-switch link hold time interval.
Port is treated as down only when it stays down for the configured hold-time interval.

fields.name: peer-detect-interval
fields.description:
Inter-switch link peer detect interval. This is the amount of time in seconds that the
device will wait for inter-switch-link interface to link up after a reboot. If the ISL link
does not come up within this time window, the device will declare itself as split from its peer.

fields.name: keepalive
fields.description: Keepalive timer configuration common to primary and secondary configuration

fields.name: dead-interval
fields.description:
Keepalive dead time interval. Default is 3 seconds for CX, 5 seconds for PVOS.
3-20 is the supported range for PVOS.

fields.name: hello-interval
fields.description:
Keepalive hello time interval in seconds fox CX and in milliseconds for PVOS.
Default is 1 second for CX, 1000 milliseconds for PVOS.
400-10000 in milliseconds is the supported range for PVOS.

fields.name: udp-port
fields.description:
UDP port number of peer device. Default is 7678 for CX and the default for PVOS is 1024.
1024-49151 is the supported range for PVOS.

fields.description:
Determines whether this port has VSX active-forwarding enabled or not.
This should be set on Upstream SVIs only and not on downstream SVIs
that have active-gateway enabled. Active forwarding cannot be enabled on
an interface in which active gateway is configured.

fields.name: id

fields.name: shutdown-on-split
fields.description:
Configures non-vsx interface to go down along with VSX interfaces during split.
This also configures the interface-vlan, whose vlan tag is not configured
on any of the MCLAGs, to go down on VSX split. In case of interface-vlans,
this command is recommended to be configured on those interface-vlans which
would establish L3 adjacency with other devices that are not
part of VSX MCLAGs but part of ISL and that would require immediate reconvergence
on VSX split.For example, VxLAN tunnels formed through VSX switches whose overlay routes
are advertised through these interface-vlans can be configured with this command.

fields.name: sync-features
fields.description: VSX configuration that syncs to both primary and secondary.

fields.name: linkup-delay-timer
fields.description:
Number of seconds that multi-chassis LAGs should be held down after the ISL is
considered to be fully established and VSX switches are synchronized. Comes into
effect on new ISL deployments, ISL flaps or full device reboot.

fields.name: split-recovery-disable
fields.description:
Disables split brain recovery.
By default, split-recovery mode is enabled. When ISL goes out-of-sync and if
Keep-alive is established then secondary vsx lags will be brought down.
Subsequently if Keep-alive also fails it causes split condition. In this case
if split-recovery mode is enabled secondary will make its vsx lags up else
secondary will continue to keep its vsx lags down.

fields.name: system-mac
fields.description:
System MAC address to be used by L2 control plane protocols.
A pair of VSX switches must have the same system MAC.
If system MAC is not configured, L2 control plane protocols
will use the VSX Primary device MAC address as their
Bridge Identifier. MAC address will be in
[0-9a-fA-F]{2}(:[0-9a-fA-F]{2}){5} format.

fields.name: l3-vlans
fields.description: List of VLANs to be created on both primary and secondary.

fields.name: inter-switch-link-timers
fields.description: Inter-Switch-Link timer configuration common to primary and secondary.

fields.name: dead-interval
fields.description:
Inter-switch link dead interval. The dead interval is the amount of time to wait for
hellos from peer before declaring the peer to be missing. Lesser dead-intervals might cause
ISL flap due to dead-interval expiry during scenarios like redundancy switchover.

fields.name: hello-interval
fields.description: Inter-switch link hello interval.

fields.name: hold-time
fields.description:
Inter-switch link hold time interval.
Port is treated as down only when it stays down for the configured hold-time interval.

fields.name: peer-detect-interval
fields.description:
Inter-switch link peer detect interval. This is the amount of time in seconds that the
device will wait for inter-switch-link interface to link up after a reboot. If the ISL link
does not come up within this time window, the device will declare itself as split from its peer.

are advertised through these interface-vlans can be configured with this command.

fields.name: security-policy
fields.description: Security policy configuration for this policy. Contains the policy type, ordered list of rules, and optional features such as CALEA lawful intercept and URL redirection.

fields.name: policy-rule
fields.description:
Ordered list of policy rules. Each rule defines a match
condition and action pair. Rules are evaluated in ascending
order by position (low to high). The key 'position' uniquely
identifies each rule within the policy.

fields.name: calea
fields.description:
Enable Communications Assistance for Law Enforcement Act
(CALEA) lawful intercept on traffic matching this policy.
When true, matching traffic is mirrored for lawful
intercept purposes.

fields.name: description
fields.description:
A user-defined description or comment for the security
policy. Maximum 256 characters.

fields.name: redirect-blocked-http-url
fields.description:
When true, HTTP requests that are denied by this policy
are redirected to the configured redirect URL instead of
being silently dropped.

fields.name: redirect-url
fields.description:
URL to redirect denied HTTP traffic to when
redirect-blocked-http-url is enabled. Maximum 256
characters.

fields.name: type
fields.description:
Security policy type that determines which protocol fields
are allowed in the policy rules (e.g., IPv4, IPv6,
Ethernet). Affects the valid rule-types for child rules.

fields.name: security-policy.policy-rule
fields.description: Ordered list of policy rules. Each rule defines a match condition and action pair. Rules are evaluated in ascending order by position (low to high). The key 'position' uniquely identifies each rule within the policy.

fields.name: description
fields.description:
A user-defined description or comment for this policy rule.
Maximum length is 256 characters.

fields.name: devices-applicable
fields.description:
Read-only field indicating whether the rule is supported by
all or a subset of target devices. Values are 'full' (all
devices support this rule) or 'partial' (only some devices
support it).

fields.name: position
fields.description:
Sequence position that determines the order in which rules
are evaluated. This is a required key field. Lower values
are evaluated first. The position must be unique for each
rule within the policy.

fields.name: security-policy.calea
fields.description: Enable Communications Assistance for Law Enforcement Act (CALEA) lawful intercept on traffic matching this policy. When true, matching traffic is mirrored for lawful intercept purposes.

fields.name: security-policy.description

fields.name: app-aaa-contract

and traffic direction. Each entry maps a specific DPI application
(e.g. facebook, youtube, zoom) to a named AAA bandwidth contract for
either upstream or downstream traffic.

fields.name: app-aaa-contract.app
fields.description: List of application-based bandwidth contracts keyed by application name and traffic direction. Each entry maps a specific DPI application (e.g. facebook, youtube, zoom) to a named AAA bandwidth contract for either upstream or downstream traffic.

fields.name: appname-direction
fields.description: Key combination of application name and direction separated by '~'.

fields.name: bwc-name
fields.description: Name of the Bandwidth contract.

fields.name: app-category-aaa-contract
fields.description: Application category-based AAA bandwidth contracts. Associates named AAA bandwidth contracts with DPI application categories and a traffic direction, allowing rate limiting to be applied at the category level rather than per individual application.

fields.name: app-category
fields.description:
List of application category-based bandwidth contracts keyed by
category name and traffic direction. Each entry maps a DPI application
category (e.g. STREAMING, GAMING, SOCIAL-NETWORKING) to a named AAA
bandwidth contract for either upstream or downstream traffic.

fields.name: app-category-aaa-contract.app-category
fields.description: List of application category-based bandwidth contracts keyed by category name and traffic direction. Each entry maps a DPI application category (e.g. STREAMING, GAMING, SOCIAL-NETWORKING) to a named AAA bandwidth contract for either upstream or downstream traffic.

fields.name: bwc-name
fields.description: Name of the Bandwidth contract.

fields.name: category-name-direction
fields.description: Key combination of application category name and direction separated by '~'.

fields.name: web-category-aaa-contract
fields.description: WebCC category-based AAA bandwidth contracts. Associates named AAA bandwidth contracts with WebCC content categories and a traffic direction, enabling rate limiting based on the type of web content being accessed (e.g. BUSINESS-ECONOMY, GAMES, EDUCATIONAL-INSTITUTIONS).

fields.name: web-category
fields.description:
List of WebCC category-based bandwidth contracts keyed by WebCC category
name and traffic direction. Each entry maps a WebCC content category to
a named AAA bandwidth contract for either upstream or downstream traffic.
There can be at most one contract per category per direction.

fields.name: web-category-aaa-contract.web-category
fields.description: List of WebCC category-based bandwidth contracts keyed by WebCC category name and traffic direction. Each entry maps a WebCC content category to a named AAA bandwidth contract for either upstream or downstream traffic. There can be at most one contract per category per direction.

fields.name: bwc-name
fields.description: Name of the Bandwidth contract.

fields.name: webcategory-name-direction
fields.description: Key combination of WebCC category name and direction separated by '~'.

fields.name: web-reputation-aaa-contract
fields.description: WebCC reputation-based AAA bandwidth contracts. Associates named AAA bandwidth contracts with WebCC reputation risk levels and a traffic direction, enabling differentiated rate limiting based on the trustworthiness of web destinations. Risk levels are: TRUSTWORTHY (81-100), LOW_RISK (61-80), MODERATE_RISK (41-60), SUSPICIOUS (21-40), and HIGH_RISK (1-20).

fields.name: web-reputation
fields.description:
List of WebCC reputation-based bandwidth contracts keyed by reputation
risk level and traffic direction. Each entry maps a WebCC reputation
level (TRUSTWORTHY, LOW_RISK, MODERATE_RISK, SUSPICIOUS, or HIGH_RISK)
to a named AAA bandwidth contract for either upstream or downstream
traffic. There can be at most one contract per risk level per direction.

fields.name: web-reputation-aaa-contract.web-reputation
fields.description: List of WebCC reputation-based bandwidth contracts keyed by reputation risk level and traffic direction. Each entry maps a WebCC reputation level (TRUSTWORTHY, LOW_RISK, MODERATE_RISK, SUSPICIOUS, or HIGH_RISK) to a named AAA bandwidth contract for either upstream or downstream traffic. There can be at most one contract per risk level per direction.

fields.name: bwc-name
fields.description: Name of the Bandwidth contract.

fields.name: webrepname-direction
fields.description: Key combination of WebCC reputation name and direction separated by '~'.
